ge (3 Qs)

31.explanation_en:
The earliest written account of the Dasarajna con-
flict (Battle of the Ten Kings) is found in the
Rigveda, specifically in Mandala 7. The conflict de-
scribes the victory of King Sudas of the Bharata Trtsu
dynasty over a coalition of ten prominent tribes.
Important Facts:
➤ The Battle of the Ten Kings was fought on the banks
of the river Parushni, identified with the modern Ravi
River.
➤ King Sudas was guided and supported by his chief
priest, sage Vashistha.
➤ The opposing coalition was led by sage
Vishwamitra and included both Aryan tribes (such as
Puru, Yadu, Turvasha, Anu, Druhyu) and non-Aryan con-
federates.
➤ The Rigveda is the oldest of the four Vedas, con-
taining 1,028 hymns structured into 10 Mandalas.
➤ The famous Gayatri Mantra dedicated to Savitr is
also located in the Rigveda, in Mandala 3.

32.question_text_en:
Q.3 What type of stone was specifically chosen by
sculptors of the Gandhara School for their high relief
61 Download App Visit Website

carvings?
32.explanation_en:
Sculptors belonging to the Gandhara School of Art
primarily utilized blue-grey schist stone (and later
stucco) to create their high relief sculptures. The use of
this fine-grained schist permitted the intricate carving of
naturalistic drapery, facial features, and Greek-inspired
realistic details.
Important Facts:
➤ The Gandhara School of Art flourished primarily dur-
ing the reign of the Kushana Empire, particularly un-
der Emperor Kanishka I.
➤ It is termed the Greco-Buddhist school due to its
distinctive amalgamation of Greek-Hellenistic realistic
styles with Buddhist spiritual motifs.
➤ In contrast, the contemporary indigenous Mathura
School of Art primarily employed spotted red
sandstone.
➤ The Amaravati School of Art in southern India
predominantly used white marble (or carved lime-
stone slabs).
➤ Major geographic centres of Gandhara art included
Taxila, Peshawar, Begram, and Bamiyan.

33.question_text_en:
Q.2 The widespread popularity of Francois Bernier's
writings in Europe, despite their acknowledged
inaccuracies, most strongly reflects which underlying
factor?
72 Download App Visit Website

options.text_en: His writings were sole source on India.

33.explanation_en:
Francois Bernier constructed his travelogues around a
binary framework contrasting Mughal India unfavourably
with contemporary Europe. European audiences enthu-
siastically accepted his works because they rein-
forced familiar Eurocentric comparisons por-
traying European systems of private property and
monarchical order as inherently superior to Eastern
despotism.
Important Facts:
➤ Francois Bernier was a French physician and
traveler who resided in India for twelve years (1656–
1668) during the Mughal period.
➤ He was closely associated with the Mughal court as a
personal physician to Prince Dara Shikoh and later to
Danishmand Khan.
➤ His major work, "Travels in the Mogul Empire",
was dedicated to the French King Louis XIV.
➤ Bernier argued that the absence of private prop-
erty in land in Mughal India led to economic ruin, a
thesis later utilized by Karl Marx (Asiatic mode of pro-
duction) and Montesquieu (Oriental despotism).
➤ Other notable European travelers to Mughal India
during the 17th century included Jean-Baptiste
Tavernier and Niccolao Manucci.

34.question_text_en: Q.3 The demand curve shows the relationship between:

options.text_en:
Cost and profit
YouTube Telegram 88
GENERAL AWARENESS

34.explanation_en:
A demand curve graphically represents the functional
relationship between the price of a commodity and
the quantity demanded by consumers, holding other
factors constant (*ceteris paribus*). It typically slopes
downward from left to right due to the inverse relation-
ship between price and demand.
Important Facts:
➤ According to the Law of Demand, as the price of a
good increases, the quantity demanded decreases, and
vice versa.
➤ The downward slope of a standard demand curve is
caused by the substitution effect and the income
effect.
➤ Exceptions to the downward-sloping demand curve
include Giffen goods and Veblen goods.
➤ A movement along the demand curve is caused by a
change in the commodity's own price.
➤ A shift of the demand curve is caused by changes in
non-price determinants like consumer income,
tastes, or prices of related goods.

35.question_text_en:
Q.4 In national income accounting, depreciation is
subtracted from which of the following measures?
35.explanation_en:
In national income accounting, depreciation (con-
sumption of fixed capital) is subtracted from Gross
Domestic Product (GDP) to arrive at the Net
Domestic Product (NDP). The mathematical formu-
lation is: NDP = GDP − Depreciation.
Important Facts:
➤ Depreciation represents the monetary value of
wear and tear or obsolescence of capital assets during
the production process.
➤ Subtracting depreciation from Gross National Product
(GNP) yields Net National Product (NNP): NNP =
GNP − Depreciation.
➤ NNP at factor cost is considered the truest mea-
sure of a country's National Income.
➤ GDP measures the total monetary value of all final
goods and services produced within the domestic terri-
tory of a nation in a given financial year.
➤ Gross Capital Formation minus depreciation
gives Net Capital Formation, indicating actual
growth in the nation's capital stock.

36.question_text_en:
Q.2 Consider the following statements: Statement I: The
5th Five-year plan proposes the twin objectives of
removing poverty and attaining self-reliance. Statement II:
The rolling plan was launched between the sixth and the
seventh five-year plan, Which of the above statements
is/are correct?

options.text_en: Both statements I and II are correct
Both statements I and II are incorrect
Statement I is correct, Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, Statement II is correct

36.explanation_en:
Statement I is correct because the Fifth Five-Year
Plan (1974–1979) focused explicitly on "Garibi
Hatao" (removal of poverty) and achieving self-re-
liance. Statement II is incorrect because the
Rolling Plan was introduced by the Janata Party gov-
ernment between the Fifth and Sixth Five-Year
Plans (1978–1980), not between the sixth and seventh.
Important Facts:
➤ The draft of the Fifth Five-Year Plan was pre-
pared and launched under the guidance of D.P. Dhar.
➤ The Fifth Plan introduced the landmark Minimum
Needs Programme (MNP) in 1974.
➤ The concept of the Rolling Plan was originally con-
ceptualized by Swedish economist Gunnar Myrdal.
➤ The Janata Party government terminated the Fifth
Plan a year early in 1978 and initiated the Rolling Plan
for 1978–1980.
➤ The Sixth Five-Year Plan was later formally im-
plemented for the period 1980–1985 under the
Congress government.

37.question_text_en:
Q.9 What is the rationale behind granting Maharatna
status to certain Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs)?

options.text_en: To limit their autonomy in financial decisions
To provide greater financial and operational autonomy
To bring them under state government control

37.explanation_en:
The primary objective of conferring Maharatna sta-
tus on eligible Central Public Sector Enterprises
06 Download App Visit Website

(CPSEs) is to empower mega-enterprises with greater
operational and financial autonomy, enabling
them to expand operations, make substantial capital in-
vestments, and emerge as global giants.
Important Facts:
➤ The Maharatna category for Central Public
Sector Enterprises was introduced by the Government of
India in May 2010.
➤ Maharatna CPSE boards can decide on equity in-
vestment in joint ventures/subsidiaries up to 15% of
net worth (or Rs5,000 crore) without prior government
approval.
➤ To qualify for Maharatna status, a CPSE must already
hold Navratna status and be listed on an Indian
stock exchange.
➤ The qualifying criteria include an average annual net
profit of over Rs5,000 crore and average annual
turnover of over Rs25,000 crore over the past three
years.
➤ Prominent Maharatna companies include ONGC,
NTPC, IOCL, SAIL, BHEL, and Coal India
Limited.

38.question_text_en:
Q.10 Before 1991, a system of licenses, quotas, and
permits restricted private sector growth. What was this
system called?
38.explanation_en:
The elaborate bureaucratic framework of licenses, per-
mits, and quotas governing the establishment and ex-
pansion of private businesses in India prior to 1991 was
popularly termed the "License Raj" (or Permit Raj). It
was dismantled by the historic New Economic
Policy (NEP) of 1991.
Important Facts:
➤ The term "License Raj" was originally coined by vet-
eran freedom fighter and Swatantra Party founder C.
Rajagopalachari.
➤ Under this regime, the Industries (Development
and Regulation) Act, 1951 required firms to secure
government licenses to open, produce, or expand fac-
tory capacities.
➤ The Monopolies and Restrictive Trade
Practices (MRTP) Act, 1969 placed severe caps
YouTube Telegram 10
GENERAL AWARENESS
on the growth and assets of large corporations.
➤ The historic 1991 economic reforms were intro-
duced under Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao and
Finance Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh.
➤ The 1991 reforms ushered in the LPG model
(Liberalisation, Privatisation, and Globalisation), abolish-
ing industrial licensing for most sectors.

39.question_text_en:
Q.7 Which Article provides for the establishment of an
Inter-State Council?
39.explanation_en:
Article 263 of the Constitution of India provides for the
establishment of an Inter-State Council by the
President of India to investigate and discuss subjects of
common interest between the Union and the States or
among the States themselves.
Important Facts:
➤ The Inter-State Council was formally established in
1990 by a Presidential Order on the recommendation of
the Sarkaria Commission (1983–1988).
➤ The Prime Minister of India serves as the ex-of-
ficio Chairman of the Inter-State Council.
➤ The members include Chief Ministers of all States,
Chief Ministers of UTs with legislative assemblies,
Administrators of other UTs, and six Union Cabinet
Ministers.
➤ The Council functions as an advisory body to foster
cooperative federalism and resolve inter-governmental
disputes.
➤ Article 262 separately deals with the adjudication
of disputes relating to waters of inter-state rivers or river
valleys.

40.question_text_en:
Q.7 How many types of emergencies can be proclaimed
by the President of India under the Constitution?
40.explanation_en:
Part XVIII of the Constitution of India provides for three
types of emergencies that can be proclaimed by
the President: National Emergency (Article 352),
State Emergency / President's Rule (Article 356),
and Financial Emergency (Article 360).
Important Facts:
YouTube Telegram 12
GENERAL AWARENESS
➤ National Emergency (Article 352) is invoked
on the grounds of war, external aggression, or armed re-
bellion.
➤ The phrase "armed rebellion" replaced "internal dis-
turbance" via the 44th Constitutional Amendment
Act, 1978.
➤ President's Rule (Article 356) is declared upon
the failure of constitutional machinery in a state.
➤ Financial Emergency (Article 360) can be de-
clared if the financial stability or credit of India is threat-
ened; it has never been proclaimed in India.
➤ Emergency provisions in the Indian Constitution are
borrowed primarily from the Government of India
Act, 1935, while suspension of Fundamental Rights
during emergency is drawn from the Weimar
Constitution of Germany.

41.question_text_en:
Q.2 In a federal system resting on "limited government,"
the Supreme Court is designed to be the final authority for
what specific purpose?
41.explanation_en:
In a constitutional federal democracy governed by the
principle of limited government, the Supreme Court func-
YouTube Telegram 12
GENERAL AWARENESS
bsite, and every link redirects to that same website. If you are
ampered with — those links will not give you any mock test.
8
d High Court (9 Qs)
tions as the final arbiter and authoritative inter-
preter of the Constitution. This safeguards federal
equilibrium and prevents organs of state from encroach-
ing beyond their prescribed constitutional jurisdictions.
Important Facts:
➤ Under Article 132 and Article 133, the Supreme
Court of India exercises appellate jurisdiction over sub-
stantial questions of constitutional interpretation.
➤ The concept of Judicial Review empowers the
Supreme Court to invalidate legislative or executive acts
violating the Constitution (Article 13).
➤ Article 141 mandates that the law declared by the
Supreme Court shall be binding on all courts within the
territory of India.
➤ The doctrine of Basic Structure was propounded
by the Supreme Court in the landmark Kesavananda
Bharati case (1973).
➤ Under Article 32, the Supreme Court is designated
as the guarantor and protector of Fundamental Rights.

42.question_text_en:
Q.7 Which of the following is newly introduced in Bharatiya
Nyaya Sanhita?

options.text_en: Mob lynching as a specific offence

Manual scavenging
YouTube Telegram 13
GENERAL AWARENESS

42.explanation_en:
The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) has codified
mob lynching as a distinct and separate penal of-
fence under Section 103(2). Under this provision, murder
committed by a mob of five or more persons on grounds
of race, caste, sex, place of birth, language, or personal
belief attracts capital punishment or life imprisonment.
Important Facts:
➤ Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 re-
placed the Indian Penal Code (IPC) of 1860.
➤ Section 103(2) of the BNS specifically prescribes
punishment for murder committed by five or more per-
sons acting in concert.
➤ The prescribed punishment for mob lynching ranges
from life imprisonment to the death penalty,
along with a fine.
➤ The new criminal laws, including BNS, BNSS, and
BSA, came into official force across India on 1 July
2024.
➤ Sedition was omitted and replaced by offences en-
dangering the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of
India under Section 152.

43.question_text_en: Q.2 Which is the brightest star visible in the night sky?
43.explanation_en:
Sirius, commonly known as the Dog Star, is the
brightest individual star visible in Earth's night sky, with
an apparent visual magnitude of −1.46. It is located in
the constellation Canis Major.
YouTube Telegram 14
GENERAL AWARENESS
1
em (14 Qs)
Important Facts:
➤ Sirius appears remarkably bright primarily because of
its intrinsic luminosity combined with its proximity to
Earth (about 8.6 light-years away).
➤ Sirius is actually a binary star system consisting of a
main-sequence star (Sirius A) and a faint white dwarf
companion (Sirius B).
➤ The second brightest star visible in the night sky is
Canopus, situated in the constellation Carina with an
apparent magnitude of −0.74.
➤ Polaris (the North Star) is an indicator of celestial
north, but ranks only around the 48th brightest star in the
night sky.
➤ Alpha Centauri is the closest star system to our
Solar System, located at approximately 4.37 light-
years.

44.question_text_en:
Q.8 According to Hugo de Vries, what is the primary cause
of speciation?
44.explanation_en:
Dutch botanist Hugo de Vries proposed the
Mutation Theory of Evolution, asserting that spe-
ciation is caused by sudden, discontinuous large mu-
tations rather than the gradual minor variations pro-
posed by Charles Darwin. He termed this single-step
large mutation causing speciation as saltation.
Important Facts:
➤ Hugo de Vries formulated his Mutation Theory based
on his breeding experiments with the evening primrose
plant (Oenothera lamarckiana).
➤ Unlike Darwinian variations which are small and di-
rectional, mutations according to De Vries are random
and directionless.
➤ De Vries coined the term "saltation", meaning a
single-step, drastic mutation leading to the emergence of
a new species.
➤ Hugo de Vries is also celebrated as one of the three
scientists who independently rediscovered Gregor
Mendel's laws of inheritance in 1900.
➤ Modern evolutionary synthesis subsequently inte-
grated both Darwinian natural selection and genetic
mutations.

45.question_text_en:
Q.9 Which of the following statements accurately
describes a key objective of the Major Atmospheric
Cherenkov Experiment (MACE) Observatory in Hanle,
Ladakh?

options.text_en: To study visible light from stars.

To detect high-energy gamma rays.
05 Download App Visit Website
MOCKMATRIX
PRACTICE TO PERFECTION
To observe radio waves from space.
To measure cosmic microwave background radiation.

45.explanation_en:
The primary scientific objective of the Major
Atmospheric Cherenkov Experiment (MACE)
telescope at Hanle, Ladakh is the detection and ob-
servation of high-energy cosmic gamma rays. It
studies astrophysical phenomena such as blazars, pul-
sars, and supernova remnants through atmospheric
Cherenkov radiation.
Important Facts:
➤ The MACE telescope was constructed by the
Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) with
technical support from ECIL and other Indian partners.
➤ Positioned at an altitude of approximately 4,300
metres, MACE is the highest Cherenkov telescope in
the world.
➤ With a diameter of 21 metres, it is the second-
largest atmospheric Cherenkov telescope in the world.
➤ Hanle is situated in the Cold Desert of Ladakh,
recognized as a designated Dark Sky Reserve due
to pristine cloudless skies.
➤ The observatory detects Cherenkov flashes produced
when incoming very-high-energy (VHE) gamma
rays interact with Earth's upper atmosphere.

46.question_text_en:
Q.2 Which state has the highest number of national park
in India?
46.explanation_en:
Madhya Pradesh possesses the highest number of
National Parks among all Indian states, boasting 11
designated national parks. The Union Territory of
Andaman and Nicobar Islands ranks next with 9 national
parks, while Assam has 7.
Important Facts:
➤ Madhya Pradesh is home to prominent parks such as
Kanha, Bandhavgarh, Pench, Panna, and Kuno
National Park.
➤ Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh was cho-
sen as the premier site for the Cheetah
Reintroduction Project launched in 2022.
➤ Madhya Pradesh also holds the highest tiger popula-
tion in the country, earning the moniker "Tiger State
of India".
➤ India's very first national park was Hailey National
Park (presently Jim Corbett National Park), es-
tablished in 1936 in Uttarakhand.
➤ Hemis National Park in Ladakh is the largest na-
tional park in India by area, spanning over 4,400 sq
km.

47.question_text_en:
Q.11 Which novel by South Korean Nobel laureate Han
Kang was awarded the 2026 National Book Critics Circle
Award for Fiction?
47.explanation_en:
Han Kang's celebrated novel "We Do Not Part" re-
ceived widespread international critical acclaim and hon-
ours, including the National Book Critics Circle
Award for Fiction. The novel confronts the trauma of
the 1948 Jeju Island massacre through poignant lyrical
prose.
Important Facts:
➤ Han Kang was awarded the Nobel Prize in
Literature in 2024 "for her intense poetic prose that
confronts historical traumas and exposes the fragility of
human life."
➤ She became the first South Korean writer and the
first Asian woman to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.
➤ She previously achieved global prominence when her
novel "The Vegetarian" won the International
Booker Prize in 2016 (translated by Deborah Smith).
➤ The original Korean edition of *We Do Not Part* was
published in 2021 under the title *Jakbyeolhaji anne-
unda*.
➤ Her other internationally acclaimed novels include
"Human Acts" (2014) and "The White Book"
(2016).

48.question_text_en:
Q.12 Fill in the blank: The 2025 International Booker
Prize-winning book "Heart Lamp" is translated from
______ language.
48.explanation_en:
The acclaimed work "Heart Lamp" is translated from
the Kannada language. Indian literature translated
from regional languages into English has garnered dis-
tinguished recognition on major international platforms
including the Booker prizes.
Important Facts:
➤ The International Booker Prize is awarded an-
nually for a single book translated into English and pub-
lished in the United Kingdom or Ireland.
➤ The prize money of £50,000 is divided equally be-
tween the author and the translator.
➤ In 2022, author Geetanjali Shree made history
by winning the International Booker Prize for "Tomb of
Sand", translated from Hindi by Daisy Rockwell.
➤ Kannada is one of the designated Classical
Languages of India, having been accorded the sta-
tus in 2008.
➤ Major modern stalwarts of Kannada literature include
Jnanpith laureates Kuvempu, D.R. Bendre, and
U.R. Ananthamurthy.

49.question_text_en:
Q.6 What are the two major components of the GII
framework?

options.text_en: Knowledge Drivers and Innovation Impact Index
Innovation Input and Innovation Output Sub-Indices

Research Efficiency and Knowledge Commercialization
Scores

49.explanation_en:
The Global Innovation Index (GII) framework is
structured around two primary pillars: the Innovation
Input Sub-Index and the Innovation Output Sub-
Index. Together, these sub-indices measure the en-
abling environment for innovation and the actual results
achieved.
Important Facts:
➤ The GII is published annually by the World
Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO), a
49 Download App Visit Website

specialized agency of the United Nations.
➤ The Innovation Input Sub-Index evaluates five
pillars: Institutions, Human capital & research,
Infrastructure, Market sophistication, and Business so-
phistication.
➤ The Innovation Output Sub-Index evaluates
two pillars: Knowledge & technology outputs and
Creative outputs.
➤ The overall GII score is calculated as the average of
the Input and Output sub-indices.
➤ India has witnessed significant progress in the GII
rankings over the past decade, entering the top 40 in-
novative economies globally.

50.question_text_en:
Q.7 Which initiative was launched in 2025 to provide
digital identities and simplify verification for Indian Micro,
Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs)?
50.explanation_en:
The Udyam Assist Platform (UAP) was instituted
by the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
(MSME) to bring informal micro-enterprises into the for-
mal economic net by generating a formal digital iden-
tifier (Udyam Assist Certificate). This enables
small business units to seamlessly access priority sector
lending and statutory benefits.
Important Facts:
➤ The UAP initiative was developed by the Small
Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)
as the nodal implementing agency.
➤ It targets non-GST registered informal micro enter-
prises (IMEs) to facilitate access to Priority Sector
Lending (PSL).
➤ Formal registration on the main Udyam Portal origi-
nally commenced on 1 July 2020 following revised
MSME definitions.
➤ The revised MSME definition incorporates composite
criteria of investment in plant/machinery and an-
nual turnover.
➤ For a Micro Enterprise, the ceiling is set at invest-
ment up to Rs1 crore and turnover up to Rs5 crore.

1.question_text_en:
Q.10 Which of the following numbers will replace the
question mark (?) in the given series?
5, 7, 11, 19, 35, ?
1.explanation_en:
Q.10
Right option (A): Only I is implicit.
Explanation
• Assumption I is implicit because investing heavily in
smart classrooms and digital learning tools presupposes
that they can enhance students' learning experience.
• Assumption II is not implicit because the statement
says the school 'intends to... apply for grants', meaning
the grants have not yet been received.

➤ The headquarters of the World Trade Organization is
situated in Geneva, Switzerland.
➤ Unlike GATT, which covered only trade in goods, the
WTO encompasses trade in services (GATS) and intel-
lectual property (TRIPS).
➤ As of recent accessions, the WTO comprises 166
member nations.
➤ Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala became the first woman
and the first African to serve as Director-General of the
WTO.

29.question_text_en:
Q.2 In the context of the Gupta administration, what did
the term 'Uparika' signify?
29.explanation_en:
During the Gupta period, the empire was divided into
provinces known as Bhuktis, and the administrative
head or governor appointed over a Bhukti was desig-
nated as Uparika (or *Uparika Maharaja*).
Important Facts:
➤ Provinces (*Bhuktis*) were further subdivided into
districts termed Vishayas, administered by a
Vishayapati.
➤ The *Vishayapati* was assisted in district administra-
tion by an advisory council including the *Nagara
Sreshthi*, *Sarthavaha*, *Prathama Kulika*, and
*Prathama Kayastha*.
➤ Village level administration was managed by the vil-
lage headman called Gramika or *Gramadhyaksha*.
➤ Military commanders were designated as
Mahabaladhikrita or *Senapati*.
➤ The Gupta empire represented a decentralized ad-
ministrative structure with considerable local autonomy
given to provincial rulers.

30.question_text_en:
Q.2 The matter-of-fact manner in which Ibn Battuta
describes the buying and gifting of slaves most strongly
indicates that:

options.text_en:
Slavery was considered morally acceptable and socially
normal within his interpretive framework

He was unaware of the existence of social hierarchies in the
subcontinent
He intended to criticise the institution of slavery explicitly

Slavery was unique to the Indian subcontinent during this
period
YouTube Telegram 70
GENERAL AWARENESS
1
anate (3 Qs)

30.explanation_en:
Ibn Battuta's uncritical, casual accounts of purchasing,
employing, and presenting enslaved men and women as
customary gifts reflect the historical reality that slavery
was a deeply institutionalized, ubiquitous,
and socially normalized practice across the me-
dieval Islamic world and medieval Indian society.
Important Facts:
➤ Ibn Battuta was a renowned 14th-century
Moroccan scholar and traveler who arrived in India in
1333 during the reign of Sultan Muhammad bin
Tughlaq.
➤ He documented his travels across Africa, Asia, and
India in his famous book 'Rihla' (written in Arabic).
➤ Tughlaq appointed Ibn Battuta as the Qazi (judge)
of Delhi, a post he held for several years.
➤ In his writings, he records purchasing slaves, horses,
and almonds as customary presents to offer to the
Sultan.
➤ Female slaves were widely employed in imperial
households for domestic service, music, and royal
espionage.

31.question_text_en:
Q.3 The coexistence of Bernier's claim of declining
manufactures with his observation of thriving exports and
inflow of precious metals most strongly indicates that:

options.text_en:
Economic decline can coexist with strong external trade
under certain structural conditions

Export growth always reflects improvement in artisanal
production

State control completely destroyed commercial activity in
the Mughal Empire

Precious metals flowed into India despite the absence of
trade
YouTube Telegram 73
GENERAL AWARENESS

31.explanation_en:
François Bernier observed that despite widespread op-
pression of artisans and absence of private property
rights under Mughal rule, Indian textiles and handicrafts
dominated international commerce, bringing immense in-
flows of gold and silver. This apparent paradox demon-
strates that under specific historical and structural condi-
tions, a narrative of domestic artisanal dis-
tress can coexist with flourishing external
trade.
Important Facts:
➤ François Bernier was a French physician and
traveler who visited India during the reign of Emperor
Aurangzeb (1656–1668).
➤ He authored the famous travelogue 'Travels in the
Mogul Empire'.
➤ Bernier argued that the absence of private land own-
ership in the Mughal Empire was the primary cause of its
economic degradation.
➤ He described Mughal India as a place where the king
owned all land, reducing the state to a land of "beggars
and barbarians."
➤ However, historical records reveal that 17th-century
Mughal India was an economic manufacturing power-
house, supplying nearly a quarter of global textile output.

32.question_text_en:
Q.4 R. Nallakannu is best known for his association with
which movement?
32.explanation_en:
R. Nallakannu is a revered veteran communist leader
and social reformer who joined India's Freedom
struggle at a very young age, actively participating in
the anti-colonial resistance and peasants' rights strug-
gles in Tamil Nadu.
Important Facts:
➤ Born in 1925 in Tamil Nadu, he dedicated his entire
life to public service, agrarian labour rights, and environ-
mental protection.
➤ He participated actively in the Quit India Movement
and agrarian movements, facing imprisonment and tor-
ture under colonial rule.
YouTube Telegram 83
GENERAL AWARENESS
➤ He served as the State Secretary of the
Communist Party of India (CPI) in Tamil Nadu for
over two decades.
➤ In 2022, the Government of Tamil Nadu conferred
upon him the prestigious 'Thagaisal Thamizhar'
(Eminent Tamilian) award.
➤ He is widely celebrated for fighting legal battles
against illegal river-sand mining and environmental ex-
ploitation in the state.

33.question_text_en: Q.4 Microeconomics primarily deals with:
33.explanation_en:
Microeconomics is the branch of economics that fo-
cuses on the behavior, decision-making, and resource
allocation of individual economic units, such as
single consumers, households, and individual business
firms.
Important Facts:
➤ The terms 'microeconomics' and 'macroeconomics'
were coined by Norwegian economist Ragnar Frisch
in 1933.
➤ Key theories under microeconomics include con-
sumer demand theory, theory of the firm, and market
equilibrium pricing.
➤ In contrast, macroeconomics examines aggre-
gate economic phenomena such as national income,
gross domestic product, inflation, and fiscal budgets.
➤ Microeconomic analysis relies heavily on the ce-
teris paribus (all other things being equal) assump-
tion.
➤ The interaction of supply and demand in individual
88 Download App Visit Website

product and factor markets is central to microeconomic
study.

34.question_text_en: Q.5 A good with negative income elasticity is called:
34.explanation_en:
An inferior good is defined as a commodity whose de-
mand decreases when consumer income increases, giv-
ing it a negative income elasticity of demand
($E_y < 0$).
Important Facts:
➤ Income elasticity of demand measures the
percentage change in quantity demanded in response to
a percentage change in consumer income.
➤ A normal good has a positive income elasticity of
demand ($E_y > 0$), meaning consumption rises as in-
come increases.
➤ A luxury good is a category of normal goods where
income elasticity is greater than one ($E_y > 1$).
➤ A Giffen good is a special sub-category of inferior
goods where the quantity demanded increases as price
increases, violating the Law of Demand.
➤ Examples of inferior goods include low-grade cereals
or basic public transport services that people substitute
as they become wealthier.

35.question_text_en:
Q.3 What major issue did many parts of the country face
during the last year of the Sixth Plan (1984-85)?

options.text_en:
Widespread industrial strikes
99 Download App Visit Website
MOCKMATRIX
PRACTICE TO PERFECTION

35.explanation_en:
During the terminal year of the Sixth Five-Year Plan
(1984-85), several regions across India experienced
severe drought and famine-like conditions due to
deficient and erratic monsoon rainfall, which adversely
affected agricultural productivity and rural food grain
supplies.
Important Facts:
➤ The Sixth Five-Year Plan ran from 1980 to
1985 under the leadership of Prime Minister Indira
Gandhi.
➤ The target growth rate of the Sixth Plan was 5.2%,
while the achieved growth rate was 5.7%.
➤ The Sixth Plan marked the beginning of economic lib-
eralization and shifted emphasis towards poverty allevia-
tion.
➤ Major anti-poverty programmes like the Integrated
Rural Development Programme (IRDP) and
NREP were expanded during this plan.
➤ The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural
Development (NABARD) was established during
this period on 12 July 1982.

36.question_text_en:
Q.8 What is mob lynching under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita
(BNS)?

options.text_en:
Involves violence by a group on grounds like identity or
suspicion
Applies only when religious motives are proven
Requires prior conspiracy among all members
It is treated as simple assault

36.explanation_en:
Under Section 103(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya
Sanhita (BNS), 2023, mob lynching is specifically
defined as an offence where a group of five or more per-
sons acting in concert commits murder on grounds of
race, caste or community, sex, place of birth, language,
personal belief or any other similar ground.
Important Facts:
➤ Under Section 103(2) of the BNS, the penalty for
mob lynching ranges from life imprisonment to capital
punishment (death penalty), alongside a fine.
➤ The provision does not restrict motive to religion
alone; it broadly covers caste, race, linguistic identity, or
similar characteristics.
➤ The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) replaced the
36 Download App Visit Website

colonial-era Indian Penal Code (IPC) of 1860.
➤ The new criminal laws officially came into effect
across India on 1 July 2024.
➤ Prior to the BNS, the IPC had no separate, dedicated
statutory penal provision specifically penalizing mob
lynching.

37.question_text_en:
Q.9 What is the distinction between terrorism and
organized crime?

options.text_en:
There is no distinction under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita
(BNS).

Terrorism aims to threaten national security, while organized
crime focuses on unlawful gain.
Organized crime is limited to violent offences only.

37.explanation_en:
In legal and criminological frameworks, including the
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), terrorist acts are
motivated by ideological, political, or subversive goals
aimed at threatening the sovereignty, unity, and security
of the nation or terrorizing the public, whereas orga-
nized crime is driven by continuous unlawful activity
for material or financial benefit.
Important Facts:
➤ Under the BNS, terrorist acts are defined and pe-
nalized under Section 113.
➤ Organized crime is explicitly defined and penal-
ized as a distinct offence under Section 111 of the
BNS.
➤ Organized crime syndicates engage in illicit activities
like extortion, kidnapping, drug trafficking, and cyber-
crimes primarily for economic profit.
➤ Terrorism utilizes calculated acts of violence, sabo-
tage, and fear to destabilize government authority or
public safety.
➤ While organized crime syndicates and terror groups
occasionally form operational nexus, their core motiva-
tional objectives remain distinct.

38.question_text_en: Q.3 The crust is described as brittle in nature because:

options.text_en: It is composed of soft minerals

38.explanation_en:
The Earth's crust is described as brittle because it is
cold, rigid, and solid; when subjected to tectonic forces,
differential stress, and strain exceeding its elastic limit, it
fractures and breaks rather than undergoing ductile de-
formation.
Important Facts:
➤ The crust is the outermost solid shell of the Earth,
categorized into continental and oceanic crust.
➤ The continental crust is thicker and largely granitic
(Sial), while the oceanic crust is denser and basaltic
(Sima).
➤ Sudden fractures and displacements along faults in
the brittle crust cause earthquakes.
➤ Below the crust lies the Mohorovicic discontinu-
ity (Moho), which separates the crust from the mantle.
➤ Deeper mantle rocks deform plastically due to im-
mense temperature and confining pressure, contrasting
with the brittle crust.
50 Download App Visit Website

39.question_text_en:
Q.6 The North Western mineral region of India is
composed of territories from which of the following pairs of
states?
39.explanation_en:
The North-Western mineral belt of India covers
the Aravalli range in Rajasthan and extends into parts
of Gujarat. This region is rich in non-ferrous metallic
minerals, building stones, salt, and petroleum reserves.
Important Facts:
➤ Rajasthan is well known for rich deposits of copper,
lead, zinc, gypsum, marble, and sandstone.
➤ Gujarat is noted for petroleum and natural gas re-
serves (Ankleshwar, Cambay basin), salt production,
and bauxite.
➤ The famous Khetri Copper Belt and Zawar
zinc-lead mines are situated in Rajasthan within this
belt.
➤ Sedimentary rocks in this region are rich in non-
metallic mineral deposits such as limestone and fuller's
earth.
➤ This region contrasts with the Chota Nagpur plateau,
which is India's mineral heartland dominated by iron ore
and coal.

40.question_text_en:
Q.7 Fill in the blank: The largest linguistic group in India
belongs to the ________ language family.

options.text_en:
Indo-Aryan
73 Download App Visit Website
MOCKMATRIX
PRACTICE TO PERFECTION

40.explanation_en:
The Indo-Aryan sub-family of the Indo-European lan-
guage family constitutes the largest linguistic group in
India, spoken by approximately 78% of the country's
population. It includes prominent languages such as
Hindi, Bengali, Marathi, Punjabi, and Gujarati.
Important Facts:
➤ The second-largest linguistic family in India is the
Dravidian family, spoken by about 20% of the popula-
tion.
➤ The Austro-Asiatic (Austric) family is spoken by
around 1.11% of the population, including languages
like Santhali and Khasi.
➤ The Sino-Tibetan (Tibeto-Burman) family ac-
counts for roughly 0.85% of the population, predomi-
nantly in the Northeastern states.
➤ The Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution
currently recognizes 22 official languages.
➤ Hindi, Bengali, and Marathi are the three most spo-
ken native languages in India as per Census data.

41.question_text_en:
Q.1 Which of the following best explains the role of
enzymes in biochemical reactions?

options.text_en: They act as catalysts lowering activation energy
They change the end products permanently

41.explanation_en:
Enzymes act as biological catalysts that accelerate
chemical reactions by lowering the activation en-
ergy required for the transformation of substrates into
products, without being consumed or permanently al-
tered in the process.
Important Facts:
➤ Almost all enzymes are globular proteins, with the
exception of certain catalytic RNA molecules known as
ribozymes.
➤ The specific region of the enzyme where substrate
molecules bind and undergo reaction is called the ac-
tive site.
➤ The lock-and-key model was proposed by Emil
Fischer, while Daniel Koshland proposed the induced-
fit model.
➤ Enzymes do not alter the chemical equilibrium of a
reversible reaction; they merely accelerate the rate of
reaching equilibrium.
➤ Optimum enzyme catalytic activity is dependent on
physiological temperature and pH conditions.

42.question_text_en:
Q.10 Which primary satellite was carried by the PSLV-C62
mission?
42.explanation_en:
The Indian Space Research Organisation's (ISRO)
PSLV-C62 commercial mission carried EOS-N1 as its
primary Earth Observation satellite. The dedicated com-
mercial mission was managed through NewSpace
India Limited (NSIL), launching from the Satish
Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota.
Important Facts:
➤ EOS-N1 is designed to strengthen advanced space-
based Earth observation and monitoring capabilities.
➤ The PSLV-C62 mission was launched in the PSLV-
DL configuration featuring two strap-on solid motors.
➤ The launch vehicle carried multiple domestic and in-
ternational co-passenger satellites alongside the primary
YouTube Telegram 20
GENERAL AWARENESS
payload.
➤ It also hosted the Spanish startup Orbital Paradigm's
KID Capsule (re-entry technology demonstrator).
➤ NewSpace India Limited (NSIL) is the com-
mercial arm of the Department of Space, established in
2019.

43.question_text_en:
Q.11 What is the world-leading resolution of the Bharat
Forecasting System?
43.explanation_en:
The Bharat Forecasting System (BharatFS), de-
veloped by the Pune-based Indian Institute of Tropical
Meteorology (IITM) and deployed by the India
Meteorological Department (IMD), delivers numerical
weather prediction at a global benchmark 6-kilometer
resolution.
Important Facts:
➤ The system significantly improves localized weather
forecasts, extreme rainfall warnings, and cyclone track
predictions.
➤ It was adopted to replace earlier global forecasting
models operating at a 12-kilometer grid resolution.
➤ It utilizes the state-of-the-art high-performance super-
computing systems Arka and Arunika.
➤ The model is developed under the aegis of the
Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES).
➤ The high spatial resolution enables accurate pin-
pointing of micro-climatic and small-scale thunderstorm
events.

44.question_text_en:
Q.6 Fill in the blank: The IMEC initiative aims to
strengthen connectivity between India and ________
region.
44.explanation_en:
The India-Middle East-Europe Economic
Corridor (IMEC) was announced during the 2023
G20 New Delhi Summit to stimulate economic de-
velopment by fostering connectivity between India, the
Arabian Gulf (Middle East), and Europe. It com-
prises two distinct corridors: the East Corridor connect-
ing India to the Arabian Gulf and the Northern Corridor
25 Download App Visit Website

connecting the Arabian Gulf to Europe.
Important Facts:
➤ IMEC was launched on 9 September 2023 on
the sidelines of the G20 Summit in New Delhi.
➤ The project includes railway networks, ship-to-rail
transit networks, and road transport routes.
➤ Key signatories include India, the US, the UAE,
Saudi Arabia, France, Germany, Italy, and the
EU.
➤ Along with transport routes, it aims to deploy electric-
ity cables, high-speed digital lines, and clean hydrogen
pipelines.
➤ It is positioned as an alternative connectivity and
trade network to China's Belt and Road Initiative (BRI).

45.question_text_en:
Q.9 Who became the first woman Municipal
Commissioner of the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation
(BMC)?
45.explanation_en:
Senior IAS officer Ashwini Bhide achieved the his-
toric milestone of being appointed as the first woman
Municipal Commissioner of the Brihanmumbai
Municipal Corporation (BMC), Asia's richest civic
body.
Important Facts:
➤ Ashwini Bhide is an Indian Administrative Service
(IAS) officer of the 1995 batch from the Maharashtra
cadre.
➤ She previously earned widespread acclaim as the
Managing Director of the Mumbai Metro Rail
Corporation Limited (MMRCL) for executing the
Mumbai Metro Line 3 (Aqua Line) project.
➤ Established in 1888, the Brihanmumbai Municipal
Corporation manages civic governance for Mumbai.
➤ She also served as Additional Municipal
Commissioner of the BMC prior to this historic elevation.
➤ Smita Sabharwal is a Telangana cadre officer, while
Kiran Bedi is India's first female IPS officer.

46.question_text_en:
Q.13 Nipun Kumar Malhotra, recognized with the National
Award 2025, is known for his work in which area?
46.explanation_en:
Nipun Kumar Malhotra is a prominent disability
rights activist and social entrepreneur who received the
National Award (2025) under the Role Model cate-
gory for his pioneering contributions to disability
rights, universal accessibility, and social in-
clusion.
Important Facts:
➤ He is the founder and CEO of the Nipman
39 Download App Visit Website

Foundation, which promotes accessible infrastructure
and assistive technology.
➤ Born with Arthrogryposis, he has campaigned exten-
sively for barrier-free public transportation and accessi-
ble voting booths.
➤ He instituted the prestigious Nipman Foundation
Equal Opportunity Awards to recognize inclusive
institutions and employers.
➤ He is an alumnus of St. Stephen's College and the
Delhi School of Economics.
➤ The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
confers the National Awards annually on
International Day of Persons with Disabilities
(3 December).

47.question_text_en:
Q.14 A. E. Muthunayagam, awarded the Padma Shri in
2026, is known for his contributions in which field?
47.explanation_en:
Dr. A. E. Muthunayagam is a legendary aerospace
scientist honored with the Padma Shri in 2026 for his
trailblazing contributions to Space Research and
Engineering, notably serving as the founding director
of ISRO's Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre (LPSC) and
developing India's liquid rocket engine capabilities.
Important Facts:
➤ Dr. Muthunayagam played a monumental role in the
development of the Vikas engine, the workhorse liq-
uid engine for PSLV and GSLV.
➤ He was the founder-director of the Liquid
Propulsion Systems Centre (LPSC), established
by ISRO in 1985.
➤ He later served as the Secretary to the Government
of India in the Department of Ocean
Development.
➤ His pioneering efforts paved the way for India's self-
reliance in cryogenic and liquid rocket propulsion sys-
tems.
➤ He closely collaborated with Dr. Vikram Sarabhai and
Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam during the early formative years
of the Indian space programme.
YouTube Telegram 24
GENERAL AWARENESS

48.question_text_en:
Q.7 What is India's rank in the World Happiness Report
2026 out of the 147 countries featured?
48.explanation_en:
In the World Happiness Report 2026, India se-
cured the 116th rank among the 147 evaluated na-
tions. The report assesses national happiness based on
key variables such as GDP per capita, social support,
healthy life expectancy, freedom, generosity, and corrup-
tion perception.
Important Facts:
➤ The report is published annually by the United
Nations Sustainable Development Solutions
Network (UN SDSN).
➤ Finland retained its position as the world's happiest
country for multiple consecutive years.
➤ The publication marks the International Day of
Happiness, celebrated on 20 March.
➤ India had previously ranked 126th in the 2023 and
2024 editions of the report.
➤ The rankings are primarily based on life evaluations
reported from the Gallup World Poll.

49.question_text_en:
Q.8 As per the World Happiness Report 2026, which non-
European country ranked among the top five happiest
countries?
49.explanation_en:
According to the World Happiness Report 2026,
Costa Rica achieved an exceptional top-five position,
making it the only non-European nation to break into the
topmost tier of the rankings. The top ranks are tradition-
ally dominated by Nordic and European nations like
Finland, Denmark, and Iceland.
Important Facts:
➤ Costa Rica is a Central American country
renowned for high social cohesion and environmental
sustainability without a standing military since 1948.
➤ The top positions are overwhelmingly occupied by
Nordic countries led by Finland and Denmark.
➤ Previously, non-European countries that featured in
or near the top 10 included Israel and New Zealand.
➤ The World Happiness Report evaluates six key fac-
tors: GDP per capita, healthy life expectancy, social sup-
port, freedom to make life choices, generosity, and free-
dom from corruption.
➤ Costa Rica consistently achieves high happiness
metrics relative to its GDP per capita level.

50.question_text_en:
Q.8 The Green Credit Programme primarily aims to
incentivize which type of actions?

options.text_en:
Environmentally positive actions
YouTube Telegram 25
GENERAL AWARENESS

50.explanation_en:
The Green Credit Programme (GCP) is a market-
based mechanism designed to incentivize voluntary en-
vironmentally positive actions undertaken by in-
dividuals, communities, and private industries, thereby
promoting sustainable living and ecological restoration.
Important Facts:
➤ The programme was officially launched by the Prime
Minister during the COP28 Summit in Dubai in 2023.
➤ It operates under the broader vision of the LiFE
(Lifestyle for Environment) movement.
➤ Key eligible activities include afforestation, water har-
vesting, sustainable agriculture, and waste manage-
ment.
➤ The Indian Council of Forestry Research
and Education (ICFRE) serves as the GCP adminis-
trator.
➤ Green credits generated are tradeable on a domestic
platform and are independent of standard carbon credits.

26.explanation_en:
En Passant (French for "in passing") is a special
pawn-capturing move in the game of Chess.
Important Facts:
➤ It allows a pawn to capture an opponent's pawn that
has moved forward two squares on its initial move as if it
had only advanced one square.
➤ The capturing pawn must be on its fifth rank (for
11 Download App Visit Website

White) or fourth rank (for Black) to execute En Passant.
➤ The capture must be made on the very next turn im-
mediately following the opponent's double-step advance;
otherwise, the right is lost.
➤ Other special moves in chess include castling
(kingside and queenside) and pawn promotion.
➤ The governing international body for chess is the
International Chess Federation (FIDE), head-
quartered in Lausanne, Switzerland.

27.question_text_en:
Q.19 Which term refers to a situation in Chess where a
player is NOT in check but has no legal move available?
27.explanation_en:
In chess, a Stalemate occurs when the player whose
turn it is to move is not under check and has no legal
moves left, immediately resulting in a draw.
Important Facts:
➤ Under official FIDE rules, a stalemate immediately
ends the game with a half-point awarded to each player
(½–½).
➤ Checkmate, by contrast, occurs when a king is in
check and has no legal move to escape, ending the
game as a decisive loss.
➤ Stalemate is often utilized as a drawing tactic by a
player in an otherwise losing material position.
➤ Other drawing conditions in chess include threefold
repetition, fifty-move rule, and insufficient material.
➤ A standard chess game is played on an $8 \times 8$
grid consisting of 64 squares.

35.explanation_en:
A Proportional tax imposes the same constant tax
rate on all levels of income, automatically scaling tax col-
lection directly in proportion to total income changes.
Important Facts:
➤ Under a proportional tax system, the marginal tax
rate equals the average tax rate across all income brack-
ets.
➤ It is commonly referred to as a flat tax system.
➤ An automatic stabilizer moderates economic fluctua-
94 Download App Visit Website

tions automatically without requiring fresh legislative in-
tervention.
➤ In contrast, a progressive tax takes a higher percent-
age from higher-income earners, whereas a regressive
tax imposes a heavier relative burden on low earners.
➤ Corporate income taxes with a single statutory rate
function essentially on a proportional structure.

36.question_text_en:
Q.5 Which policy tool directly influences aggregate
demand through government spending?
36.explanation_en:
Fiscal policy directly impacts aggregate demand in an
economy through adjustments in government ex-
penditure and taxation measures.
Important Facts:
➤ Fiscal policy is formulated and implemented by the
Ministry of Finance / Government.
➤ Aggregate demand comprises consumption ($C$), in-
vestment ($I$), government spending ($G$), and net ex-
ports ($X - M$).
➤ Monetary policy, by contrast, controls money sup-
ply and interest rates and is managed by the central
bank (Reserve Bank of India).
➤ Expansionary fiscal policy involves increasing public
expenditure or lowering taxes to stimulate economic
growth.
➤ The theoretical foundation of fiscal intervention to
manage aggregate demand was established by John
Maynard Keynes.

37.question_text_en:
Q.11 Fill in the blank: The three main components of the
New Economic Policy are Liberalisation, Privatisation, and
______
37.explanation_en:
The New Economic Policy (NEP) launched in 1991 is fa-
mously structured around the three pillars of
Liberalisation, Privatisation, and
Globalisation (LPG).
Important Facts:
➤ The New Economic Policy was initiated under Prime
Minister P. V. Narasimha Rao and Finance Minister
Dr. Manmohan Singh.
➤ Liberalisation aimed at ending the license-permit
raj and dismantling unnecessary industrial restrictions.
➤ Privatisation encouraged private sector participa-
tion and strategic disinvestment in public sector enter-
prises.
➤ Globalisation opened the domestic economy to
foreign direct investments (FDI) and international trade
integration.
➤ The immediate catalyst for these sweeping reforms
was a severe Balance of Payments (BoP) crisis in
1991.

38.question_text_en:
Q.10 The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 is
applicable to which of the following?

options.text_en: Restricted only to civil court proceedings

All judicial proceedings and all executive inquiries
YouTube Telegram 13
GENERAL AWARENESS
Restricted only to High and Supreme Courts

38.explanation_en:
Under Section 1, the Bharatiya Sakshya
Adhiniyam, 2023 applies to all judicial proceed-
ings in or before any court, including courts-martial
(other than those convened under specific service acts).
Important Facts:
➤ The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 replaced
the colonial Indian Evidence Act, 1872.
➤ The Act came into statutory force across India on 1
July 2024.
➤ It does not apply to affidavits presented to any court
or officer, nor to proceedings before an arbitrator.
➤ It accords primary evidentiary status to electronic
and digital records, treating them on par with physi-
cal documents.
➤ The enactment forms part of the triad of new criminal
laws alongside the BNS, 2023 and the BNSS, 2023.

39.question_text_en:
Q.11 Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita,
2023, what is the defining feature of a "Zero FIR"?

options.text_en: A report where no specific suspect is named
A report filed regardless of the crime's jurisdiction
A report filed electronically without visiting a station
A report filed when no physical evidence exists

39.explanation_en:
A Zero FIR allows a cognizable offence to be regis-
tered at any police station, irrespective of whether
the crime took place within its territorial jurisdiction.
Important Facts:
➤ Provision for Zero FIR is explicitly codified under
Section 173 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha
Sanhita (BNSS), 2023.
➤ After recording the Zero FIR, the police station trans-
fers the case documents to the appropriate jurisdictional
police station for investigation.
➤ It ensures prompt registration of serious offences, es-
pecially crimes against women, without procedural de-
lays over jurisdiction.
➤ The concept gained legal momentum following the
recommendations of the Justice J.S. Verma
Committee in 2013.
➤ A Zero FIR is given the number serial 0 until it
37 Download App Visit Website

reaches the concerned police station where a regular
FIR number is assigned.

40.question_text_en:
Q.4 The outer core of the Earth's interior exists in which
physical state?
40.explanation_en:
The Earth's outer core exists in a liquid state due
to high temperatures exceeding the melting point of its
iron-nickel alloy.
Important Facts:
➤ The outer core extends from a depth of approxi-
mately 2,900 km to 5,150 km beneath the Earth's
surface.
➤ The boundary between the mantle and the outer core
is called the Gutenberg discontinuity.
➤ It is primarily composed of molten iron and nickel
(often termed the NiFe layer).
➤ Convection currents of molten iron in the outer core
generate the Earth's geomagnetic field via the geo-
dynamo effect.
➤
S-waves (secondary/shear seismic waves)
cannot pass through liquids and thus create an S-wave
shadow zone across the outer core.

41.question_text_en:
Q.4 Assam contributes approximately how much to India's
total tea production?
41.explanation_en:
Assam is India's largest tea-producing state, contribut-
ing approximately 50% (over half) of the country's
total tea yield.
Important Facts:
➤ The Brahmaputra Valley and Barak Valley are
the primary tea cultivation hubs in Assam.
➤ Indigenous tea plants in Assam were first identified
by British officer Robert Bruce in 1823.
➤ The state is famous for producing rich, full-bodied
black tea variety known as *Camellia sinensis* var.
*assamica*.
➤ The head office of the Tea Board of India is lo-
cated in Kolkata, West Bengal.
➤ Jorhat in Assam hosts the renowned Tocklai Tea
Research Institute, one of the oldest tea research
centers in the world.

42.question_text_en:
Q.9 Which of the following correctly describes the
components and charges involved in the formation of a
nucleosome?

options.text_en:
Negatively charged RNA wrapped around a neutral histone
octamer.

Positively charged DNA wrapped around a negatively
charged histone hexamer.

Negatively charged DNA wrapped around a positively
charged histone octamer.

Neutral DNA wrapped around a basic protein complex rich
in Lysine and Arginine.

42.explanation_en:
A nucleosome consists of negatively charged
DNA wrapped around a core of eight positively
charged histone proteins called a histone octamer.
99 Download App Visit Website

Important Facts:
➤ DNA carries a net negative charge due to the pres-
ence of phosphate groups along its sugar-phosphate
backbone.
➤ Histones are basic proteins rich in the positively
charged amino acid residues lysine and arginine.
➤ The histone octamer contains two molecules each of
four core histones: H2A, H2B, H3, and H4.
➤ A typical nucleosome wraps approximately 200
base pairs (bp) of DNA around the histone core.
➤ Nucleosomes in chromatin give a characteristic
"beads-on-a-string" appearance under an electron
microscope.

43.question_text_en:
Q.12 The LVM3 rocket employed for the CMS-03 mission
is classified under which launch vehicle class?
43.explanation_en:
ISRO's LVM3 (Launch Vehicle Mark-3), formerly known
as GSLV Mk III, is classified as a Heavy lift launch
vehicle designed to carry heavy communication satel-
lites.
06 Download App Visit Website

Important Facts:
➤ LVM3 is a three-stage launch vehicle with two solid
strap-on motors (S200), a core liquid stage (L110), and
a cryogenic upper stage (C25).
➤ It has the capacity to launch payloads of up to 4,000
kg into Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (GTO).
➤ For Low Earth Orbit (LEO), LVM3 can deliver pay-
loads of approximately 8,000 kg.
➤ The vehicle successfully executed prestigious mis-
sions including Chandrayaan-2, Chandrayaan-3,
and OneWeb commercial deployments.
➤ It is the designated launch vehicle for India's indige-
nous crewed spaceflight programme, Gaganyaan.

44.question_text_en:
Q.13 The Bharat Forecasting System has been developed
by which institute?

options.text_en: Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology, Pune

44.explanation_en:
The advanced multi-scale Bharat Forecasting
System (BFS) high-resolution weather forecasting plat-
form was developed by the Indian Institute of
Tropical Meteorology (IITM), Pune.
Important Facts:
➤ IITM Pune functions as an autonomous research in-
stitution under the Ministry of Earth Sciences
(MoES).
➤ It spearheads climate modelling, monsoon dynamics,
and seasonal atmospheric forecasting in India.
➤ The system harnesses high-performance computing
systems such as the Pratyush and Mihir supercom-
puters.
➤ IITM was established in November 1962 as the
Institute of Tropical Meteorology under the WMO/UNDP
project.
➤ It collaborates closely with the India Meteorological
Department (IMD) to provide operational extreme
weather alerts.

45.question_text_en:
Q.5 Geoengineering refers to large-scale interventions in
which system to intentionally cool the planet?

options.text_en:
Solar radiation system
15 Download App Visit Website
MOCKMATRIX
PRACTICE TO PERFECTION

45.explanation_en:
Geoengineering refers to deliberate, large-scale tech-
nological interventions directly into the Earth's cli-
mate system to counteract anthropogenic global
warming and cool the planet.
Important Facts:
➤ Geoengineering approaches are broadly divided into
Solar Radiation Management (SRM) and
Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR).
➤ SRM seeks to reflect a small fraction of sunlight back
into space using techniques like stratospheric aerosol in-
jection.
➤ CDR technologies aim to sequester greenhouse
gases directly through afforestation, bioenergy with car-
bon capture, and direct air capture.
➤ Major international bodies, including the IPCC, eval-
uate geoengineering as potential supplementary re-
sponses with notable ecological risks.
➤ The concept was discussed as early as the mid-20th
century, gaining renewed prominence amid accelerating
global climate shifts.

46.question_text_en: Q.7 Chabahar Port is located in which country?
46.explanation_en:
Chabahar Port is a deep-water seaport situated in
southeastern Iran, on the Gulf of Oman. It provides
India an alternative transit route to Afghanistan and
Central Asia, bypassing Pakistan.
Important Facts:
➤ The port lies in the Sistan and Baluchestan
Province of Iran along the Makran coast.
➤ India and Iran signed an agreement to develop the
Shahid Beheshti terminal at Chabahar Port.
➤ It is an integral link in the International North–
South Transport Corridor (INSTC) network.
➤ India commenced development of the port following a
bilateral agreement first conceptualized in 2003.
➤ It provides direct maritime access to landlocked
Afghanistan without passing through overland
Pakistani routes.

47.question_text_en:
Q.10 In January 2026, which person was given the post of
Vigilance Commissioner?
47.explanation_en:
Senior officer Praveen Vashista was appointed to the
post of Vigilance Commissioner in the Central
Vigilance Commission (CVC).
Important Facts:
➤ The Central Vigilance Commission (CVC)
was set up in 1964 based on the recommendations of
the Santhanam Committee.
➤ The CVC was accorded statutory status by the enact-
ment of the Central Vigilance Commission Act,
2003.
➤ The Commission consists of a Central Vigilance
Commissioner as chairperson and not more than two
Vigilance Commissioners.
➤ Members of the CVC are appointed by the
President of India on the recommendation of a
three-member committee consisting of the Prime
Minister, the Union Home Minister, and the Leader of the
Opposition in the Lok Sabha.
➤ They hold office for a term of four years or until at-
taining the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.

General) of the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) in
January 2026?

appointed to head the Indo-Tibetan Border Police
(ITBP) as its Director General.

lished on 24 October 1962 in the wake of the Sino-
Indian conflict.
➤ ITBP is primarily tasked with guarding the 3,488 km
long India-China border along the Himalayas.
➤ It operates under the administrative authority of the

➤ The motto of the ITBP is "Shaurya - Dridhata -

49.question_text_en:
Q.9 What is India's rank in the Human Development Index
(HDI) 2025?
49.explanation_en:
India secured the 130th position in the Human
Development Index (HDI) report published by the
United Nations Development Programme
(UNDP).
Important Facts:
➤ The Human Development Index is published annually
by the UNDP.
➤ The HDI was developed by Pakistani economist
Mahbub ul Haq and Indian Nobel laureate Amartya
Sen in 1990.
➤ HDI measures achievements across three basic di-
mensions: a long and healthy life, access to
knowledge, and a decent standard of living.
➤ Life expectancy at birth, expected years of schooling,
mean years of schooling, and GNI per capita are its pri-
mary indicators.
50 Download App Visit Website

➤ In the global rankings, nations like Switzerland and
Norway consistently feature at the top tier.

50.question_text_en:
Q.10 What is the name of the life evaluation scale used in
the World Happiness Report?
50.explanation_en:
The World Happiness Report measures subjective
well-being using the Cantril Ladder question, asking
respondents to evaluate their lives on a ladder scale
from 0 to 10.
Important Facts:
➤ The scale was originally created by social researcher
Hadley Cantril in 1965.
➤ On this ladder scale, 10 represents the best possible
life and 0 represents the worst possible life.
➤ The World Happiness Report is released by the UN
Sustainable Development Solutions Network.
➤ The survey data used for evaluating the rankings is
gathered by the Gallup World Poll.
➤ Key variables assessed alongside the ladder include
GDP per capita, social support, healthy life expectancy,
freedom, generosity, and corruption perceptions.

specific survey instrument to determine the primary "Life
Evaluation" ranking?

Happiness Report uses the Cantril Self-Anchoring
Striving Scale (Cantril Ladder), where respondents
rate their current life on a ladder scale from 0 to 10.

a ladder with rungs numbered from 0 (worst possible
life) to 10 (best possible life).

searcher Hadley Cantril in 1965.

lished since 2012 by the Sustainable Development
Solutions Network.

scores: GDP per capita, social support, healthy life ex-
pectancy, freedom, generosity, and absence of
corruption.

good?
34.explanation_en:

low-income households, serving as a classic example of
an inferior or Giffen good. For a Giffen good, an in-
crease in its price leads to an increase in quantity de-
manded because consumers cannot afford superior sub-
stitutes.
Important Facts:
➤ Giffen goods are rare, highly inferior goods that vio-
late the Law of Demand.
YouTube Telegram 89

Sir Robert Giffen.

and strongly outweighs the substitution effect.

sloping.
➤ Staple low-cost carbohydrates like coarse grains or
potatoes commonly illustrate Giffen behavior.

ment expenditure over total receipts excluding borrow-

ings, representing the total amount of money the govern-
ment needs to borrow in a financial year.
Important Facts:

the government from all domestic and external sources.

enue expenditure and revenue receipts.
➤ Primary Deficit is calculated as Fiscal Deficit mi-
nus interest payments (Primary Deficit = Fiscal
Deficit − Interest Payments).
➤ The FRBM Act, 2003 was enacted in India to insti-
tutionalize fiscal discipline and reduce deficits.

45.question_text_en:
Q.10 If a double-stranded DNA molecule contains 20%
Adenine, what is the expected percentage of Guanine
based on Chargaff's rules?
45.explanation_en:
According to Chargaff's rules, Adenine equals Thymine
(A = T = 20%, total 40%). The remaining bases Guanine
and Cytosine constitute 60% together, and since G = C,
Guanine is 30% (60% / 2).
Important Facts:
➤ Chargaff's rules were formulated by biochemist
Erwin Chargaff in the late 1940s.
➤ The rule states that in double-stranded DNA, the ratio
of purines to pyrimidines is 1:1 (A + G = T + C).
➤ Adenine pairs with Thymine via two hydrogen
bonds (A=T).
➤ Guanine pairs with Cytosine via three hydrogen
bonds (G≡C).
➤ Chargaff's findings provided critical experimental data
for Watson and Crick's double-helix model of DNA.

geographical label to a religious identity most clearly
illustrates which historical process?

options.text_en:

foreign rulers

Evolution of social categories where terms acquire new
meanings over time

Consistent use of cultural terms without any change in
meaning
Direct translation of regional names into religious identities

33.explanation_en:
The semantic evolution of the term 'Hindu'—from an Old
Persian geographical descriptor for people living beyond
the Indus (Sindhu) River to a distinct religious identifier—
exemplifies how social categories evolve and ac-
quire new meanings over historical periods.
Important Facts:
➤ The word 'Hindu' derives from the Sanskrit root
Sindhu, referring to the Indus River system.
➤ In ancient Achaemenid Persian inscriptions (e.g.,
Darius I at Persepolis/Naqsh-e-Rustam), Hiduš was
employed purely as a geographic designation.
➤ The Greeks modified the term to Indos, from which
the European term India originated.
➤ In Arabic and Persian medieval texts, the term Al-
Hind denoted the geographic territory and its inhabi-
tants.
➤ Only in late medieval and colonial periods did the
term gradually solidify into a cohesive religious identity.

achieved growth rate was 5.7%.
Important Facts:
➤ The Sixth Five-Year Plan ran for the period of
1980 to 1985 under Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.
➤ The plan targeted a growth rate of 5.2% and
achieved an actual growth rate of 5.7%, making it suc-
cessful.
➤ Major poverty alleviation programmes like the
Integrated Rural Development Programme
(IRDP) and TRYSEM were emphasized.
➤ The NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and
Rural Development) was established during this plan in
1982.
➤ The plan marked the beginning of economic liberal-
ization in the Indian economy.

38.question_text_en:
Q.14 Fill in the blank: The government identifies certain
high-performing PSUs and grants them greater autonomy
by giving them the status of 'Navratna' or '________'.
38.explanation_en:
The Government of India categorizes profitable Central
Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) into Maharatna,
Navratna, and Miniratna (Category-I and Category-
II) to confer operational and financial autonomy.
Important Facts:
➤ The Navratna and Miniratna schemes were first
introduced by the Government of India in 1997.
➤ In 2009, the government introduced an even higher
category known as Maharatna for mega-enterprises.
➤ Miniratna CPSEs are sub-divided into two groups:
Category-I and Category-II, based on profitability
and net worth.
➤ These statuses allow PSU boards to incur capital ex-
penditures without prior government approval up to de-
fined monetary ceilings.
➤ The categorization is administered by the
Department of Public Enterprises (DPE) under
the Ministry of Finance.

39.question_text_en:
Q.14 Which of the following punishments is newly
introduced in Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
39.explanation_en:
Community service has been introduced as a new
form of punishment for petty offences under Section 4 of
the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS).
Important Facts:
➤ Section 4 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita,
2023 explicitly adds Community service to the list
of recognized punishments.
➤ It is intended for minor and petty offences like small
thefts, defamation, or public misconduct to encourage
reformative justice.
➤ The BNS, 2023 replaced the colonial-era Indian
Penal Code (IPC) of 1860.
➤ Other traditional punishments retained include death,
imprisonment for life, imprisonment (rigorous/simple),
forfeiture of property, and fine.
➤ The new criminal laws came into legal enforcement
across India on 1 July 2024.

Under Section 173 of the Bharatiya Nagarik
Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS), provisions for
registering an e-FIR (electronic communication) and for-
mal statutory recognition of Zero FIR (irrespective of
jurisdiction) have been explicitly strengthened.
Important Facts:
➤ The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita,
2023 (BNSS) replaced the colonial-era Code of
Criminal Procedure, 1973 (CrPC).
➤ Section 173 of BNSS allows information about cog-
nizable offences to be given electronically (e-FIR).
➤ It also mandates that an FIR can be registered at any
police station regardless of jurisdiction (Zero FIR), to
be transferred later.
➤ For e-FIRs, the informant must sign the formal docu-
ment within three days of submission.
➤ The new criminal procedural code came into force
across India on 1 July 2024.

41.question_text_en:
Q.6 Which earthquake waves travel fastest through the
Earth?
41.explanation_en:
Primary waves (P-waves) are longitudinal compres-
sional waves and are the fastest seismic waves, travel-
ing through the Earth and arriving first at seismograph
stations.
Important Facts:
➤ P-waves travel at velocities between 5 to 8 km/s
in the Earth's crust, which is faster than S-waves and
surface waves.
➤ P-waves can propagate through all three mediums:
solids, liquids, and gases.
➤ They are longitudinal waves, meaning particle
motion is parallel to the direction of wave propagation.
➤ Secondary waves (S-waves) are slower trans-
verse waves and can travel only through solids.
➤
Surface waves (Rayleigh and Love waves)
are the slowest but typically cause the greatest structural
damage.

42.question_text_en:
Q.4 At present, how many National Waterways have been
declared in India under the National Waterways Act,
2016?
42.explanation_en:
Under the National Waterways Act, 2016, the
Government of India declared 111 National
Waterways (NWs) by adding 106 new waterways to
the existing 5.
Important Facts:
➤ The National Waterways Act, 2016 came into
effect in April 2016.
➤ The Act recognized a total of 111 waterways as
National Waterways for inland navigation.
➤ National Waterway 1 (NW-1) on the Ganga-
Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system is the longest opera-
tional waterway (1,620 km).
➤ Inland waterways in India are managed and devel-
oped by the Inland Waterways Authority of India
(IWAI).
➤ IWAI was established in 1986 and is headquartered
in Noida, Uttar Pradesh.

During the intrinsic pathway of programmed cell death
(apoptosis), cytochrome c is released from the inter-
membrane space of the mitochondria into the cy-
tosol, triggering caspase activation.
Important Facts:
➤ Mitochondria are known as the "powerhouses
of the cell" because they synthesize ATP via cellular
respiration.
➤ In the intrinsic apoptotic pathway, mitochondrial outer
membrane permeabilization causes the release of cy-
tochrome c.
➤ Once released into the cytosol, cytochrome c binds to
Apaf-1 to form the apoptosome, which activates ini-
tiator caspases.
➤ Mitochondria possess their own double-stranded cir-
cular DNA and 70S ribosomes.
➤ The inner mitochondrial membrane contains folds
known as cristae to increase surface area.

Q.18 Which mission preceded the LVM3-M5 flight of the
LVM3 rocket?
44.explanation_en:
The Chandrayaan-3 mission was launched on the
LVM3-M4 rocket flight on 14 July 2023, making it the
immediate predecessor to the LVM3-M5 operational
launch vehicle flight.
Important Facts:
➤ The Chandrayaan-3 lunar exploration mission was
designated as the LVM3-M4 mission.
➤ ISRO's LVM3 (Launch Vehicle Mark-3) was
previously designated as the GSLV Mk III.
➤ LVM3 is a three-stage launch vehicle with two solid
strap-on motors (S200), a liquid core stage (L110), and
a cryogenic upper stage (C25).
➤ Chandrayaan-3 achieved a historic soft landing on
the south polar region of the Moon on 23 August
2023.
➤ Aditya-L1 was launched using the PSLV-C57
rocket, not an LVM3 vehicle.

by which Union Minister?

Jitendra Singh, launched the high-resolution Bharat
Forecasting System (BFS).
Important Facts:
➤ The Bharat Forecasting System (BFS) was
developed to provide high-resolution weather forecasts
across India.
08 Download App Visit Website

Earth Sciences (MoES) and the India
Meteorological Department (IMD).
➤ Dr. Jitendra Singh holds the portfolio of the
Ministry of Science and Technology and Ministry of Earth
Sciences.
➤ The system harnesses high-performance computing
to enhance regional forecasting for monsoons, storms,
and extreme rainfall events.
➤ It significantly improves disaster preparedness and
agro-meteorological advisory services for farmers.

46.question_text_en:
Q.7 What is the primary goal of geoengineering
interventions?
46.explanation_en:
The primary goal of climate geoengineering
(specifically Carbon Dioxide Removal techniques) is to
deliberately mitigate global warming by removing
greenhouse gases from the atmosphere or reflecting
solar radiation.
Important Facts:
➤ Geoengineering interventions are broadly catego-
rized into Solar Radiation Management (SRM)
and Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR).
➤ Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR) technologies
capture and sequester carbon dioxide directly from the
atmosphere.
➤ Examples of CDR include direct air capture
(DAC), afforestation, and ocean fertilization.
➤ The ultimate objective of geoengineering is to counter
anthropogenic climate change and lower planetary
heating.
➤ These technologies are studied extensively under the
Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change
(IPCC) frameworks.

the Government of India to review and recommend
changes to central government employees' pay struc-
ture.
➤ Justice (Retd.) Ranjana Prakash Desai previ-

and Chairperson of the Press Council of India.
➤ The 7th Central Pay Commission was headed
by Justice A.K. Mathur and was set up in 2014.
➤ Central Pay Commissions are usually constituted
once every 10 years.
➤ Recommendations of the Pay Commission apply to
central government employees, armed forces personnel,
and pensioners.

49.question_text_en:
Q.14 The Human Development Index (HDI) is released by
which organization?
49.explanation_en:
The Human Development Index (HDI) is compiled
and published annually by the United Nations
Development Programme (UNDP) as part of its
Human Development Report.
Important Facts:
➤ The HDI was devised and introduced in 1990 by
Pakistani economist Mahbub ul Haq and Indian econ-
omist Amartya Sen.
➤ It evaluates countries across three dimensions: life
expectancy, education (mean and expected
years of schooling), and gross national income
(GNI) per capita.
➤ The report is published annually under the aegis of
the United Nations Development Programme
(UNDP).
➤ The HDI value ranges on a scale between 0 and 1,

ment.
➤ The UNDP headquarters is located in New York
City, USA.

making it the unhappiest country globally?

consistently ranked at the very bottom of the global list
as the least happy country.

the UN Sustainable Development Solutions
Network.
➤ Afghanistan has held the lowest position among all
surveyed countries due to severe humanitarian crises.
➤ Finland has routinely secured the top rank as the
world's happiest country for multiple consecutive years.
➤ The index relies on data from the Gallup World
Poll assessing factors like GDP per capita, social sup-
port, and healthy life expectancy.
➤ The report is traditionally released around the
International Day of Happiness (20 March).

continuously struck by the player?

tion ritual known as the Purvaranga.

on population size, literacy, sex ratio, workforce, and ur-
banization.

34.explanation_en:

as Terra Mater (or Tellus).

Gaia.
➤ Earth is the third planet from the Sun and the densest
planet in the solar system.

Apollo and solar deities to signify supreme spiritual wis-
dom.
➤ Sculptures in Gandhara art were predominantly made
using grey sandstone and stucco.
➤ Other prominent stylistic features include wavy hair,
realistic anatomical drapery, and sharp facial features.

40.question_text_en:
Q.1 Which organization is responsible for enforcing
criminal laws in India?
40.explanation_en:
In India, the enforcement and administration of criminal
law fall under the mandate of the Police (investigation
and law enforcement) and the Judiciary (adjudication
and sentencing).
Important Facts:
➤ Under the Seventh Schedule of the Indian
Constitution, 'Police' and 'Public Order' are State
subjects under List II.

amend substantive and procedural criminal laws such as
the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).

stitutional safeguards, and issues penal sentences upon
trial conviction.
➤ The Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) /
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS)
governs criminal procedural enforcement in India.
➤ Law enforcement agencies investigate cognizable of-
fences under statutory mandates without prior judicial
warrants.

41.question_text_en:
Q.2 What are the specialized receptors that detect the
sensation of taste called?
41.explanation_en:
Sensory receptors that detect taste stimuli are known as
gustatory receptors, predominantly clustered within
taste buds on the tongue surface.
Important Facts:

sweet, sour, salty, bitter, and umami.
➤ Receptors responsible for detecting the sense of
smell are known as olfactory receptors.
➤ Taste buds reside within elevated projections on the
tongue known as papillae (circumvallate, foliate, and
fungiform).
➤ Taste sensations are relayed to the central nervous
system via cranial nerves VII (Facial), IX
(Glossopharyngeal), and X (Vagus).
➤ Gustatory perception combines closely with olfactory
signals to create overall flavor perception in the brain.

tured detailed observations of active regions and a so-

27.question_text_en: Q.8 Teejan Bai is associated with which folk tradition?
27.explanation_en:
Teejan Bai is an internationally acclaimed exponent of
Pandavani, the traditional narrative folk singing art
form of Chhattisgarh.
