➤ In Pandavani, stories from the epic Mahabharata
are narrated with musical accompaniment, primarily
holding a stringed instrument called Tambura.
➤ Teejan Bai performs the Kapalik style of Pandavani,
characterized by dynamic enactments, while Vedamati
is the seated recitation style.
➤ She was honoured with the Padma Shri in 1988,
the Padma Bhushan in 2003, and the Padma
Vibhushan in 2019.
➤ She received the Sangeet Natak Akademi
Award in 1995 and the prestigious Fukuoka Arts
and Culture Prize in 2018.
➤ Pandavani is native to Chhattisgarh and neighbor-
ing tribal belts of Central India.

ing art forms passed down orally across generations.
➤ In Pandavani, the lead artist enacts the heroic deeds
of the Pandavas, portraying Bhima as the central
heroic figure.
➤ The lead narrator is accompanied by supporting mu-
sicians playing instruments such as the Kartal,

Bai are the most renowned pioneers of this folk art.

Nakula-Sahadeva, and Draupadi.
➤ The largest and most elaborately carved ratha among
them is the Dharmaraja Ratha, dedicated to Lord
Shiva.
➤ Mahabalipuram is recognized globally as a
UNESCO World Heritage Site (inscribed in 1984).

32.question_text_en:
Q.1 The Battle of Talikota (1565 AD) led to the decline of
which major South Indian empire?
32.explanation_en:
The Battle of Talikota (also called the Battle of
Rakkasa-Tangadi) fought in 1565 AD brought a cata-
strophic defeat and led to the collapse of the
Vijayanagara Empire.
Important Facts:
➤ The battle was fought between the Vijayanagara
Empire led by de facto ruler Aliya Rama Raya and
the combined forces of the Deccan Sultanates (Bijapur,
Golconda, Ahmadnagar, and Bidar).
➤ Following the defeat, the magnificent capital city of

by brothers Harihara I and Bukka Raya I of the

Penukonda and later to Chandragiri under the

➤ The prominent dynasties that ruled Vijayanagara
were Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva, and Aravidu.

33.question_text_en: Q.7 What is meant by the opportunity cost?
33.explanation_en:
In economics, opportunity cost represents the value
or benefit of the next best alternative foregone
when making a decision between mutually exclusive
choices.
Important Facts:
➤ The concept of opportunity cost is foundational to un-
derstanding the economic problem of scarcity and
choice.
➤ Austrian economist Friedrich von Wieser formu-
lated the formal concept of alternative or opportunity
cost.
➤ Opportunity cost includes both explicit out-of-pocket
expenses and implicit non-monetary trade-offs.
➤ The slope of the Production Possibility
Frontier (PPF) measures the marginal opportunity
cost of producing one good over another.
➤ Sunk costs (past non-recoverable expenditures) are
not considered when calculating opportunity cost.

34.question_text_en:
Q.9 A "Deficit Budget" is usually preferred during which
economic condition?
34.explanation_en:
A deficit budget—where government expenditures ex-
ceed revenues—is typically implemented during an eco-
nomic depression or recession to inject aggre-
gate demand and stimulate output and employment.
Important Facts:
➤ Deficit financing to pull an economy out of recession
is a central tenet of Keynesian economics, formu-
lated by John Maynard Keynes.
➤ In times of recession, increased government spend-
ing stimulates business investment and consumer pur-
chasing power through the fiscal multiplier effect.
➤ During periods of high inflation, governments
adopt a surplus budget or contractionary fiscal policy to
reduce excess demand.
➤ The main components of government budget deficits
include the fiscal deficit, revenue deficit, and pri-
mary deficit.
➤ In India, fiscal discipline targets are governed by the
YouTube Telegram 96
GENERAL AWARENESS
Fiscal Responsibility and Budget
Management (FRBM) Act, 2003.

35.question_text_en:
Q.16 Fill in the blank: The process of selling a portion of
the government's shareholding in a Public Sector
Undertaking (PSU) to private investors is called ________.
35.explanation_en:
The process by which the government dilutes or sells its
equity stake in public sector enterprises to private in-
vestors is called Disinvestment.
Important Facts:
➤ Disinvestment can be minority disinvestment, major-
ity disinvestment, or complete strategic disinvest-
ment (privatization).
➤ In India, disinvestment policy gained major momen-
tum under the New Economic Policy of 1991.
➤ The Department of Investment and Public Asset
Management (DIPAM), under the Ministry of Finance,
manages the government's investments and disinvest-
ment in PSUs.
➤ Strategic disinvestment involves transferring a major
share of government equity along with the transfer of
management control.
➤ In 1999, a separate Department of Disinvestment
was established, which was renamed DIPAM in 2016.

36.question_text_en:
Q.17 What does the term 'Financial Liberalization'
primarily refer to in the context of the 1991 reforms?

options.text_en:
Nationalizing small finance banks
YouTube Telegram 10
GENERAL AWARENESS

36.explanation_en:
In the 1991 economic reforms, financial liberalization pri-
marily meant deregulating financial markets and reduc-
ing private and foreign investment restric-
tions in banking and financial services.
Important Facts:
➤ Financial sector reforms in 1991 were initiated follow-
ing the recommendations of the Narasimham
Committee I (1991).
➤ The reforms reduced statutory reserve requirements
such as the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) and the
Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR).
➤ Interest rate structures were deregulated, allowing
commercial banks to determine deposit and lending
rates based on market forces.
➤ Private domestic banks and foreign banks were per-
mitted to establish operations and expand their presence
in India.
➤ The Securities and Exchange Board of India
(SEBI) was given statutory powers in 1992 to regulate
modern capital markets.

37.question_text_en: Q.18 What does 'License Raj' refers to?
37.explanation_en:
'License Raj' refers to the elaborate system of govern-
ment regulations, permits, and industrial licensing
required to set up and run businesses in India between
1947 and 1991.
Important Facts:
➤ The system was formalized through the Industries
(Development and Regulation) Act, 1951 and
the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956.
➤ It created bureaucratic bottlenecks, red tape, and
quotas that severely restricted private enterprise growth.
➤ Under the License Raj, government approvals were
needed not just to set up a factory, but even to expand
output or introduce new products.
➤ The system was largely dismantled with the introduc-
tion of the New Industrial Policy on 24 July
1991.
➤ The 1991 policy abolished industrial licensing for all
except a handful of strategic, hazardous, and security-
related industries.

38.question_text_en:
Q.3 Which Fundamental Right was removed by the 44th
Amendment?
38.explanation_en:
The Right to Property was removed from the list of
Fundamental Rights by the 44th Constitutional
Amendment Act, 1978.
Important Facts:
➤ Originally, the Right to Property was guaranteed as a
Fundamental Right under Article 19(1)(f) and
Article 31.
➤ Following the 44th Amendment, it was made a
legal/constitutional right under Article 300A in Part XII
of the Constitution.
➤ The 44th Amendment Act was enacted during the
tenure of the Morarji Desai-led Janata Party gov-
ernment.
14 Download App Visit Website

➤ With this deletion, the total number of Fundamental
Rights in the Indian Constitution was reduced from
seven to six.
➤ Legal rights under Article 300A lack the direct remedy
under Article 32 of the Supreme Court's writ
jurisdiction.

39.question_text_en:
Q.3 Which Article restricts discussion on the conduct of
Judges in Parliament?
39.explanation_en:
Article 121 of the Constitution of India provides that
no discussion shall take place in Parliament regarding
the conduct of any Judge of the Supreme Court or High
Court in the discharge of their duties, except upon a mo-
tion for removal.
Important Facts:
➤ A corresponding provision, Article 211, prohibits
State Legislatures from discussing the conduct of
Supreme Court and High Court judges.
19 Download App Visit Website

➤ Article 120 provides for the language to be used in
Parliament (Hindi or English).
➤ Article 122 states that courts cannot inquire into
the validity of proceedings of Parliament on grounds of
alleged irregularity of procedure.
➤ Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts can
only be removed under Article 124(4) on grounds of
proved misbehaviour or incapacity.
➤ The procedure for investigation and removal of
judges is regulated by the Judges (Inquiry) Act,
1968.

40.question_text_en: Q.4 Who administers the oath to a Judge of a High Court?
40.explanation_en:
Under Article 219 of the Constitution of India, a Judge
of a High Court takes and subscribes an oath or affirma-
tion before the Governor of the State (or someone
appointed by them).
Important Facts:
➤ High Court judges are appointed by the President
of India under Article 217.
➤ The form of oath for High Court judges is prescribed
in the Third Schedule of the Constitution.
➤ A High Court judge can hold office until attaining the
age of 62 years.
➤ Under Article 217(1)(a), a High Court judge sub-
mits their resignation in writing addressed to the
President of India.
➤ Under Article 69, the Vice President takes oath be-
fore the President; under Article 159, the Governor
takes oath before the Chief Justice of the respective
High Court.

The Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation)

the age of 14 years in hazardous occupations and pro-
cesses.

➤ Article 24 of the Indian Constitution prohibits the
employment of children below 14 years of age in facto-

➤ The Child Labour Amendment Act, 2016
completely banned employment of children below 14
years in all occupations and processes.
➤ The 2016 amendment introduced the category of
adolescent (14 to 18 years) and barred them from
hazardous occupations.
➤ Article 21A makes free and compulsory education
a fundamental right for children aged 6 to 14 years.
➤ India ratified International Labour Organization (ILO)
Conventions 138 and 182 in 2017.

42.question_text_en: Q.7 Which layer of Earth is the thickest?
42.explanation_en:
The Mantle is the thickest layer of the Earth, extending
from the base of the crust down to a depth of approxi-
mately 2,900 km.
Important Facts:
➤ The mantle makes up about 84% of the Earth's total
volume and approximately 67% of its mass.
➤ The boundary separating the crust and the mantle is
51 Download App Visit Website

known as the Mohorovičić discontinuity (Moho).
➤ The upper portion of the mantle, extending between
100 km and 400 km, is called the asthenosphere,
which is semi-fluid and drives tectonic plate movement.
➤ The boundary between the mantle and the outer core
is known as the Gutenberg discontinuity.
➤ The Earth's crust is the thinnest layer, with an aver-
age thickness of 5–30 km under oceanic and continental
plates.

43.question_text_en:
Q.5 Which of the following cotton species is not cultivated
in India?
43.explanation_en:
Gossypium tomentosum is a wild, non-commercial
species of cotton endemic to the Hawaiian Islands and is
not cultivated in India.
Important Facts:
➤ India is the only country that grows all four commer-
YouTube Telegram 16
GENERAL AWARENESS
cially cultivated species of cotton: *G. arboreum*, *G.
herbaceum*, *G. hirsutum*, and *G. barbadense*.
➤ *Gossypium arboreum* and *Gossypium herbaceum*
are diploid species known as Old World or Desi cot-
ton.
➤ *Gossypium hirsutum* (American cotton) and
*Gossypium barbadense* (Egyptian cotton) are
tetraploid New World species.
➤ *Gossypium hirsutum* accounts for the vast majority
of total cotton production in India.
➤ Cotton is primarily cultivated on nutrient-rich black
cotton soil (Regur soil), mainly in the Deccan
plateau.

44.question_text_en:
Q.11 The wings of a butterfly and a bird are examples of
which structures?

options.text_en:
Hominid features
YouTube Telegram 20
GENERAL AWARENESS

44.explanation_en:
The wings of a butterfly and a bird are analogous
structures because they perform the same function of
flight but have different embryonic origins and basic
anatomical structures.
Important Facts:
➤ Analogous structures arise as a result of conver-
gent evolution, where unrelated organisms adapt to
similar environments or ecological niches.
➤ Homologous structures share a common em-
bryonic origin and basic anatomy but perform different
functions (e.g., human arm and bat wing).
➤ Homologous organs are the result of divergent
evolution.
➤ Insect wings are non-cellular membranous folds sup-
ported by veins, whereas bird wings are modified fore-
limbs supported by bones.
➤ Vestigial organs are rudimentary structures that
have lost their ancestral function through evolution, such
as the human vermiform appendix.

45.question_text_en: Q.23 What is the advantage of placing Aditya-L1 at L1?

options.text_en: Continuous view of the Sun without eclipses

45.explanation_en:
The primary advantage of placing the Aditya-L1 satellite
in a halo orbit around the Sun-Earth Lagrange point 1
(L1) is having an uninterrupted, continuous view of
the Sun without any occultation or eclipses.
Important Facts:
➤ Aditya-L1 is India's first dedicated space mission to
study the Sun, developed and launched by ISRO.
➤ It was launched on 2 September 2023 aboard the
PSLV-C57 rocket from Sriharikota.
➤ The satellite successfully entered its halo orbit
around L1 on 6 January 2024.
➤ Lagrange Point 1 (L1) is located approximately 1.5
million kilometres away from Earth towards the Sun.
➤ The satellite carries seven scientific payloads to ob-
serve the photosphere, chromosphere, and solar corona.

46.question_text_en:
Q.8 Why is a direct numerical comparison of the AQI
between India and the USA technically complex?
46.explanation_en:
A direct comparison is complex because the National Air
Quality Index of India and the US AQI use differing
category breakpoints and mathematical formulas
for converting pollutant concentrations into index values.
Important Facts:
➤ India's National AQI considers eight pollutants:
PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NH3, and Pb.
16 Download App Visit Website

➤ The US EPA AQI monitors five major criteria pollu-
tants: ground-level ozone, PM (PM2.5 and PM10), CO,
SO2, and NO2.
➤ A concentration value of PM2.5 corresponds to differ-
ent AQI numbers and different health severity brackets
under Indian versus US standards.
➤ In India, the sub-index for PM2.5 is based on a 24-
hour average, with different thresholds for 'Good',
'Moderate', and 'Poor' categories.
➤ India's National AQI was launched in October
2014 by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB).

47.question_text_en:
Q.21 Who won the 2026 National Book Critics Circle
Award in the Autobiography category for the memoir
'Mother Mary Comes to Me'?
47.explanation_en:
Renowned Indian author Arundhati Roy won the
2026 National Book Critics Circle Award in the
Autobiography category for her memoir *Mother Mary
Comes to Me*.
Important Facts:
➤ *Mother Mary Comes to Me* is Arundhati Roy's re-
flective memoir detailing her relationship with her
mother, Mary Roy.
➤ Arundhati Roy won the prestigious Booker Prize in
1997 for her debut novel *The God of Small Things*.
➤ Her second novel, *The Ministry of Utmost
Happiness*, was published in 2017.
YouTube Telegram 24
GENERAL AWARENESS
➤ Her mother, Mary Roy, was a prominent educator
and women's rights activist who won a landmark 1986
Supreme Court case on Syrian Christian inheritance
rights.
➤ The National Book Critics Circle Awards are
prestigious annual literary awards presented in the
United States since 1975.

48.question_text_en:
Q.22 Fill in the blank: The 2025 International Booker
Prize-winning book "Heart Lamp" was translated into
English by ________.
48.explanation_en:
The collection *Heart Lamp*, authored by Kannada
writer Banu Mushtaq, was translated into English by
Deepa Bhasthi.
Important Facts:
➤ *Heart Lamp* is a collection of short stories originally
written in Kannada by lawyer and writer Banu
Mushtaq.
➤ It won the International Booker Prize 2025,
with the prize money shared equally between the author
and the translator.
➤ Deepa Bhasthi is an Indian writer, curator, and lit-
erary translator based in Kodagu, Karnataka.
➤ In 2022, Geetanjali Shree's novel *Tomb of Sand*
(translated by Daisy Rockwell) became the first Hindi
work to win the International Booker Prize.
➤ The International Booker Prize is awarded annually
for a single book of fiction translated into English and
published in the UK or Ireland.

49.question_text_en:
Q.23 Dr. Kallipatti Ramasamy Palaniswamy, who received
the Padma Bhushan, is known for his contributions in
which field?
49.explanation_en:
Dr. Kallipatti Ramasamy Palaniswamy is a veteran gas-
troenterologist who was conferred the Padma
42 Download App Visit Website

Bhushan for his distinguished services in Medicine
and Healthcare.
Important Facts:
➤ Dr. Palaniswamy is a senior consultant in gastroen-
terology and therapeutic endoscopy at Apollo Hospitals,
Chennai.
➤ He played a pioneering role in establishing the
Department of Gastroenterology at Stanley Medical
College, Chennai.
➤ He previously served as the National President of the
Indian Society of Gastroenterology.
➤ He was earlier honoured with the Padma Shri in
the field of medicine in 2007.
➤ The Padma Bhushan is India's third-highest civil-
ian award, preceded by the Bharat Ratna and Padma
Vibhushan.

50.question_text_en:
Q.10 The PM Programme for Restoration, Awareness
Generation, Nourishment, and Amelioration of Mother
Earth (PRANAM) scheme primarily incentivises states to
reduce dependence on which agricultural input?
50.explanation_en:
The PM-PRANAM scheme was launched to incentivize
States and Union Territories to promote the balanced
use of alternative fertilizers and reduce the usage of
chemical fertilisers.
Important Facts:
➤ PM-PRANAM was announced by the Union Finance
Minister in the Union Budget 2023-24.
➤ The scheme is funded through savings in fertilizer
subsidies generated by reducing chemical fertilizer con-
sumption.
➤ Under the scheme, 50% of fertilizer subsidy savings
are provided as a grant to the state that saves the
money.
➤ The scheme promotes balanced soil health by en-
couraging bio-fertilizers and organic alternatives like
nano urea.
➤ It is administered by the Department of
Fertilizers under the Ministry of Chemicals and
Fertilizers.

36.question_text_en: Q.8 What does elasticity of demand measures?

36.explanation_en:
Elasticity of demand (specifically price elasticity)
measures the responsiveness or sensitivity of
the quantity demanded of a good to a change in its
price.
Important Facts:
➤ It is calculated as the percentage change in
quantity demanded divided by the percentage
change in price.
➤ When elasticity is greater than 1, demand is termed
elastic; when less than 1, it is inelastic.
➤ If demand does not change at all with price, it is
called perfectly inelastic ($E_d = 0$).
➤ If quantity drops to zero with any price rise, it is called
perfectly elastic ($E_d = \infty$).
➤ The concept was popularized and formalized in eco-
nomics by Alfred Marshall.

(relevancy of facts forming part of the same transaction)
under the new Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam?

options.text_en: Continues with similar principles as earlier law

37.explanation_en:
The legal doctrine of res gestae (facts connected to
form part of the same transaction) has been retained un-
der Section 4 of the Bharatiya Sakshya
Adhiniyam, 2023, preserving the exact core princi-
ples previously contained in Section 6 of the Indian
Evidence Act, 1872.
Important Facts:
➤ Under the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, the doctrine
was codified under Section 6.
➤ Under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam
(BSA), 2023, it is placed in Section 4.
➤ It provides that facts which form part of the same
transaction are relevant, whether they occurred at the
same time and place or at different times and places.
➤ The BSA came into force on 1 July 2024, replacing
the colonial Indian Evidence Act.
YouTube Telegram 13
GENERAL AWARENESS
➤ Res gestae serves as a well-established exception to
the general exclusion of hearsay evidence.

38.question_text_en:
Q.17 What is the status of burden of proof under Bharatiya
Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA)?

options.text_en: It applies only in civil cases.
It is always on the accused.

It primarily lies on the prosecution but may shift in specific
circumstances.

38.explanation_en:
Under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, the initial bur-
den of proving guilt rests fundamentally on the prose-
cution beyond reasonable doubt, but the onus can
shift to the accused in specific legal circumstances
(such as special knowledge or statutory presumptions).
Important Facts:
➤ The concept of burden of proof is covered under
Part III (Chapter VIII) of the Bharatiya Sakshya
Adhiniyam, 2023.
➤ Section 104 of the BSA provides that whoever de-
sires any court to give judgment dependent on legal
rights must prove facts.
➤ When an accused relies on general exceptions of the
law, the burden of proving their existence lies on the ac-
cused.
➤ The burden of proving fact especially within the
knowledge of any person lies upon that person.
➤ The BSA replaces the Indian Evidence Act, 1872
while retaining modern evidentiary standards.

within the hindbrain, coordinates voluntary movements
and maintains posture, equilibrium, and bodily
balance.

brain".

spinal cord, and other parts of the brain to regulate mo-
tor movements.

pressure.
➤ The cerebrum (part of the forebrain) is responsible
for higher thinking, memory, emotion, and perception.
➤ Impairment of the cerebellum can lead to ataxia,
characterized by a loss of coordination.

43.question_text_en:
Q.25 What is the significance of Lagrange points in space
missions?

options.text_en: They reduce fuel needs for stable positioning

43.explanation_en:
Lagrange points are positions in space where the
gravitational forces of two large bodies balance the cen-
tripetal force required for a smaller object to move with
them, thereby drastically reducing the fuel
needed to maintain a stable position.
Important Facts:
➤ There are five Lagrange points (labeled L1
through L5) for any system of two orbiting bodies.
➤ India's Aditya-L1 solar observatory is placed in a
halo orbit around the Sun-Earth L1 point.
➤ Points L1, L2, and L3 lie on the line connecting the
two masses and are points of unstable equilibrium.
➤ The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST)
operates around the Sun-Earth L2 point.
➤ Points L4 and L5 form equilateral triangles with the
two large masses and are stable positions.

44.question_text_en:
Q.9 How is the final numerical value of India's National
AQI (NAQI) determined for a 24-hour period?

options.text_en: Sum of the top three sub-indices

44.explanation_en:
Under India's National Air Quality Index (NAQI) method-
ology, the overall AQI value for a given location is deter-
mined by the maximum (highest) sub-index
value among all evaluated criteria pollutants.
Important Facts:
➤ The NAQI monitors 8 key pollutants: $PM_{10}$,
$PM_{2.5}$, $NO_2$, $SO_2$, $CO$, $O_3$, $NH_3$,
and $Pb$.
➤ A minimum of three pollutants must be monitored, of
which one must be $PM_{10}$ or $PM_{2.5}$, to calcu-
late the AQI.
➤ The dominant pollutant responsible for the highest
sub-index is designated as the lead pollutant.
➤ The index classifies air quality into 6 distinct cate-
gories: Good, Satisfactory, Moderately Polluted, Poor,
Very Poor, and Severe.
➤ NAQI was launched in India in October 2014 un-
der the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan.

26.question_text_en:
Q.32 How many periods are there in a standard basketball
match?
26.explanation_en:
A standard basketball game consists of four periods
(quarters). Under FIBA rules, each quarter lasts for 10
minutes, while in the NBA, each quarter is 12 min-
utes.
Important Facts:
➤ Under International Basketball Federation (FIBA)
regulations, a match consists of 4 quarters of 10 minutes
each, totaling 40 minutes.
➤ In the National Basketball Association (NBA), play
consists of 4 quarters of 12 minutes each, totaling 48
minutes.
➤ If the score is tied at the end of the fourth period,
games proceed to overtime periods of 5 minutes.
➤ Basketball was invented in December 1891 by
Canadian physical education instructor Dr. James
Naismith.
➤ Each team has 5 players on the court at any given
time.

27.question_text_en:
Q.14 During which month is the Hornbill Festival
celebrated every year?
27.explanation_en:
The Hornbill Festival is celebrated every year from
1st to 10th December in Nagaland. It is famously
known as the "Festival of Festivals".
Important Facts:
➤ The Hornbill Festival is organized annually at the
Naga Heritage Village, Kisama, near Kohima.
➤ The event is organized by the State Tourism and Art
& Culture Departments of Nagaland.
➤ It was first launched in the year 2000 to encourage
inter-tribal interaction and promote cultural heritage.
➤ The festival is named after the Indian Hornbill, a
bird held in high reverence in Naga tribal folklore.
➤ December 1st also marks the Nagaland
Statehood Day, as Nagaland became the 16th state
of India on 1 December 1963.

28.question_text_en:
Q.17 Which state in India had the lowest rural sex ratio as
per the Census 2011?
28.explanation_en:
As per the Census 2011, Haryana recorded the low-
est rural sex ratio among all Indian states, with 882 fe-
males per 1,000 males in rural areas.
Important Facts:
➤ Overall sex ratio is defined as the number of females
per 1,000 males in a population.
➤ Haryana's overall sex ratio in Census 2011 was 879,
which was the lowest among all Indian states.
➤ The state with the highest overall and rural sex ratio
in India in Census 2011 was Kerala (1,084 females per
1,000 males).
➤ The national average sex ratio of India as per Census
2011 stood at 943 females per 1,000 males.
➤ The Government of India launched the Beti
Bachao Beti Padhao campaign from Panipat,
Haryana in January 2015 to address child sex ratio
decline.

29.question_text_en:
Q.9 Which of the following countries is not a member of
BIMSTEC?
29.explanation_en:
Pakistan is not a member of BIMSTEC. BIMSTEC
comprises seven nations located around the Bay of
Bengal region in South Asia and Southeast Asia.
Important Facts:
➤ BIMSTEC stands for the Bay of Bengal Initiative for
Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation.
➤ It was established on 6 June 1997 through the
Bangkok Declaration.
➤ The seven member states are Bangladesh,
Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, and Thailand.
➤ The permanent secretariat of BIMSTEC is located in
Dhaka, Bangladesh.
➤ Pakistan is a member of SAARC (South Asian
Association for Regional Cooperation), but not of
BIMSTEC.

30.question_text_en:
Q.13 In which architectural tradition is the decorative
technique of Pietra Dura mainly employed?
30.explanation_en:
Pietra Dura (Parchin Kari) is an inlay technique where
cut and fitted, highly polished semi-precious stones are
set into stone walls, prominently used in Mughal
tombs and monuments.
Important Facts:
➤ Pietra Dura reached its artistic pinnacle in India dur-
ing the reign of Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan.
➤ The technique is extensively displayed in world-fa-
mous monuments such as the Taj Mahal in Agra and
the Red Fort in Delhi.
➤ The tomb of Itimad-ud-Daulah in Agra is cele-
brated as one of the earliest Mughal structures to exten-
sively utilize Pietra Dura on white marble.
➤ The stones commonly inlaid include lapis lazuli, onyx,
jasper, turquoise, and carnelian.
➤ The technique originated in Italy during the 16th-cen-
tury Renaissance before being embraced and perfected
by Mughal artisans.

and the market together answer the questions of what to
produce, how to produce, and how to distribute?

options.text_en:

31.explanation_en:
In a mixed economy, economic decisions concerning
production and distribution are answered jointly through
both the market price mechanism and govern-
ment planning.
Important Facts:
➤ India adopted a mixed economic system after
independence, balancing public sector control with pri-
vate enterprise.
➤ In a pure capitalist economy, decisions are
driven entirely by market forces of demand and supply
with minimal government intervention.
➤ In a pure socialist (command) economy, the
central government makes all decisions regarding pro-
duction, allocation, and pricing.
➤ The concept of a mixed economy gained prominence
in the 20th century, influenced by John Maynard Keynes.
➤ Under India's Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948
and 1956, key strategic sectors were reserved for the
public sector alongside private business.

32.question_text_en:
Q.19 Under financial sector reforms 1991, the limit for
foreign investment in private sector banks is:
32.explanation_en:
Following financial sector liberalization initiated in 1991
and subsequent policy revisions, the composite ceiling
for foreign investment (FDI and FPI) in Indian private
sector banks was raised to 74 per cent.
Important Facts:
➤ Foreign investment up to 49 per cent in private
sector banks is permitted under the automatic route.
➤ Foreign investment beyond 49 per cent and up to 74
per cent is allowed under the government ap-
proval route.
➤ Financial sector reforms in India were initiated based
on the recommendations of the Narasimham
Committee I (1991).
➤ In public sector banks (PSBs), foreign investment is
capped at 20 per cent through the government ap-
proval route.
➤ Foreign investment rules ensure that at least 26 per
cent of paid-up capital in private banks remains under
resident Indian shareholding.

33.question_text_en:
Q.4 Which Article abolishes titles except military and
academic distinctions, preventing creation of hereditary
privileges and ensuring equality among citizens?
33.explanation_en:
Article 18 of the Indian Constitution abolishes all titles,
explicitly barring the State from conferring titles on any-
one, except for military and academic distinctions, to en-
sure democratic equality.
Important Facts:
➤ Article 18(1) prohibits the State from conferring
any title except military or academic distinctions.
➤ Article 18(2) prohibits citizens of India from ac-
cepting any title from any foreign State.
➤ Article 17 provides for the abolition of "untouchabil-
ity" and forbids its practice in any form.
➤ The Supreme Court in the Balaji Raghavan case
(1996) upheld the validity of National Awards (Bharat
Ratna, Padma awards), ruling they are decorations and
not titles.
➤ National awards cannot be used as prefixes or suf-
fixes to the names of the awardees.

principle of cooperative federalism through institutional
mechanisms enabling collaboration between Union and
states in policy formulation?

34.explanation_en:
The Inter-State Council, established under Article
263, serves as a dedicated constitutional institutional
mechanism fostering coordination, consultation, and co-
operative federalism between the Union and states.
Important Facts:
➤ Article 263 empowers the President to establish
an Inter-State Council to inquire into and advise upon
disputes and common policy issues.
➤ It was first established in 1990 following recommen-
dations of the Sarkaria Commission (1988).
➤ The Prime Minister acts as the Chairman of the
Inter-State Council.

Chief Ministers/Administrators of Union Territories, and
six Union Cabinet Ministers.

the Inter-State Council promotes decentralized consen-
sus-building.

35.question_text_en:
Q.9 Which situation best demonstrates legislative flexibility
of Indian federalism allowing Parliament to legislate on
State List temporarily?
35.explanation_en:
Under Article 250, during the operation of a
National Emergency (proclaimed under Article 352),
the Parliament acquires the power to make laws for the
whole or any part of India on matters enumerated in the
State List.
Important Facts:
➤ Article 352 empowers the President to proclaim a
National Emergency on grounds of war, external aggres-
sion, or armed rebellion.
➤ During a National Emergency, under Article 250,
Parliament gains overriding power to legislate on any
subject in the State List.
➤ Laws made by Parliament under Article 250 cease to
have effect six months after the proclamation of emer-
gency ceases to operate.
24 Download App Visit Website

➤ Additionally, under Article 249, the Rajya Sabha
can authorize Parliament to legislate on a State List sub-
ject in the national interest by a two-thirds majority.
➤ This unitary shift during extraordinary situations illus-
trates the organic flexibility of Indian federalism.

which matters?

options.text_en:
Revenue matters

36.explanation_en:
Article 134 of the Indian Constitution provides for the
appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court in
regard to criminal matters.
Important Facts:
➤ Under Article 134, an appeal lies to the Supreme
Court against judgments in criminal proceedings of a
High Court under specific conditions.
➤ If a High Court reverses an acquittal and sentences
an accused person to death, an appeal lies as of right.
➤ In contrast, appeals in civil matters to the
Supreme Court are governed by Article 133.
➤ Article 132 provides appellate jurisdiction in certain
cases involving constitutional interpretation.
➤ Article 136 provides discretionary power to grant
Special Leave to Appeal (SLP).

37.question_text_en:
Q.4 Why do polar regions experience extreme daylight or
darkness for extended periods during certain times of the
45 Download App Visit Website

year?
37.explanation_en:
The extreme periods of daylight and darkness in polar
regions occur due to Earth's axial tilt effect
($23.5^\circ$) relative to its orbital plane as it revolves
around the Sun.
Important Facts:
➤ Earth's rotational axis is tilted at an angle of
$23.5^\circ$ from the perpendicular to its orbital plane
(or $66.5^\circ$ to the plane).
➤ During the summer solstice in June, the North Pole
is tilted continuously toward the Sun, causing the phe-
nomenon of the Midnight Sun.
➤ Conversely, during this period, the South Pole is
tilted away from the Sun, remaining in continuous dark-
ness (polar night).
➤ The boundary lines marking continuous 24-hour day
or night are the Arctic Circle ($66.5^\circ\text{ N}$)
and Antarctic Circle ($66.5^\circ\text{ S}$).
➤ Axial tilt combined with Earth's revolution is also the
primary driver for the cycle of seasons on Earth.

38.question_text_en:
Q.8 Which of the following best describes the "Ogilvie-
Gordon" theory or the concept of "Isostasy" in
Geomorphology?

options.text_en:
The horizontal movement of tectonic plates due to mantle
convection.

The state of gravitational equilibrium between the Earth's
crust and mantle, where tectonic plates "float" at a height
dependent on their thickness and density.

The process of rock disintegration due to chemical
weathering in tropical climates.

The formation of mid-oceanic ridges through seafloor
spreading.

38.explanation_en:
Isostasy refers to the state of gravitational equi-
librium between Earth's lithosphere (crust) and as-
thenosphere (mantle), wherein tectonic blocks float at an
elevation proportional to their crustal thickness and den-
sity.
Important Facts:
➤ The term isostasy was proposed in 1889 by
American geologist Clarence Dutton.
➤ The concept is explained primarily through two classi-
cal models: the Airy hypothesis (constant density,
varying depth of roots) and the Pratt hypothesis
(varying density, uniform depth of compensation).
➤ Maria Ogilvie Gordon was a pioneering geologist
known for her groundbreaking tectonics and structural
geomorphology work in the Dolomites.
➤ Continental crust has a lower average density
($\approx 2.7\text{ g/cm}^3$) compared to oceanic crust
($\approx 3.0\text{ g/cm}^3$) and the mantle ($\approx
3.3\text{ g/cm}^3$).
➤ Isostatic rebound occurs when heavy surface loads
(such as massive ice sheets) melt, causing the de-
pressed crust to slowly rise.

Important Facts:

(temperature) and *haline* (salinity), which govern sea-
water density.
➤ Tidal energy generated by the gravitational pull
of the moon and sun provides critical mechanical
energy required for deep-ocean vertical mixing.
➤ Cold, salty water sinks in polar regions such as the
North Atlantic and spreads through the deep ocean
basins.
➤ This global overturning conveyor belt plays a pivotal

across latitudes.
➤ The complete global overturn cycle takes approxi-

40.question_text_en:
Q.2 What is the largest part of the northern plain, which is
formed of older alluvium, called?
40.explanation_en:
The largest part of the northern plains is composed of
older alluvial soil and is called Bhangar. It lies above
the floodplains of the rivers and presents a terrace-like
feature.
Important Facts:
➤ Bhangar contains calcareous deposits locally
known as kankar.
➤ Khadar refers to the newer, younger alluvial de-
posits of the floodplains that are renewed almost every
year.
➤ Bhabar is a narrow belt (8 to 16 km wide) along the
foothills of the Shiwaliks composed of pebbles where
streams disappear.
➤ Terai is a wet, swampy, and marshy tract lying south
of the Bhabar belt with thick forest cover.
➤ Alluvial soil is the most widespread soil type in India,
covering around 40% of the country's total land area.

41.question_text_en:
Q.6 Which of the following pairs of crops is correctly
matched with its cropping season in Northern States?
41.explanation_en:
Zaid is the short summer cropping season between
Rabi and Kharif (from March to June) during which crops
like vegetables, fodder crops, watermelon,
and cucumber are cultivated.
Important Facts:
➤ India has three distinct cropping seasons: Kharif,
Rabi, and Zaid.
➤ Kharif crops are sown with the onset of the mon-
soon (June–July) and harvested in autumn; examples in-
clude rice, maize, cotton, and jowar.
➤ Rabi crops are sown in winter (October–
December) and harvested in spring (April–June); exam-
ples include wheat, gram, barley, and mustard.
➤ Wheat, gram, and mustard are typical Rabi crops,
making options (a), (b), and (d) incorrectly matched.
➤ Zaid crops rely heavily on artificial irrigation during
the dry summer months before the southwest monsoon
arrives.

42.question_text_en:
Q.3 Which fundamental force of nature is responsible for
keeping planets, including Earth, in stable orbits around
the Sun in the solar system?
42.explanation_en:
Gravitational attraction is the fundamental force
that binds celestial bodies together and provides the
necessary centripetal force to keep planets in stable or-
bits around the Sun.
Important Facts:
➤ Gravitational force is mathematically described by
Sir Isaac Newton's Law of Universal
Gravitation (1687).
➤ It is formulated as $F = G \frac{m_1 m_2}{r^2}$,
where $G$ is the universal gravitational constant
($6.674 \times 10^{-11} \text{
N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{kg}^2$).
➤ Gravity is the weakest of the four fundamental forces
of nature, but it operates over infinite distances.
➤ In Albert Einstein's General Theory of
Relativity (1915), gravity is described as the curvature
of spacetime caused by mass and energy.
➤ Gravity governs orbital dynamics, tides on Earth, and
large-scale cosmic structure formation.

43.question_text_en:
Q.1 The muscular tube that connects the kidney to the
urinary bladder is called:
43.explanation_en:
The ureter is the muscular tube that transports urine
from the renal pelvis of each kidney to the urinary
bladder through peristaltic contractions.
Important Facts:
➤ The human body has two ureters, one originating
from each kidney, measuring about 25 to 30 cm in length
in adults.
➤ Urine is propelled downward along the ureter into the
bladder by waves of smooth muscle contraction called
peristalsis.
➤ The urethra is the tube that conveys urine from the
urinary bladder to the outside of the body during urina-
tion.
➤ The nephron is the structural and functional micro-
scopic filtration unit of the kidney.
➤ The renal artery carries oxygenated, unfiltered
blood from the abdominal aorta directly to the kidney.

early diagnosis and effective treatment of diseases in
healthcare systems?

options.text_en:
Improves diagnosis accuracy

ing, automated laboratory analyzers, and genomic test-
ing, fundamentally improve diagnosis accuracy

ization of internal organs.
➤ Molecular diagnostics such as PCR and next-gener-

reach.

tient mortality rates and overall disease burden.

writing.

48.question_text_en:

48.explanation_en:
According to the Brand Finance Global Soft

49.question_text_en:
Q.12 Regarding the Mission Shakti (Integrated Women
Empowerment Programme), how is the governance
structured between 'Sambhal' and 'Samarthya' sub-
schemes?

options.text_en:
'Sambhal' is for safety and security; 'Samarthya' is for
empowerment.

'Sambhal' is for urban women; 'Samarthya' is for rural
women only.

'Sambhal' handles credit linkage; 'Samarthya' handles legal
aid.

49.explanation_en:
Under Mission Shakti, the sub-scheme 'Sambhal'
is dedicated to the safety and security of women,
while the sub-scheme 'Samarthya' is dedicated to the
empowerment of women.
Important Facts:
➤ Mission Shakti was launched by the Ministry of
Women and Child Development for implementa-
tion during the 15th Finance Commission period (2021–
22 to 2025–26).
➤ 'Sambhal' components include One Stop Centres
(OSC), Women Helpline (181), Beti Bachao Beti Padhao
(BBBP), and Nari Adalats.
➤ 'Samarthya' components include Ujjawala,
Swadhar Greh, Working Women Hostels, National
60 Download App Visit Website

Creche Scheme, and Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana
Yojana (PMMVY).
➤ The 'Sambhal' sub-scheme is funded as a 100%
Central Sponsored Scheme for operational components
with direct DBT where applicable.
➤ The overarching objective is to provide a continuum
of care and support for women across their lifecycle.

50.question_text_en:
Q.13 What is the governance significance of the 'U-WIN'
Platform launched by the Ministry of Health?

options.text_en:
It tracks the status of international health insurance for
NRIs.

It is the digital registry for the Universal Immunization
Programme (UIP) to track every pregnant woman and child.

It is a portal for University students to apply for health
research grants.

It monitors the implementation of the National Health Policy
in Union Territories.

50.explanation_en:
The U-WIN portal serves as India's dedicated digital
platform designed to register and electronically track ev-
ery pregnant woman and newborn child for vac-
cination under the Universal Immunization
Programme (UIP).
Important Facts:
➤ The U-WIN platform was developed replicating the
technological architecture and success of the Co-WIN
platform used during COVID-19 vaccination.
➤ It operates under the aegis of the Ministry of
Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW).
➤ It maintains an electronic vaccination registry to elimi-
nate dropouts and track beneficiaries from birth to 16
years of age.
➤ Beneficiaries receive automated SMS alerts and
can download digital, verifiable vaccination certificates.
➤ Under UIP, India provides free vaccines against 12
life-threatening diseases nationally and sub-
nationally.

➤ The concept of 'Equal Protection of the Laws'
is borrowed from the American Constitution (14th
Amendment).
➤ Article 14 protects both citizens and non-citi-
zens (foreigners) as well as legal persons (corpora-
tions).
➤ The Supreme Court has ruled that the Rule of Law
embodied in Article 14 is a part of the basic structure
of the Constitution.
➤ Article 12 defines the term 'State', while Article 13
provides for judicial review of laws inconsistent with
Fundamental Rights.

34.question_text_en:
Q.6 Which Article abolishes untouchability and declares its
practice in any form as an offence punishable by law?
34.explanation_en:
Article 17 of the Indian Constitution abolishes un-
touchability and forbids its practice in any form, mak-
ing its enforcement a punishable offence.
Important Facts:
➤ Article 17 is an absolute right that is available
against both the State and private individuals.
➤ The term 'untouchability' is not defined in the
Constitution or in any Act of Parliament.
➤ To enforce Article 17, Parliament enacted the
Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955, renamed in
1976 as the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955.
➤ Article 16 guarantees equality of opportunity in mat-
ters of public employment.
➤ Article 18 provides for the abolition of all titles, except
military and academic distinctions.

35.question_text_en:
Q.4 The 10th Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals
with:

options.text_en: Election disputes of Members of Parliament

35.explanation_en:
The Tenth Schedule of the Indian Constitution con-
tains the legal provisions regarding the disqualifica-
tion of legislators on grounds of defection
(Anti-Defection Law).
Important Facts:
➤ The Tenth Schedule was inserted into the
Constitution by the 52nd Constitutional
Amendment Act, 1985.
➤ The decision on disqualification under the Tenth
Schedule is made by the Speaker or Chairman of
the respective House.
➤ In the landmark Kihoto Hollohan case (1992),
the Supreme Court held that the Presiding Officer's deci-
sion is subject to judicial review.
➤ The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act,
2003 omitted the provision protecting one-third split in a
political party from disqualification.
➤ Articles 102(2) (for Parliament) and 191(2) (for
State Legislatures) link membership disqualification to
the Tenth Schedule.

36.question_text_en:
Q.6 Fill in the blank: Article 133 of the Constitution deals
with appeals to the Supreme Court in
36.explanation_en:
Article 133 of the Indian Constitution provides for the
appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court in ap-
peals from High Courts in regard to civil matters (civil
adjudications).
Important Facts:
➤ Under Article 133, an appeal lies to the Supreme
Court if the High Court certifies that the case involves a
substantial question of law of general impor-
tance.
➤ Article 132 covers appellate jurisdiction of the
Supreme Court in constitutional matters.
➤ Article 134 deals with the appellate jurisdiction of
the Supreme Court in criminal matters.
➤ Article 136 provides discretionary power to the
Supreme Court to grant Special Leave to Appeal
(SLP).
➤ Part V, Chapter IV (Articles 124–147) of the
Constitution deals with the Union Judiciary (Supreme
Court).

38.question_text_en:
Q.9 What causes the variation in time zones across
different regions of the Earth based on longitudinal
differences?
38.explanation_en:
The rotation of Earth from west to east causes the
Sun to appear to move across the sky, producing a 4-
minute time difference for every 1 degree of longi-
tude.
Important Facts:
➤ The Earth rotates 360 degrees on its axis in ap-
proximately 24 hours, which equals 15 degrees per
hour or 1 degree in 4 minutes.
➤ Places located east of the Prime Meridian (0°
longitude) at Greenwich see the Sun earlier and are
ahead in time.
➤ India's standard time is based on the 82°30' E longi-
tude, which is 5 hours and 30 minutes ahead of
Greenwich Mean Time (GMT +5:30).
➤ The International Date Line roughly follows the
180° meridian; crossing it westward advances the cal-
endar by one day.
➤ Earth's revolution around the Sun, combined with
its axial tilt, is responsible for the change of seasons, not
daily time zones.

genetic traits and characteristics are passed down from
parents to their progeny.

"Father of Genetics" for his pioneering work on pea

logical differences exhibited by individuals of the same
species.
➤ Mutation is a sudden, inheritable change in the nu-
cleotide sequence of an organism's genome.

44.question_text_en:
Q.11 The "Krakatoa Mechanism" in climatology refers to
which of the following phenomena?

options.text_en:
The influence of volcanic aerosols in the stratosphere
reflecting solar radiation and causing global cooling.

The generation of tsunamis through underwater
earthquakes.
The movement of tectonic plates in the Sunda Strait.
The impact of sound waves on cloud seeding.

44.explanation_en:
The Krakatoa Mechanism refers to large explosive
volcanic eruptions injecting sulfur dioxide aerosols
into the stratosphere, which backscatter solar insolation
and cause temporary global cooling.
Important Facts:
➤ The phenomenon is named after the colossal erup-
tion of the Krakatoa (Krakatau) volcano in the
Sunda Strait, Indonesia, in August 1883.
➤ Sulfur dioxide ($SO_2$) gas injected into the strato-
sphere oxidizes to form reflective sulfate aerosol
17 Download App Visit Website

veils.
➤ Because the stratosphere lacks weather and pre-
cipitation, these aerosols can persist for 1 to 3 years.
➤ The 1883 Krakatoa eruption caused global tempera-
tures to drop by approximately 1.2°C in the subsequent
year.
➤ A similar planetary cooling effect was documented
following the eruption of Mount Pinatubo (Philippines)
in 1991.

and rural primary and secondary healthcare.

the following states?
27.explanation_en:
Kharchi Puja is a major Hindu festival celebrated in
the northeastern state of Tripura. The festival involves
the worship of the fourteen deities (Chaturdasha
Devata) over seven consecutive days.
Important Facts:

Chaturdasha Devata Temple in Old Agartala.

ing in July).
➤ The ritual marks the cleansing and purification of
Mother Earth (Ama Pechi).
➤ The chief royal priest who oversees the sacred rituals
is known as the Chantai.
➤ Although originally a royal tribal festival of the
Tripuri people, it is now celebrated across all
communities.

30.question_text_en:
Q.10 In the later phase of the Gandhara School of art,
which group of materials was primarily used for making
sculptures instead of blue-grey schist stone?
30.explanation_en:
While the early phase of the Gandhara School predomi-
nantly utilized blue-grey schist stone, its later
phase (around the 3rd to 5th centuries CE) saw wide-
spread adoption of mud, lime, and stucco (plaster)
along with clay for sculpting Buddha figures.
Important Facts:
➤ The Gandhara School of Art developed in north-
western ancient India during the rule of the Kushana
dynasty.
➤ It is famously characterized as a Greco-Buddhist
style combining Hellenistic sculptural techniques with
Buddhist themes.
➤ Stucco allowed artists greater plasticity and speed
in crafting intricate facial expressions and drapery folds.
➤ Major centres of the Gandhara school included
Taxila, Peshawar, Begram, and Hadda.
➤ Unlike Gandhara art, the contemporary Mathura
School of Art primarily utilized spotted red sandstone.

and the economic model on which they were based is
correctly matched?

on the Harrod-Domar Model, which emphasized in-
creasing the rate of savings and capital accumulation to
boost national income and agricultural growth.
Important Facts:

based on the Nehru-Mahalanobis Model, focusing
on heavy industry.
➤ The First Five-Year Plan allocated primary priority to
agriculture, irrigation, and power generation projects.
➤ Major multipurpose dam projects like Bhakra
Nangal, Hirakud, and Mettur were initiated during
the First Plan.
➤ The First Plan achieved an impressive GDP growth
rate of 3.6%, against its target of 2.1%.
➤ India adopted centralized planning inspired by the
Soviet model and established the Planning
Commission in March 1950.

33.question_text_en:
Q.1 Which constitutional feature ensures accountability of
executive through requirement that it must enjoy
confidence of lower house of legislature?
33.explanation_en:
In a Parliamentary system, the executive is drawn
directly from the legislature and remains collectively re-
sponsible to the lower house of the legislature (Lok
Sabha in India), retaining power only as long as it enjoys
its majority confidence.
Important Facts:
➤ Article 75(3) of the Indian Constitution explicitly
provides that the Council of Ministers is collectively re-
sponsible to the House of the People (Lok Sabha).
➤ A defeat in a No-Confidence Motion forces the
Prime Minister and the entire Council of Ministers to re-
sign.
➤ India borrowed the parliamentary model of gover-
nance from the British Westminster system.
➤ In a Presidential system (like the USA), the ex-
ecutive is independent of the legislature and not subject
to legislative confidence votes.
➤ The principle of collective responsibility is the
core foundational bedrock of parliamentary democracy.

➤ Article 122 prevents courts from inquiring into par-
liamentary proceedings on grounds of alleged proce-
dural irregularity.

37.question_text_en:
Q.10 Which factor primarily causes the variation of
seasons on Earth, considering the tilt and movement of
Earth relative to the Sun throughout the year?
37.explanation_en:
The primary cause of seasonal variation on Earth is the
tilt of Earth's axis (at an angle of approximately
23.5 degrees) combined with its revolution around the
Sun, which changes the angle and duration of incoming
solar insolation throughout the year.
Important Facts:
47 Download App Visit Website

➤ Earth's axis maintains a permanent axial tilt of 66.5
degrees relative to its orbital plane (and 23.5 degrees
from the perpendicular).
➤ When the Northern Hemisphere tilts towards the Sun,
it experiences summer, while the Southern
Hemisphere experiences winter.
➤ Summer Solstice occurs on June 21, when the
Sun's rays fall directly over the Tropic of Cancer.
➤ Winter Solstice occurs on December 22, when
the Sun shines directly over the Tropic of Capricorn.
➤ The slight change in the Earth-Sun distance (perihe-
lion and aphelion) plays only a minor role in seasonal
temperature differences.

38.question_text_en:
Q.11 Why does the Sun appear to rise in the east and set
in the west when observed from Earth daily?
38.explanation_en:
The apparent daily motion of the Sun rising in the east
and setting in the west is caused by the rotation of
Earth from west to east on its polar axis.
Important Facts:
➤ Earth completes one full rotation on its axis in ap-
proximately 23 hours, 56 minutes, and 4 sec-
onds (one sidereal day).
➤ Because Earth spins towards the east, celestial bod-
ies in space appear to move across the sky towards the
west.
➤ Rotation of Earth is the fundamental cause of the cy-
cle of day and night.
➤ In our solar system, Venus and Uranus rotate in a
retrograde (east-to-west) direction, opposite to Earth.
➤ The rotational speed of Earth at the equator is ap-
proximately 1,670 km/h (about 460 m/s).

drought in India.

39.explanation_en:
During a strong La Niña event, unusually cold waters in
the eastern Pacific strengthen the trade winds and drive
warm waters westward, causing enhanced convec-
tion over the Western Pacific/Indonesia, which
invigorates the ascending branch of the Walker cell and
typically strengthens the Indian monsoon.
Important Facts:
➤ La Niña represents the cold phase of the El Niño–
Southern Oscillation (ENSO) cycle.
➤ In contrast, El Niño events are associated with
warmer central/eastern Pacific waters and frequently
cause monsoon droughts in India.
➤ The Walker Circulation is a vast east-west atmo-
spheric circulation pattern along the tropical Pacific
ocean.
➤ La Niña conditions often result in above-normal rain-
fall and colder winter conditions across Northern India.
➤ The phenomenon of cooler-than-average sea surface
temperatures during La Niña leads to an elevated ther-
mocline in the eastern Pacific.

➤ The Himachal range represents the Lesser or
Middle Himalayas, lying between the Himadri and
the Shiwalik.

Q.1 Regarding the UNFCCC's "Common But
Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective
Capabilities" (CBDR-RC) principle, what is its primary
legal implication?

options.text_en:
All nations must reduce carbon emissions by the exact
same percentage by 2030.

Developed nations must take the lead in combating climate
change due to their historical contribution to GHGs and
greater financial resources.

Developing nations are exempted from all environmental

developed nations must take the lead in mitiga-

➤ Under the Kyoto Protocol (1997), binding emis-
sion reduction targets were imposed exclusively on de-
veloped (Annex I) countries.
➤ The 2015 Paris Agreement reaffirmed CBDR-RC
while introducing nationally determined contributions
(NDCs) for all nations.

Answer: 52 apples

26.question_text_en: Q.41 What is the standard shape of a basketball?
26.explanation_en:
A basketball is a three-dimensional object manufactured
strictly in a spherical geometry to ensure uniform
bounce, roll, and aerodynamic balance.

cumference of 29.5 inches (75 cm) for men's profes-
sional play (Size 7).
➤ Basketball was invented in December 1891 by
Canadian physical educator Dr. James Naismith in
Springfield, Massachusetts.
➤ The global governing body for the sport of basketball
is FIBA (International Basketball Federation), founded
in 1932.
➤ Basketball was introduced as an official men's
Olympic medal sport at the 1936 Berlin Olympics.
➤ The standard height of the rim (hoop) above the court
floor is exactly 10 feet (3.05 metres).

28.question_text_en:
Q.21 From 2001 to 2011, what was the decline in India's
average annual growth rate of population?
28.explanation_en:
India's average annual exponential population growth
rate dropped from 1.97% during 1991–2001 to 1.64%
during 2001–2011, reflecting a decline of 0.32% (or
~0.33 percentage points).
Important Facts:
➤ The decadal growth rate of India's population during
2001–2011 was 17.7%, down from 21.5% in 1991–
2001.
➤ According to the Census 2011, India's total popula-
tion stood at approximately 1.21 billion (121.08
crore).
➤ Nagaland was the only Indian state to record a
negative population growth rate (−0.58%) during the
2001–2011 decade.
➤ Meghalaya registered the highest decadal popula-
tion growth rate among Indian states at 27.95%.
➤ The year 1921 is termed the 'Year of the Great
Divide' in Indian demographic history because popula-
tion growth turned permanently positive thereafter.

29.question_text_en:
Q.15 St. Philomena's Church in Mysore is an example of
which architectural style?
29.explanation_en:
St. Philomena's Cathedral in Mysuru (Mysore),
Karnataka, is built in the Neo-Gothic architectural
style, inspired by the Cologne Cathedral in Germany.
Important Facts:
➤ Constructed in 1936, the church was designed by a
French architect named Daly during the reign of
Maharaja Krishnaraja Wadiyar IV.
➤ The cathedral features towering twin spires that rise
to a height of 175 feet (53 metres).
➤ Its twin spires and stained-glass windows depicting
events from the life of Christ are classic hallmarks of
Gothic Revival (Neo-Gothic) architecture.
➤ The church was erected in honour of Saint
Philomena, a 4th-century Greek saint and martyr.
➤ Krishnaraja Wadiyar IV laid the foundation stone of
the present cathedral structure in October 1933.

30.question_text_en:
Q.10 Which of the Five-Year Plan had a target growth rate
of 5.2% and an actual growth rate of 5.7%?
30.explanation_en:
The Sixth Five-Year Plan (1980–1985) targeted a
GDP growth rate of 5.2% and successfully achieved an
actual growth rate of 5.7% (or 5.66%).
Important Facts:
➤ The Sixth Five-Year Plan marked the beginning
of economic liberalisation in India, focusing on poverty
eradication (Garibi Hatao) and technological self-re-
liance.
➤ Key rural development initiatives such as the
Integrated Rural Development Programme
(IRDP) and NREP were expanded during this plan.
➤ NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural
Development) was established on 12 July 1982 dur-
ing the Sixth Plan.
➤ The EXIM Bank of India was also set up in 1982
under this plan to boost foreign trade.
➤ India's Five-Year Plans were formulated by the
Planning Commission, which was replaced by NITI
Aayog on 1 January 2015.

32.explanation_en:
The Right to Freedom of Religion is guaranteed
as a Fundamental Right under Articles 25 to 28 in
Part III of the Constitution of India.

➤ Article 25 guarantees freedom of conscience and
free profession, practice, and propagation of religion.
➤ Article 26 grants the freedom to manage religious

taxes for the promotion of any particular religion.
➤ Article 28 guarantees freedom regarding atten-
dance at religious instruction or worship in certain edu-
cational institutions.
➤ The word 'Secular' was explicitly inserted into the
Preamble of the Indian Constitution by the 42nd
Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976.

orbit around the Sun without the planet drifting away into
space?

options.text_en:

YouTube Telegram 18

39.explanation_en:
The Sun's gravitational force exerts a continuous
centripetal pull on Earth, balancing its orbital velocity and
holding it in an elliptical orbit.
Important Facts:
➤ According to Newton's Universal Law of
Gravitation, gravitational attraction is directly propor-
tional to the product of masses and inversely propor-
tional to the square of the distance.
➤ Earth orbits the Sun at an average distance of ap-
proximately 149.6 million kilometres (1
Astronomical Unit).
➤ The elliptical shape of planetary orbits is described by
Kepler's First Law of Planetary Motion.
➤ Earth travels along its orbit around the Sun with an
average orbital speed of about 29.78 km/s.
➤ Without gravitational force acting as a centripetal
force, Earth would fly off in a straight line tangentially
into space.

40.question_text_en:
Q.5 Which phenomenon explains the bending of light as it
passes through Earth's atmosphere, affecting how
celestial objects appear?
40.explanation_en:
Atmospheric refraction is the bending of light rays
as they pass through atmospheric layers of varying opti-
cal density, making celestial objects appear slightly
higher than their true positions.
Important Facts:
➤ Atmospheric refraction causes the Sun to appear visi-
ble about 2 minutes before actual sunrise and 2
minutes after actual sunset.
➤ The apparent twinkling of stars at night is also
caused by continuous fluctuations in atmospheric refrac-
tion.
➤ Refraction occurs because the speed of light
changes when passing between media of different re-
fractive indices.
➤ Snell's Law quantitatively describes the relationship
between angles of incidence and refraction: n₁ sin θ₁ =
n₂ sin θ₂.
➤ Celestial objects near the horizon suffer the highest
degree of atmospheric refraction compared to those at
the zenith.

discovery of a new species of burrowing reed snake?
41.explanation_en:
Herpetologists discovered a new species of burrowing
snake in Meghalaya's West Garo Hills district, high-
lighting the exceptional and hidden squamate biodiver-
sity of the Garo Hills.
Important Facts:
➤ The Garo Hills form the western portion of the
Meghalaya plateau and are renowned for dense tropical
wet evergreen and semi-evergreen forests.
➤ The region is home to the Nokrek Biosphere
Reserve, located primarily in the East and West Garo
Hills.
➤ Burrowing reed snakes possess specialized morpho-
logical adaptations for fossorial (underground burrowing)
lifestyles in moist leaf litter and loose soil.
➤ The state of Meghalaya is part of the Indo-Burma
biodiversity hotspot, one of the richest biodiversity
regions in the world.
➤ Tura is the largest town and administrative headquar-
ters of the West Garo Hills district.

42.question_text_en:
Q.13 Who is known for discovering the basic rules of
inheritance through experiments on pea plants?
42.explanation_en:
Gregor Johann Mendel discovered the fundamental
laws of inheritance through systematic hybridization ex-
periments on garden pea plants (*Pisum sativum*), earn-
ing him the title 'Father of Genetics'.
Important Facts:
➤ Mendel formulated the Law of Segregation, the
Law of Independent Assortment, and the Law
of Dominance.
➤ He conducted his pea plant experiments at St.
Thomas's Abbey in Brno between 1856 and 1863.
➤ Mendel published his groundbreaking work titled
*Experiments on Plant Hybridization* in 1866.
➤ His laws were independently rediscovered in 1900
by Hugo de Vries, Carl Correns, and Erich von
Tschermak.
➤ Charles Darwin authored *On the Origin of
Species* (1859), proposing the theory of evolution by
natural selection.

43.question_text_en:
Q.32 What is the importance of using satellite technology
in monitoring climate change and environmental
degradation globally?
43.explanation_en:
Earth observation satellites provide global observa-
tion, enabling continuous, wide-scale synoptic monitor-
ing of global climate variables, deforestation, and atmo-
spheric dynamics.
Important Facts:
➤ Earth observation satellites capture critical planetary
parameters such as sea-surface temperatures, ice-sheet
12 Download App Visit Website

melt rates, and greenhouse gas concentrations.
➤ Remote sensing enables consistent monitoring of re-
mote regions like the polar ice caps and the deep
Amazon rainforest.
➤ India's ISRO operates dedicated remote sensing
constellations including the Cartosat, Resourcesat,
and Oceansat series.
➤ The Copernicus Programme operated by the
European Union is the world's largest earth observation
programme.
➤ Satellites operate in diverse orbits such as Low Earth
Orbit (LEO) for high-resolution imaging and
Geostationary Orbit (GEO) for meteorological tracking.

44.question_text_en:
Q.12 Regarding the "Great Acceleration" in the context of
the Anthropocene, which indicator showed the most
dramatic surge post-1950?

options.text_en: Total forest cover in the Northern Hemisphere.

Global primary energy use and atmospheric Carbon Dioxide
concentration.
Deep-sea biodiversity in the Arctic Ocean.
The rate of volcanic eruptions along the Ring of Fire.

44.explanation_en:
The "Great Acceleration" post-1950 is charac-
terised by steep upward curves in human socio-eco-
nomic activity, especially global primary energy
use and atmospheric CO₂ concentrations.
Important Facts:
➤ The concept of the 'Great Acceleration' was popular-
ized by chemist Paul Crutzen and historian J.R.
McNeill.
➤ Atmospheric CO₂ levels rose sharply from roughly
310 ppm in 1950 to over 420 ppm in recent years.
➤ The Anthropocene is proposed as a distinct geologi-
cal epoch marking humanity's dominant impact on
Earth's ecosystems.
➤ Post-1950 trends also exhibit exponential increases
in world population, dam constructions, water usage,
and fertilizer consumption.
➤ The global energy surge after the Second World War
was driven overwhelmingly by fossil fuels: coal, oil, and
natural gas.

able energy-based power plants of individual

(MNRE).

tariffs.
