26.question_text_en:
Q.18 Which of the following pair (regarding Indian
Festivals) is correctly matched?
26.explanation_en:
Chapchar Kut is an agricultural festival celebrated in
Mizoram marking the completion of clearing bamboo
forests for jhum cultivation. Hornbill is held in
Nagaland, Losar is celebrated in Himalayan regions
(such as Ladakh and Arunachal Pradesh), and
Pongal is celebrated in Tamil Nadu.
Important Facts:
➤ Chapchar Kut is celebrated during March after
clearing the jungle for shifting cultivation (jhum).
➤ The traditional bamboo dance Cheraw is a promi-
nent highlight of the Chapchar Kut festival.
➤ Hornbill Festival is celebrated annually from 1 to
10 December in Nagaland (Kisama heritage village).
➤ Losar marks the traditional Tibetan and Buddhist
New Year celebrated in Ladakh, Sikkim, and Arunachal
Pradesh.
➤ Pongal is a multi-day harvest festival dedicated to
the Sun god, celebrated widely across Tamil Nadu.

27.question_text_en:
Q.19 Which Sikh festival is celebrated annually in Muktsar
to honour the memory of the 'Chalis Mukte' (forty Sikh
martyrs) who died fighting against the Mughal emperor
Wazir Khan?
27.explanation_en:
The festival of Maghi (celebrated on the first day of the
Punjabi month of Magh) is held as Mela Maghi at
Muktsar Sahib to commemorate the bravery of the
Chalis Mukte (Forty Liberated Ones) who laid down
their lives in the Battle of Muktsar (1705).
Important Facts:
➤ The Battle of Khidrana (Muktsar) was fought in
1705 between the Mughal forces under Wazir Khan and
Guru Gobind Singh Ji.
➤ The forty Sikh soldiers who sacrificed their lives were
blessed by Guru Gobind Singh Ji as the Chalis Mukte
(Forty Liberated Ones).
➤ Following their sacrifice, the town of Khidrana was re-
named Sri Muktsar Sahib.
➤ Mai Bhago, a revered Sikh heroine, rallied and led
these forty warriors into the battlefield.
➤ The annual fair, Mela Maghi, is held on the day of
Makar Sankranti / Maghi at Sri Muktsar Sahib in Punjab.

28.question_text_en:
Q.13 As of 2024, which BRICS country is the largest by
geographical area?
28.explanation_en:
Russia is the largest country in the world and among all
BRICS nations by total geographic landmass, spanning
an immense territory of over 17.1 million square
kilometres across Eastern Europe and Northern Asia.
Important Facts:
➤ Russia possesses a total surface area of approxi-
mately 17,098,242 sq km, making it the world's and
BRICS' largest nation by area.
➤ The five founding/early BRICS nations ranked by
land area are Russia, followed by China, Brazil,
India, and South Africa.
➤ The acronym BRIC was coined in 2001 by British
economist Jim O'Neill.
➤ South Africa officially joined the association in 2010,
transforming the bloc into BRICS.
➤ The BRICS group expanded at the beginning of 2024
to include new members like Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, and
the UAE.

29.question_text_en: Q.7 PM Jan Dhan Yojana primarily aims at:
29.explanation_en:
Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) is a
national mission for comprehensive financial inclu-
sion, launched to ensure that every household across
India has access to basic banking services, savings ac-
counts, credit, remittance, and insurance.
Important Facts:
➤ PMJDY was launched by Prime Minister Narendra
Modi on 28 August 2014 with the slogan *"Mera
Khata, Bhagya Vidhata"*.
➤ The scheme provides basic savings bank deposit
(BSBD) zero-balance accounts to unbanked individuals.
➤ Beneficiaries receive a RuPay debit card with
built-in accidental insurance cover.
➤ An overdraft (OD) facility of up to Rs10,000 is
available to eligible account holders.
➤ PMJDY serves as the foundational pillar for the JAM
(Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile) Trinity enabling di-
rect benefit transfers (DBT).

30.question_text_en:
Q.16 The presence of a stepped water tank known as a
'surya-kund' with miniature temples carved on its steps is
a unique architectural feature of which temple style?
30.explanation_en:
The stepped water tank called Surya-kund, lined with
numerous miniature shrines along its terraces and steps,
is the hallmark of the Solanki (Maru-Gurjara)
School of architecture, famously seen at the Sun
Temple in Modhera, Gujarat.
Important Facts:
➤ The Sun Temple at Modhera was built in 1026
CE during the reign of King Bhimdev I of the Solanki
dynasty.
➤ The temple complex consists of three main compo-
nents: the sanctum (Gudhamandapa), the assembly
hall (Sabhamandapa), and the stepped reservoir
(Surya-kund).
➤ The Surya-kund contains 108 miniature shrines
dedicated to various deities carved along the stepped
terraces.
➤ The Solanki school belongs to the western Indian
branch of the Nagara architectural order.
➤ The sanctum was designed so that the first rays of
the rising sun fell directly on the deity during equinoxes.

31.question_text_en:
Q.2 Which three kingdoms emerged in the southern
regions of the Subcontinent around 400 BCE?
31.explanation_en:
In ancient South India (Tamilakam), the three prominent
early ruling lineages known as the Muventhar (Three
Crowned Kings) were the Cholas, Cheras, and
Pandyas. They emerged during the late Megalithic /
early Sangam period.
Important Facts:
➤ The Sangam literature collectively refers to the
Cholas, Cheras, and Pandyas as the Muventhar
(three crowned kings).
➤ The Cheras ruled over Kerala and western Tamil
Nadu, with their main port at Muziris and capital at
Vanji/Karur.
➤ The Cholas controlled the Kaveri delta and northern
Tamil Nadu, with their capital at Uraiyur and port at
67 Download App Visit Website

Puhar (Kaveripattinam).
➤ The Pandyas ruled over southern Tamil Nadu, with
their ancient capital at Madurai and port at Korkai.
➤ Ashoka's Major Rock Edict II (3rd century BCE) men-
tions the Cholas, Pandyas, Satiyaputras, and
Keralaputras as border states in the south.

32.question_text_en:
Q.6 Which of the following was first introduced under the
Act of 1892?
32.explanation_en:
The Indian Councils Act 1892 enlarged the legisla-
tive councils and gave members the power to discuss
the annual financial statement (budget) and ask
83 Download App Visit Website

questions on domestic matters. Direct elections were in-
troduced in 1919, while bicameralism at the Centre
came under the Government of India Act 1919.
Important Facts:
➤ Under the Indian Councils Act 1892, members
of the legislative councils were allowed to discuss the
budget, though they could not vote on it.
➤ Members were granted the right to address questions
to the executive on matters of public interest with prior
notice.
➤ The Act introduced an indirect system of
election/recommendation through bodies like universi-
ties, district boards, and municipalities.
➤ Direct elections and bicameralism at the central
level were introduced under the Government of
India Act 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms).
➤ Provincial autonomy and responsible ministries in
provinces were established under the Government of
India Act 1935.

33.question_text_en:
Q.7 Which of the following initiatives was explicitly
emphasised by Wood's Despatch of 1854?
33.explanation_en:
Wood's Despatch of 1854, referred to as the
'Magna Carta of English Education in India', placed
strong emphasis on female education, vernacular el-
ementary education, and secular schooling. It also rec-
ommended setting up universities in Calcutta, Bombay,
and Madras.
Important Facts:
➤ Sir Charles Wood, President of the Board of
Control, sent this educational despatch to the Governor-
General Lord Dalhousie in 1854.
➤ It advocated secular education in government-aided
institutions and strongly supported the promotion of
female education.
➤ It recommended the establishment of Universities in
Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras, which were es-
tablished in 1857.
➤ It introduced the Grants-in-Aid system to foster pri-
vate enterprise and voluntary efforts in education.
YouTube Telegram 84
GENERAL AWARENESS
➤ It recommended vernacular languages as the
medium of instruction at primary levels and English for
higher education.

34.question_text_en: Q.9 The objective of price control policies was:
34.explanation_en:
Price control policies (such as ceiling prices or ad-
ministered price mechanisms) are implemented by gov-
ernments primarily to stabilize the market, curb unrea-
sonable price spikes, and prevent inflation on essen-
tial goods and services.
Important Facts:
➤ A price ceiling sets a maximum legal price at
which a good or service can be sold to keep essentials
affordable for consumers.
➤ Government intervention through administered pric-
ing prevents hoarding, speculative price surges, and gal-
loping inflation.
➤ In India, the Essential Commodities Act, 1955
empowers authorities to regulate the supply, distribution,
and pricing of essential commodities.
➤ The Minimum Support Price (MSP) acts as a price
floor designed to protect farmers from sharp declines in
agricultural market prices.
➤ While price ceilings curb inflation, if set below equilib-
rium they can lead to excess demand and shortages in
the open market.

35.question_text_en:
Q.24 The sector that benefited most from LPG
(Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation) reforms is:
35.explanation_en:
The New Economic Policy of 1991 (LPG reforms)
opened up trade and private investment, which mas-
sively propelled India's services sector—particularly
IT, telecommunications, banking, business processing,
and financial services—to become the leading driver of
GDP growth.
Important Facts:
➤ India introduced LPG reforms in 1991 under
Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao and Finance
Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh.
➤ The services sector (tertiary sector) registered
the highest sustained double-digit growth rates following
these structural reforms.
➤ Information Technology (IT) and Business Process
Management (BPM) emerged as the primary engines of
Indian software exports.
➤ Foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows surged pre-
dominantly into service sub-sectors, including software,
telecommunications, and financial services.
➤ Today, the services sector contributes over 50% of
India's Gross Value Added (GVA).

36.question_text_en:
Q.9 In which Articles of the Indian Constitution is the Right
to Equality given?
YouTube Telegram 11
GENERAL AWARENESS
36.explanation_en:
The Right to Equality is enshrined in Articles 14
to 18 under Part III of the Constitution of India, guaran-
teeing equality before the law and prohibiting discrimina-
tion on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of
birth.
Important Facts:
➤ Article 14 guarantees equality before the law and
equal protection of the laws within India.
➤ Article 15 prohibits discrimination on grounds only
of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
➤ Article 16 ensures equality of opportunity in mat-
ters of public employment.
➤ Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids
its practice in any form.
➤ Article 18 provides for the abolition of titles, except
military and academic distinctions.

37.question_text_en:
Q.7 Which Chief Justice of India was known for heading
the bench that upheld the abrogation of Article 370 (recent
constitutional developments)?
37.explanation_en:
In December 2023, a five-judge Constitution Bench
headed by Chief Justice of India Justice D.Y.
Chandrachud unanimously upheld the validity of the
Government of India's decision to abrogate Article
370 of the Indian Constitution.
Important Facts:
➤ The five-judge Constitution bench was led by the
50th Chief Justice of India, Justice D.Y.
Chandrachud.
➤ The Supreme Court ruled that Article 370 was a
temporary provision introduced in the Constitution.
➤ The verdict held that the State of Jammu and
Kashmir did not retain sovereign status after signing the
Instrument of Accession.
➤ The Court directed the Election Commission of India
to conduct legislative assembly elections in Jammu and
Kashmir.
➤ Article 370 of the Constitution had originally granted
special autonomous status to Jammu and Kashmir
within the Indian Union.

38.question_text_en:
Q.8 The final authority to interpret the Constitution rests
with:
38.explanation_en:
The Supreme Court of India is the ultimate
guardian, protector, and final interpreter of the
Constitution of India. Its interpretation of any consti-
tutional provision is binding on all courts and authorities
throughout the territory of India under Article 141.
Important Facts:
➤ Article 141 of the Constitution states that the law
declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all
courts within the territory of India.
YouTube Telegram 13
GENERAL AWARENESS
➤ Article 132 and 133 provide appellate jurisdiction
to the Supreme Court in constitutional cases involving
substantial questions of law.
➤ The Supreme Court has the power of Judicial
Review to strike down any legislative enactment or ex-
ecutive action violating the Constitution.
➤ In the landmark Kesavananda Bharati case
(1973), the Supreme Court enunciated the Basic
Structure doctrine, limiting Parliament's amending
powers.
➤ The Supreme Court of India was established on 26
January 1950, succeeding the Federal Court of India.

39.question_text_en:
Q.12 Which factor is responsible for the apparent shift of
constellations visible in the night sky over different
seasons of the year?

options.text_en:
Moon's phases
YouTube Telegram 14
GENERAL AWARENESS

39.explanation_en:
As the Earth undergoes revolution around the Sun
along its orbit, the night side of the Earth faces in differ-
ent directions in space over the course of a year.
Consequently, different constellations appear visible dur-
ing different seasons.
Important Facts:
➤ Earth's revolution takes approximately 365.25
days to complete one orbit around the Sun.
➤ The daily rising and setting of stars across the sky
from east to west is caused by Earth's rotation on its
axis.
➤ The seasonal variation of constellations visible at
midnight occurs because the Earth's night face looks out
toward different celestial coordinates as it revolves.
➤ Constellations visible only at particular times of the
year are termed seasonal constellations (e.g.,
Orion in winter, Scorpius in summer).
➤ Constellations located close to celestial poles that re-
main visible year-round from high latitudes are known as
circumpolar constellations.

40.question_text_en: Q.4 Avalanches are most likely to occur when?

options.text_en: The snow begins to melt rapidly on slopes
The glaciers slowly move downhill over time
The rivers overflow due to seasonal rainfall
The rocks erode gradually along riverbanks

40.explanation_en:
An avalanche occurs when a mass of snow, ice, and
debris suddenly detaches and slides rapidly down a
mountain slope. Rapid warming or melting weakens the
structural bond between snow layers and lubricates the
surface underneath, triggering sudden slides.
Important Facts:
➤ Avalanches are rapid downward movements of
snowpacks triggered on steep slopes, generally between
30° and 45°.
➤ Sudden rises in temperature or rapid snowmelt
destabilize the cohesive forces within the snowpack.
➤ The presence of weak structural layers, such as hoar-
frost or loose granular snow beneath fresh heavy snow,
increases avalanche risk.
➤ High wind speeds and seismic tremors are other nat-
ural factors contributing to avalanche initiation.
➤ In India, snow avalanches frequently occur in high-al-
titude Himalayan regions of Jammu & Kashmir, Ladakh,
Himachal Pradesh, and Uttarakhand.

41.question_text_en:
Q.3 Which state/UT is home to the 'Jarawa' and
'Sentinelese' tribal groups?
41.explanation_en:
The Jarawa and Sentinelese are indigenous hunter-
gatherer communities residing in the Andaman and
Nicobar Islands. They are classified as Particularly
Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) of Negrito heritage.
Important Facts:
➤ The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are home
to six indigenous tribes: Great Andamanese, Onge,
Jarawa, Sentinelese, Shompen, and Nicobarese.
➤ The Sentinelese inhabit North Sentinel Island and
remain largely isolated from modern civilization.
➤ The Jarawa inhabit parts of South Andaman and
Middle Andaman islands.
➤ Great Andamanese, Onge, Jarawa, Sentinelese, and
Shompen are officially recognized as Particularly
Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs).
➤ The Ministry of Tribal Affairs recognizes 75 PVTGs
across 18 states and the Union Territory of Andaman
and Nicobar Islands.

42.question_text_en:
Q.12 Any land left uncultivated for a period of more than
five years is classified as:
YouTube Telegram 16
GENERAL AWARENESS
42.explanation_en:
According to land-use classification in India, land that is
available for cultivation but has been left uncultivated for
more than five successive years is termed as
Culturable Wasteland. It can be brought under culti-
vation through reclamation efforts.
Important Facts:
➤ Current Fallow represents land that is left unculti-
vated for one agricultural year or less.
➤ Fallow other than current fallow refers to
cropland left uncultivated for between one and five
years.
➤ Culturable Wasteland includes land lying fallow
for more than five consecutive years, which can
be cultivated after reclamation.
➤ Barren and Unculturable Land includes land
that cannot be cultivated with available technology (e.g.,
steep mountains, deserts, rocky outcrops).
➤ Land use statistics in India are systematically com-
piled by the Directorate of Economics and Statistics un-
der nine standard categories.

43.question_text_en:
Q.13 The gradual reduction of water flow from 18-20 litres
to 20-80 drops per minute mainly indicates:

options.text_en: Deliberate regulation for efficient irrigation of plants
Leakage due to weak bamboo joints

43.explanation_en:
In traditional bamboo drip irrigation systems
(practiced widely in Meghalaya), hillside stream water
(18–20 litres/min) is diverted through bamboo pipes and
regulated step-by-step so that it trickles at 20–80
drops per minute directly at the roots of plants for
water efficiency.
Important Facts:
➤ The bamboo drip irrigation system is an in-
digenous traditional water harvesting technique exten-
sively practiced in Meghalaya.
➤ In this method, 18–20 litres of water entering the
bamboo channel system per minute is gradually reduced
67 Download App Visit Website

to 20–80 drops per minute at the plant site.
➤ It is ideally used to irrigate black pepper and betel
leaf plantations along steep, terraced hill slopes.
➤ The system channels spring water across hundreds
of metres using interconnected, perforated bamboo
pipes without using pumps.
➤ The reduction in discharge is intentionally regulated
through pipe diameters and slope positioning to prevent
soil erosion and water wastage.

44.question_text_en:
Q.9 If India fails to provide education and employment to
its growing working-age population, what will happen to
the demographic dividend?

options.text_en: It will convert into a demographic burden.
It will reduce the dependency ratio further.

44.explanation_en:
A demographic dividend yields economic prosperity only
when the working-age population is educated, skilled,
and gainfully employed. Without adequate schooling,
health, and jobs, high numbers of unemployed youth
turn the potential dividend into a demographic bur-
den / disaster.
Important Facts:
➤ The demographic dividend refers to the eco-
nomic growth potential resulting from shifts in a
population’s age structure, specifically when the work-
ing-age share is larger.
➤ The working-age population is universally defined as
individuals aged 15 to 64 years (or 15–59 years).
➤ The dependency ratio measures the proportion of
dependents (children and elderly) relative to the working-
age population.
➤ Failure to generate productive jobs leads to youth un-
deremployment, social instability, and increased fiscal
pressure on public finances.
➤ India's demographic window of opportunity opened
around 2005-06 and is projected to last until roughly the
mid-2050s.

45.question_text_en:
Q.5 Which species was the focus of the first complete
mitochondrial genome analysis in India?
45.explanation_en:
Researchers in India successfully sequenced and ana-
lyzed the complete mitochondrial genome (mi-

46.question_text_en:
Q.6 Which taxonomic category is used for plants instead
of 'Phylum' used for animals?
46.explanation_en:
In biological classification, while animals are grouped
into different Phyla (singular: Phylum) below the
Kingdom level, plants and fungi are historically orga-
nized into equivalent taxonomic categories known as
Divisions.
Important Facts:
➤ The hierarchical taxonomic levels from highest to low-
est are: Kingdom → Phylum/Division → Class →
Order → Family → Genus → Species.
➤ The International Code of Nomenclature for algae,
fungi, and plants (ICN) permits the use of Division syn-
onymously with Phylum.
➤ Plant division names typically end with the standard
suffix -phyta (e.g., Bryophyta, Pteridophyta,
Magnoliophyta).
➤ Carl Linnaeus laid the foundation of modern bio-
logical taxonomy and the binomial nomenclature system
in his work *Systema Naturae*.
➤ Species is the basic and lowest fundamental unit of
biological classification.

for children aged 6 to 14 a Fundamental Right (added by

The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976

Constitution, adding 10 Fundamental Duties based

34.question_text_en:
Q.9 Fill in the blank: An appeal under Article 133 lies from
________ to the Supreme Court.
34.explanation_en:
Under Article 133 of the Constitution of India, an ap-
pellate jurisdiction lies to the Supreme Court from any
judgment, decree, or final order of a High Court in civil
proceedings, provided the High Court certifies it involves
a substantial question of law of general importance.
Important Facts:
➤ Article 132 provides for appellate jurisdiction of the
Supreme Court in constitutional cases.
➤ Article 133 specifically deals with the appellate ju-
risdiction of the Supreme Court in civil matters.
➤ Article 134 governs the appellate jurisdiction of the
Supreme Court in criminal matters.
➤ Article 136 provides for Special Leave to
Appeal (SLP) granted at the discretion of the Supreme
Court.
➤ The Supreme Court of India was officially established
on 28 January 1950.

36.question_text_en:
Q.13 What is the correct scientific explanation for the
occurrence of solar and lunar eclipses based on the
alignment of celestial bodies?
36.explanation_en:
Eclipses occur when the Sun, Earth, and Moon
align in a straight line (known as syzygy). A solar
eclipse happens when the Moon comes between the
Sun and Earth, while a lunar eclipse occurs when the
Earth comes between the Sun and Moon, casting shad-
ows.
Important Facts:
➤ The straight-line configuration of three celestial bod-
ies in a gravitational system is termed syzygy.
➤ A solar eclipse occurs on a New Moon day
(Amavasya).
➤ A lunar eclipse occurs on a Full Moon night
(Purnima).
48 Download App Visit Website

➤ The darker central part of the shadow during an
eclipse is called the umbra, and the lighter outer part is
the penumbra.
➤ Eclipses do not occur every month because the
Moon's orbit is tilted by about 5 degrees relative to
Earth's orbital plane.

37.question_text_en:
Q.14 Which movement of the Earth is responsible for the
occurrence of one complete year and influences seasonal
cycles globally?
37.explanation_en:
The revolution of the Earth around the Sun in
an elliptical orbit takes approximately 365.25 days,
defining one calendar year. Along with the Earth's tilted
axis of 23.5 degrees, revolution is directly responsible for
the cycle of seasons.
Important Facts:
➤ Earth takes 365 days, 5 hours, 48 minutes,
and 46 seconds to complete one revolution.
➤ The rotation of the Earth on its axis causes day and
night and takes approximately 24 hours.
➤ Earth's axis of rotation is tilted at an angle of 66.5
degrees to its orbital plane (or 23.5 degrees from
the perpendicular).
➤ Perihelion is the point when Earth is closest to the
Sun (around January 3).
➤ Aphelion is the point when Earth is farthest from
the Sun (around July 4).

38.question_text_en:
Q.1 What is the main type of rock found in the Deccan
Trap region?
38.explanation_en:
The Deccan Trap is composed predominantly of
basaltic igneous rocks formed by volcanic fissure
eruptions during the late Cretaceous period. Weathering
of these igneous rocks led to the formation of fertile
black cotton soil (Regur).
Important Facts:
➤ The Deccan volcanic province was formed around
65–66 million years ago.
➤ Basalt is an extrusive (volcanic) igneous rock rich in
iron and magnesium.
➤ The Deccan Trap covers major parts of
Maharashtra, Gujarat, and Madhya Pradesh.
➤ Weathering of Deccan basalt generates black soil,
exceptionally suited for cotton cultivation.
➤ The step-like landscape feature of horizontal lava
flows gives it the Scandinavian name "Trap", meaning
stairs.

agricultural fields rather than clustered together.

terrains like the Himalayas, Meghalaya, and parts of
Kerala.

fertile alluvial plains.

transport corridors such as roads, railway lines, rivers, or
canals.

quirements encourage the dispersion of dwellings.
➤ Semi-clustered settlements result from the
segregation or fragmentation of a large compact village.

high-voltage electrical equipment?

Its availability in multiple colours and textures
Its concentration in plateau regions of India

40.explanation_en:
Mica possesses an exceptional combination of high di-
electric strength, low power loss factor, and superb
insulating properties, making it an indispensable insulat-
ing material in high-voltage electrical apparatus.
Important Facts:
➤ Mica can withstand very high temperatures without
undergoing chemical decomposition.
➤ The major varieties of mica are muscovite
(white/potash mica) and phlogopite (magnesium
mica).
➤ Koderma district in Jharkhand is historically cele-
brated as the "Mica Capital of India".
➤ India is one of the world's leading producers of sheet
mica, with major deposits in Andhra Pradesh,
Rajasthan, and Jharkhand.
➤ Mica splits easily into extremely thin, flexible, and
heat-resistant sheets along its basal cleavage planes.

41.question_text_en:
Q.2 The process of breakdown of glucose into pyruvate
occurs in which part of the cell?
41.explanation_en:
The breakdown of glucose into pyruvate occurs during
glycolysis, which takes place in the cytoplasm of
the cell. This metabolic pathway does not require oxygen
and produces a net gain of 2 ATP and 2 NADH mole-
cules.
Important Facts:
➤ Glycolysis is also known as the EMP pathway
(Embden-Meyerhof-Parnas pathway).
➤ In glycolysis, one 6-carbon molecule of glucose is
converted into two 3-carbon molecules of pyruvate.
➤ The Krebs cycle (citric acid cycle) and oxida-
tive phosphorylation take place inside the mitochon-
dria.
➤ Glycolysis is a universal pathway occurring in both
aerobic and anaerobic organisms.
➤ Mitochondria are known as the "powerhouses
of the cell" because the majority of ATP synthesis oc-
curs there.

42.question_text_en:
Q.33 Which scientific technology allows farmers and
scientists to monitor crop conditions, soil moisture and
agricultural patterns using satellite data?
42.explanation_en:
Remote sensing technology captures electromag-
netic radiation reflected or emitted from the Earth's sur-
face via satellite and airborne sensors, enabling preci-
sion assessment of crop health, vegetative indices, and
soil moisture levels.
Important Facts:
➤ The Normalized Difference Vegetation
Index (NDVI) is a standard remote sensing index used
to measure plant health.
➤ India's dedicated remote sensing satellite series is
known as the IRS (Indian Remote Sensing) satel-
lite system.
➤ The National Remote Sensing Centre
(NRSC) is situated at Hyderabad under ISRO.
➤ Remote sensing is broadly classified into active re-
mote sensing (uses own energy source like Radar)
and passive remote sensing (uses Sun's reflected
light).
➤ The Government of India utilizes the FASAL project
(Forecasting Agricultural output using Space, Agro-mete-
orology and Land-based observations) for crop
forecasting.

13.question_text_en:
Q.84 A traveler reaches an oasis with a full canteen of
water. Every day he crosses a desert dune, he drinks one-
third of the water remaining in his canteen plus 1 liter
more. After 2 days, his canteen is empty. How much water
did he start with?
13.explanation_en:
Q.84
Right option (B): 3.75 liters
Explanation
Let the initial amount of water be x liters.
• After Day 1, water left = (2/3)x − 1.
• After Day 2, water left = (2/3)((2/3)x − 1) − 1 = 0.
⇒ (2/3)x − 1 = 1.5 ⇒ (2/3)x = 2.5 ⇒ x = 2.5 × 3 / 2 = 3.75
liters.
✔ Answer: (B)

26.question_text_en:
Q.43 In Athletics, specifically in the 100 m sprint, what is
the maximum allowable "Tailwind" for a performance to be
officially recognized as a record?
26.explanation_en:
According to World Athletics technical rules, the
maximum allowable tailwind for record validation in out-
door sprint events (up to 200 m) and horizontal jumps is
+2.0 metres per second (+2.0 m/s). Any wind as-
sistance above this threshold invalidates record status.
Important Facts:
➤ The +2.0 m/s wind limit applies to the 100 m, 200
m, 100 m/110 m hurdles, long jump, and triple
jump.
➤ Wind velocity is measured using an electronic instru-
18 Download App Visit Website

ment called a wind gauge (anemometer).
➤ For the 100 m sprint, wind assistance is measured for
a duration of 10 seconds, starting from the flash of the
starter's gun.
➤ Performances with wind exceeding +2.0 m/s are
marked as wind-assisted (w) and cannot count for
world, area, or national records.
➤ World Athletics is the international governing
body for the sport of athletics, headquartered in Monaco.

27.question_text_en:
Q.20 The festival of 'Sarhul' is a major New Year
celebration that involves the ritualistic worship of the Sal
tree. This nature-centric festival is primarily observed by
the Munda oraon and Ho tribes in which Indian state?
27.explanation_en:
Sarhul is the most prominent spring festival celebrated
in Jharkhand by tribal communities such as the
Oraon, Munda, and Ho. It marks the tribal New Year
and worships nature through the blooming of the Sal
tree (Shorea robusta).
Important Facts:
➤ Sarhul is celebrated in the Hindu month of Chaitra
on the third day of Shukla Paksha.
➤ The festival commemorates the marriage of Mother
31 Download App Visit Website

Earth with the Sun, heralding the arrival of spring.
➤ The village priest, known as the Pahan, conducts
traditional rituals and distributes Sal flowers as
prasad.
➤ Traditional dances and music accompanied by instru-
ments like Mandar and Dhol form an essential part of
the celebrations.
➤ No agricultural activities like sowing begin until Sarhul
rituals are performed.

28.question_text_en:
Q.22 According to Census 2011, what was the sex ratio
for Muslims in India?
28.explanation_en:
According to the religious demographic data released
from Census 2011, the sex ratio among the Muslim
population in India was 951 females per 1,000
males, which was higher than the national overall aver-
age.
Important Facts:
➤ The overall national sex ratio of India as per Census
2011 was 943 females per 1,000 males.
➤ Among major religious communities, the sex ratio for
Christians was the highest at 1,023, while for Sikhs
it was 903.
➤ The sex ratio among Hindus was recorded at 939
females per 1,000 males.
➤ The sex ratio for Buddhists stood at 965 and for
Jains at 954.
➤ The Registrar General and Census
Commissioner of India under the Ministry of Home
Affairs conducts the decennial national census.

30.question_text_en:
Q.4 The classic Sanskrit play 'Abhigyan Shakuntalam' was
authored by:
30.explanation_en:
Abhigyan Shakuntalam is a masterpiece Sanskrit
play authored by the classical playwright and poet
Kalidasa. The play dramatises the love story of King
Dushyanta and Shakuntala, adapted from the epic
Mahabharata.
Important Facts:
➤ Kalidasa lived during the Gupta period and is re-
garded as the greatest poet-dramatist of classical
Sanskrit.
➤ His other major plays include Malavikagnimitram
and Vikramorvashiyam.
➤ Kalidasa's celebrated epic poems (Mahakavya) are
Raghuvamsha and Kumarasambhava.
➤ His famous lyrical poems (Khandakavya) are
Meghaduta and Ritusamhara.
➤ *Abhigyan Shakuntalam* was among the earliest
Indian literary works translated into Western languages,
translated by Sir William Jones in 1789.

31.question_text_en:
Q.14 Who among the following was the first woman to
serve as India's Permanent Representative to the United
Nations?
31.explanation_en:
Ruchira Kamboj, an Indian Foreign Service (IFS) offi-
cer of the 1987 batch, made history in August 2022 by
becoming the first woman to serve as India's
Permanent Representative to the United
Nations in New York.
Important Facts:
➤ Ruchira Kamboj succeeded T.S. Tirumurti as
India's Permanent Representative to the UN.
➤ She previously served as India's Ambassador to
Bhutan, Ambassador to UNESCO in Paris, and High
Commissioner to South Africa.
➤ Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit was the first woman to be
elected President of the UN General Assembly
in 1953, but was not the Permanent Representative.
➤ The Permanent Mission of India to the UN represents
the country across the UN Secretariat and its various
bodies.
➤ Ruchira Kamboj retired from the Indian Foreign
Service in June 2024 after an illustrious career.

established in 1995, which organization administered
multilateral trade agreements?

The General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade
(GATT) governed international multilateral trade rules
from 1948 until it was officially superseded by the World
Trade Organization (WTO) on 1 January 1995
following the Marrakesh Agreement.
Important Facts:
➤ GATT was signed by 23 nations in Geneva in 1947
and came into effect on 1 January 1948.
YouTube Telegram 46

trade negotiations, which spanned from 1986 to 1994.
➤ Unlike GATT, which was an ad-hoc legal agreement
with no institutional foundation, the WTO is a full-fledged
permanent international organisation.
➤ The WTO encompasses trade in goods (GATT),
trade in services (GATS), and intellectual prop-
erty rights (TRIPS).
➤ The headquarters of the World Trade Organization is

Q.17 Which element is essential in a "Panchayatana"
temple layout?
33.explanation_en:
A Panchayatana temple style consists of a main
central shrine surrounded by four subsidiary
shrines, making a total of five shrines. The term
originates from the Sanskrit words 'Pancha' (five) and
'Ayatana' (shrine/abode).
Important Facts:
➤ The Panchayatana layout is a prominent feature
of ancient and medieval Nagara and Dravida archi-
YouTube Telegram 56
GENERAL AWARENESS
tecture.
➤ Famous examples include the Kandariya
Mahadeva Temple and Lakshmana Temple at
Khajuraho.
➤ In Odisha, the Brahmeshwara Temple in
Bhubaneswar is built on the Panchayatana plan.
➤ The subsidiary shrines are typically placed at the four
corners of a raised rectangular plinth (jagati).
➤ The layout symbolises a central presiding deity
flanked by four complementary secondary deities.

34.question_text_en:
Q.12 The model that was adopted for India's Second Five-
Year Plan was:
34.explanation_en:
India's Second Five-Year Plan (1956–1961) was
based on the Mahalanobis Model, formulated by
renowned statistician Prasanta Chandra
Mahalanobis, which emphasised heavy industrialisa-
tion and the development of basic capital goods indus-
tries.
Important Facts:
➤ The First Five-Year Plan (1951–1956) was based on
the Harrod-Domar Model focusing primarily on agri-
culture.
➤ The Second Plan laid the groundwork for public-sec-
tor steel plants at Bhilai, Rourkela, and Durgapur.
➤ P.C. Mahalanobis founded the Indian Statistical
Institute (ISI) in Kolkata in 1931.
➤ National Statistics Day is celebrated every year in
India on 29 June to mark the birth anniversary of P.C.
Mahalanobis.
➤ The Second Plan aimed at a rapid 25% increase in
national income through rapid industrialisation.

35.question_text_en:
Q.7 Fill in the blank: Article ____ explicitly states that
courts cannot question the validity of Parliamentary
proceedings.
35.explanation_en:
Article 122 of the Constitution of India provides immu-
nity to parliamentary proceedings, stating that the validity
of any proceedings in Parliament cannot be called in
question on the ground of any alleged irregularity of pro-
cedure.
Important Facts:
➤ Article 122(1) prohibits courts from inquiring into
parliamentary proceedings on grounds of irregularity of
procedure.
➤ Article 122(2) shields officers and members of
Parliament from court jurisdiction regarding powers exer-
cised for regulating procedure or conducting business.
➤ Article 120 deals with the language to be used
in Parliament (Hindi or English).
➤ Article 121 restricts discussions in Parliament re-
garding the conduct of judges of the Supreme Court or
High Courts.
➤ Article 123 empowers the President to pro-
mulgate Ordinances during the recess of
Parliament.

provisions is:

Important Facts:

Rajiv Gandhi to curb political opportunism.
➤ The question of disqualification under the Tenth
Schedule is decided by the Chairman or Speaker of
the respective House.
➤ The Supreme Court ruled in the landmark Kihoto

37.question_text_en:

initial resolution by the Rajya Sabha declaring it nec-

➤ Currently, there are three All-India Services in India:
the Indian Administrative Service (IAS), the
Indian Police Service (IPS), and the Indian
Forest Service (IFS).
➤ The Indian Forest Service was created as the
third All-India Service in 1966 under the All India
Services Act, 1951.
➤ Article 249 empowers Parliament to legislate on a
State List subject in the national interest upon a Rajya
Sabha resolution.
➤ Article 315 deals with the Public Service
Commissions for the Union and for the States (UPSC
and SPSCs).

40.explanation_en:
Erosion is the exogenic geological process involving
the wearing away, detachment, and transportation of
weathered rock material and soil across the Earth's sur-
face by geomorphic agents such as running water,
glaciers, wind, and waves.
Important Facts:
➤ Weathering refers to the in-situ breakdown of
rocks, while erosion involves the dynamic transport of
YouTube Telegram 15

4
ms (2 Qs)
that debris.

humid regions, creating landforms like gorges,
canyons, and V-shaped valleys.

41.question_text_en:
Q.4 What is the reason that different regions on Earth
experience varying climates despite receiving energy from
the same Sun?
41.explanation_en:
Due to Earth's spherical shape and the tilt of its axis, the
angle of incidence of sunlight varies with latitude.
Areas near the equator receive direct, perpendicular
rays concentrating solar energy, while higher latitudes
receive oblique rays spread over larger areas.
Important Facts:
➤ The angle at which solar radiation strikes the Earth's
surface determines the intensity of insolation.
➤ The Earth's axial tilt of 23.5 degrees combined
with revolution causes seasonal climatic variations.
YouTube Telegram 15
GENERAL AWARENESS
➤ Oblique rays at higher latitudes pass through a
thicker layer of atmosphere, losing more energy through
absorption and scattering.
➤ The equatorial region experiences a net heat sur-
plus, whereas polar regions experience a net heat
deficit.
➤ Atmospheric circulation and ocean currents act as
heat redistribution mechanisms across different
latitudes.

42.question_text_en:

which type of agricultural practice in India?

options.text_en: Slash-and-burn shifting cultivation in North-Eastern India

42.explanation_en:
In India, Jhumming is the local name for slash-and-
burn shifting cultivation primarily practiced in the
hill tracts of North-Eastern India (such as Assam,
Meghalaya, Nagaland, and Mizoram).
Important Facts:
➤ In this method, farmers clear a patch of forest land by
cutting and burning vegetation, and cultivate crops on
the ash-enriched soil for a few seasons before moving.
➤ Shifting cultivation is known by various regional
names in India: Bewar or Dahiya in Madhya Pradesh,
Podu or Penda in Andhra Pradesh.
➤ In Odisha, it is known as Koman or Bringa, and in
the Western Ghats, it is called Kumari.
➤ Globally, shifting cultivation is known as Milpa in
Mexico/Central America, Roca in Brazil, and Ladang
in Indonesia.
➤ The practice has faced restrictions due to soil ero-
sion, deforestation, and reduced fallow cycle lengths.

43.explanation_en:
The taxonomic order of the housefly (*Musca domes-
tica*) is Diptera. Insects in the order Diptera are char-
acterised by possessing only a single pair of functional
flight wings, with the hindwings modified into balancing
organs called halteres.
Important Facts:
➤ The complete taxonomic hierarchy of the housefly is:
Phylum Arthropoda, Class Insecta, Order Diptera,
Family Muscidae, Genus Musca, Species domes-
tica.
➤ 'Diptera' is derived from Greek words meaning 'two
wings'.
➤ The hind pair of wings in Diptera is modified into sen-
sory structures called halteres for gyroscopic balance
during flight.
➤ Houseflies possess sponging and lapping type
mouthparts adapted for liquid nutrition.
➤ They serve as vectors for pathogenic diseases in-
cluding cholera, typhoid, and dysentery.

44.question_text_en:
Q.34 Why is space technology important in disaster
management for predicting and monitoring natural hazards
effectively?
44.explanation_en:
Space technology, including Earth observation satellites
and meteorological constellations, provides real-
time monitoring and broad synoptic coverage, en-
abling early warnings, damage assessment, and prompt
decision-making during natural disasters.
Important Facts:
➤ Remote sensing satellites provide continuous, multi-
spectral data for tracking cyclones, floods, droughts, and
forest fires.
➤ Communication satellites ensure vital connectivity
when terrestrial communication networks collapse during
disasters.
➤ Navigation satellites like NavIC and GPS help guide
search and rescue operations to precise coordinates.
➤ India's National Remote Sensing Centre
(NRSC) under ISRO plays a central role in generating
near-real-time flood and cyclone maps.
➤ Space imagery enables accurate pre-disaster vulner-
ability mapping as well as post-disaster loss estimation.

45.question_text_en:
Q.2 The adoption of Agenda 21 at the Rio Earth Summit
(1992) primarily reflected:

options.text_en: Global commitment to link environment with development
Agreement to place forests under international ownership
Replace national policies with one global law
Prioritise economic growth over climate and biodiversity

45.explanation_en:
Agenda 21, adopted at the 1992 Rio Earth
Summit (United Nations Conference on Environment
and Development), is a comprehensive action plan re-
flecting a global commitment to integrate envi-
ronmental protection with sustainable socio-
economic development.
Important Facts:
➤ The Rio Earth Summit was held in Rio de Janeiro,
Brazil, in June 1992.
➤ 'Agenda 21' signifies a blueprint for sustainable de-
velopment in the 21st century.
➤ The summit also led to the creation of the UNFCCC,
CBD (Convention on Biological Diversity), and the Rio
Declaration.
➤ It emphasizes Local Agenda 21, urging local gov-
ernments to implement sustainable policies at the grass-
roots level.
➤ The summit popularized the principle of Common
But Differentiated Responsibilities (CBDR).

relocated to India, was originally known by which name?

Namibia to Kuno National Park in September 2022, was
20 Download App Visit Website

originally named Siyaya before being rechristened in
India. She famously gave birth to multiple litters of cubs
in Kuno.
Important Facts:
➤ Project Cheetah is the world's first intercontinen-
tal large wild carnivore translocation project.
➤ The first batch of 8 cheetahs (5 females and 3
males) was brought from Namibia to Kuno National
Park, Madhya Pradesh, in September 2022.
➤ Cheetah 'Asha' was originally named TB before be-
ing renamed in India.
➤ Asiatic cheetahs became extinct in India in 1952 due
to excessive hunting and habitat loss.
➤ Kuno National Park was selected because of its suit-
able savannah-like woodland habitat and prey base.

47.question_text_en:
Q.5 Which country was invited as the 'Guest Country' at
the 7th NSA-level meeting of the Colombo Security
Conclave in 2025?
47.explanation_en:
Malaysia was invited and participated for the first time
as the 'Guest Country' at the 7th NSA-level
meeting of the Colombo Security Conclave
(CSC) held in New Delhi in November 2025.
Important Facts:
➤ The Colombo Security Conclave (CSC) was
originally formed as a trilateral maritime security group-
ing by India, Sri Lanka, and the Maldives.
➤ Seychelles joined as a full member during the 7th
NSA-level meeting, expanding membership alongside
Mauritius.
➤ The Conclave operates on five pillars including mar-
itime safety, counter-terrorism, combating trafficking, cy-
bersecurity, and humanitarian assistance.
➤ The meeting was hosted by India's National Security
Adviser (NSA) Ajit Doval.
➤ Bangladesh had previously participated in earlier
meetings as an observer nation.

which of the following pair is correctly matched?

Faso was ranked at the 2nd position among the
countries most impacted by terrorism. The GTI is pub-
lished annually by the Institute for Economics and
Peace (IEP) to track terrorism trends globally.
Important Facts:
➤ The Global Terrorism Index is produced annu-
ally by the Institute for Economics and Peace
(IEP) based in Sydney.
➤ Burkina Faso is located in the Sahel region of
West Africa, which has become an epicentre of terror-
ism.

49.question_text_en:
Q.23 PM-SETU (Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability
Transformation through Upgraded ITIs) was launched in
which year?
49.explanation_en:
The PM-SETU scheme was approved and rolled out in
2025 by the Government of India to comprehensively
revamp and modernize 1,000 Government
Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) across the
country into world-class skill training hubs.
Important Facts:
➤ The full form of PM-SETU is Pradhan Mantri
Skilling and Employability Transformation
through Upgraded ITIs.
➤ The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of
Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
(MSDE).
➤ It adopts a Hub-and-Spoke model, designating
200 Hub ITIs and 800 Spoke ITIs across states.
➤ It introduces an industry-led Special Purpose
Vehicle (SPV) governance structure under Section 8
of the Companies Act.
➤ The scheme aligns vocational training with emerging
industry requirements such as Industry 4.0, green skills,
and advanced automation.

Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs)?

options.text_en: World Trade Organisation and World Bank
World Bank and Asian Development Bank
Reserve Bank of India and Asian Development Bank
United Nations Development Programme and World Bank

50.explanation_en:
The World Bank and the Asian Development
Bank (ADB) are the multilateral development institu-
tions extending external co-financing support to the
Government of India for implementing the PM-SETU
initiative.
Important Facts:
➤ The World Bank is headquartered in
64 Download App Visit Website

opment financing.
➤ The Asian Development Bank (ADB) was es-
tablished in 1966 and is headquartered in
Mandaluyong, Philippines.
➤ External multilateral financing assists in scaling capi-
tal expenditure for high-tech machinery and digital labs
in upgraded ITIs.
➤ The co-financing arrangement supports structural re-
forms in vocational curriculum and trainer capacity build-
ing.
➤ India is a founding member of the Asian Development
Bank and one of its largest borrowing partners.

chanics.
➤ In competitive shooting, snap caps or dummy rounds
are frequently used during dry fire practice to protect fir-
ing pins from damage.
➤ Target shooting events at the Olympics are governed
globally by the International Shooting Sport
Federation (ISSF).
➤ Abhinav Bindra won India's first individual Olympic
gold medal in the 10m Air Rifle event at the 2008
Beijing Olympics.
➤ At the 2024 Paris Olympics, Manu Bhaker be-
came the first athlete from independent India to win two
medals at a single Olympic Games in shooting.

27.question_text_en:
Q.34 Which of the following is the maximum number of
players on the field in a standard kabaddi team during
play?
27.explanation_en:
In standard competitive kabaddi, each team fields 7
players on the court at the start of play, while keeping
up to 5 substitutes on the bench (total squad size of 12).
Important Facts:
➤ A standard kabaddi match lasts for 40 minutes, di-
vided into two halves of 20 minutes each.
➤ The standard court dimension for men's kabaddi is
13 metres × 10 metres, while for women it is 12
metres × 8 metres.
➤ A raider has a maximum time limit of 30 seconds to
YouTube Telegram 16
GENERAL AWARENESS
complete a raid.
➤ Kabaddi was introduced as a competitive medal sport
at the Asian Games in 1990 Beijing.
➤ The governing body for kabaddi in India is the
Amateur Kabaddi Federation of India (AKFI).

28.question_text_en:
Q.35 Which of the following correctly matches the Asian
Games medal system?
28.explanation_en:
Like the Olympic Games, the Asian Games award
Gold, Silver, and Bronze medals to the competi-
tors finishing in first, second, and third place, respec-
tively.
Important Facts:
➤ The first edition of the Asian Games was held in
New Delhi in 1951.
➤ The Asian Games are organized every four years by
the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA).
➤ The emblem of the Asian Games features a rising
red sun with interlocking rings.
➤ The 19th Asian Games were held in Hangzhou,
China in 2023, where India achieved a record tally of
107 medals.
➤ The 20th Asian Games (2026) are scheduled to be
held in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan.

29.question_text_en:
Q.10 What is the name of the distinctive stiff skirt used in
Manipuri classical dance?
29.explanation_en:
In Manipuri classical dance (specifically in Raas
Leela), female dancers wear an iconic, barrel-shaped
stiff skirt called Poloi (or Potloi). It is embellished with
mirrors, embroidery, and stiffened canvas to maintain its
distinct cylindrical flare.
Important Facts:
➤ Potloi (or Poloi) costume was introduced during the
reign of King Bhagyachandra (Maharaja Ningthou
Ching-Thang Khomba).
➤ Raas Leela depicts the divine love of Radha and
Krishna and forms the central theme of Manipuri
dance.
➤ A translucent white veil called Koktombi is worn
over the head covering the face partially.
➤ Phanek is a traditional wraparound sarong worn by
Meitei women for daily and semi-formal wear.
➤ Manipuri is one of the major eight classical dances
recognized by the Sangeet Natak Akademi.

30.question_text_en:
Q.10 In which year was the Shanghai Cooperation
Organization (SCO) established?
30.explanation_en:
The Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO)
was established on 15 June 2001 in Shanghai, China,
by the leaders of China, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan,
Russia, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan.
Important Facts:
➤ The precursor group was known as the Shanghai
Five, formed in 1996 (China, Russia, Kazakhstan,
Kyrgyzstan, and Tajikistan).
➤ With the inclusion of Uzbekistan in June 2001, the
grouping was officially renamed the Shanghai
Cooperation Organization.
➤ India and Pakistan joined the SCO as full mem-
44 Download App Visit Website

bers at the Astana Summit in June 2017.
➤ The headquarters (Secretariat) of the SCO is located
in Beijing, China.
➤ The Executive Committee of the Regional Anti-
Terrorist Structure (RATS) of the SCO is headquartered
in Tashkent, Uzbekistan.

31.question_text_en: Q.4 PM-AASHA stands for:

options.text_en: Pradhan Mantri Aatma-Nirbhar Aay Sahayata Abhiyan
Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan
Pradhan Mantri Annadata Awas Suraksha Abhiyan
Pradhan Mantri Agricultural Aay Samridhi Abhiyan

31.explanation_en:
PM-AASHA stands for Pradhan Mantri Annadata
Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan, an umbrella scheme
launched by the Government of India in 2018 to ensure
remunerative prices to farmers for their produce.
Important Facts:
➤ The scheme was approved by the Union Cabinet in
September 2018.
➤ PM-AASHA comprises three key sub-components:
Price Support Scheme (PSS), Price Deficiency
Payment Scheme (PDPS), and Pilot of Private
Procurement and Stockist Scheme (PPSS).
➤ It covers pulses, oilseeds, and copra to protect farm-
ers against steep price falls below the Minimum Support
Price (MSP).
➤ Under PDPS, no physical procurement takes place;
farmers receive direct payment of the difference be-
tween MSP and the modal market price.
➤ The scheme is implemented under the Ministry of
Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.

32.question_text_en:
Q.5 Which organisation is responsible for pension payout
under Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM-SYM)?

options.text_en: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development

Reserve Bank of India
YouTube Telegram 49
GENERAL AWARENESS

32.explanation_en:
The Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC)
acts as the pension fund manager responsible for fund
management and the monthly pension payout under the
Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM-
SYM) scheme.
Important Facts:
➤ PM-SYM is a central sector scheme launched in
2019 by the Ministry of Labour and Employment for un-
organised workers.
➤ Beneficiaries receive an assured monthly pension of
Rs3,000 upon reaching the age of 60 years.
➤ The entry age for the scheme is between 18 and 40
years, with a monthly contribution ranging from Rs55 to
Rs200.
➤ The Central Government makes a matching 50:50
contribution equal to the subscriber's monthly contri-
bution.
➤ Workers earning a monthly income of Rs15,000 or
less who are not covered under EPFO, ESIC, or NPS
are eligible.

33.question_text_en:
Q.3 During the Delhi Sultanate period, the Lodi dynasty
introduced the architectural concept of the 'double dome'.
What was the primary structural purpose behind this
innovation?

options.text_en: To allow for the installation of an upper prayer hall.
To create an acoustic chamber for the muezzin.

To give strength to the structure and lower the inner height
of the dome.

To store water for cooling the inner chambers during
summer.

33.explanation_en:
The double dome technique provided external
grandeur and height to the building while maintaining
proportionate ceiling height internally, simultaneously
giving structural strength and thermal insulation.
Important Facts:
70 Download App Visit Website

➤ The tomb of Sikandar Lodi (located in Lodhi
Gardens, New Delhi) is widely regarded as the first ma-
ture example of a double dome in India.
➤ A double dome consists of two shells: an outer shell
providing impressive elevation and an inner shell giving
balanced interior proportions.
➤ This technique was later perfected and extensively
used during the Mughal era, prominently seen in
Humayun's Tomb and the Taj Mahal.
➤ The Lodi dynasty (1451–1526) was founded by
Bahlul Lodi and was the final dynasty of the Delhi
Sultanate.
➤ Octagonal and square tombs were typical architec-
tural features developed during the Sayyid and Lodi
periods.

34.question_text_en: Q.10 Tax reforms include:
34.explanation_en:
The primary goals of tax reforms are simplifying
the tax system, rationalizing tax slabs, reducing com-
pliance burdens, curbing tax evasion, and widening the
tax base to ensure efficient revenue collection.
Important Facts:
➤ The Tax Reforms Committee (1991) under the
chairmanship of Raja J. Chelliah laid the foundational
roadmap for modern tax rationalization in India.
➤ In 2017, the Goods and Services Tax (GST)
was introduced via the 101st Constitutional
Amendment Act to simplify indirect taxation under
"One Nation, One Tax".
➤ Direct tax reforms focus on lowering corporate and
personal income tax rates while phasing out distortionary
exemptions.
➤ The Kelkar Task Force (2002) recommended sig-
nificant structural reforms in both direct and indirect taxa-
tion.
➤ Simplifying tax procedures enhances compliance, re-
duces litigation, and encourages higher tax-to-GDP
ratios.

35.question_text_en:
Q.2 Which two international financial institutions did India
approach for a loan to manage the 1991 economic crisis?

options.text_en: World Bank and Asian Development Bank
World Bank and World Trade Organization
World Bank and International Monetary Fund
Reserve Bank of India and World Trade Organization

35.explanation_en:
During the severe balance of payments crisis in 1991,
India approached the World Bank (IBRD) and the
International Monetary Fund (IMF) for a $7 bil-
lion bailout loan to stabilize its economy.
Important Facts:
➤ The economic crisis led to the initiation of LPG re-
forms (Liberalisation, Privatisation, and Globalisation)
in 1991.
➤ In exchange for the financial assistance, the IMF and
World Bank required India to implement structural ad-
justment and trade liberalization reforms.
➤ P. V. Narasimha Rao was the Prime Minister and
Dr. Manmohan Singh was the Finance Minister dur-
ing the 1991 reforms.
➤ India's foreign exchange reserves had dropped to
dangerously low levels, sufficient to pay for barely two
weeks of imports.
➤ India pledged its gold reserves with the Bank of
England and Union Bank of Switzerland to se-
cure immediate emergency funds.

36.question_text_en:
Q.6 In which Five-Year Plan was the 'Removal of Poverty'
(Garibi Hatao) proposed as the main objective?
36.explanation_en:
The Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974–1979) focused on
two main objectives: Garibi Hatao (Removal of
Poverty) and Attainment of Self-reliance. The plan
was prepared and launched under the leadership of
Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.
Important Facts:
➤ The slogan Garibi Hatao, Desh Bachao was
given by Indira Gandhi during the 1971 general elec-
tion campaign.
➤ The Fifth Five-Year Plan was drafted by D.P.
Dhar.
➤ In 1975, the Twenty-Point Programme was in-
troduced to accelerate poverty eradication.
➤ This plan was terminated in 1978, a year early, by the
00 Download App Visit Website

Janata Party government, which introduced the
Rolling Plan.
➤ The National Programme of Minimum Needs
(MNP) was also introduced during this plan.

37.question_text_en:
Q.1 Which constitutional principle is most directly invoked
in support of the Uniform Civil Code (UCC)?
37.explanation_en:
The Uniform Civil Code (UCC) is explicitly embodied in
Article 44 under Part IV of the Indian Constitution,
which comprises the Directive Principles of State
Policy (DPSP).
Important Facts:
➤ Article 44 states that "The State shall endeavour to
secure for the citizens a Uniform Civil Code throughout
the territory of India."
➤ Directive Principles of State Policy are enumerated in
Part IV (Articles 36 to 51) of the Constitution.
➤ DPSPs are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot
be enforced directly through courts of law, but are funda-
mental in the governance of the country.
➤ The concept of Directive Principles of State Policy
was borrowed from the Irish Constitution.
➤ Uttarakhand became the first state in independent
India to pass a Uniform Civil Code Bill in 2024.

38.question_text_en:
Q.10 In a situation where Union and State laws conflict on
a Concurrent List subject and the state law has
Presidential assent, which principle determines validity of
the law?
38.explanation_en:
The Doctrine of Repugnancy under Article 254
of the Constitution of India resolves inconsistencies be-
tween Central and State laws on Concurrent List sub-
jects; under Article 254(2), a state law prevails in that
state if it has received Presidential assent.
Important Facts:
➤ Article 254(1) provides that if a State law is repug-
nant to a Union law on a Concurrent List subject, the
Union law prevails and the State law is void to the extent
of repugnancy.
➤ Article 254(2) acts as an exception: if the State
law is reserved for the consideration of the President
and receives assent, it prevails in that State.
➤ Even after presidential assent, Parliament has the
power under the proviso to Article 254(2) to enact a sub-
sequent law adding to, amending, or repealing such a
State law.
➤ The Concurrent List (List III) is detailed in the
Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution and
contains 52 subjects.
➤ The concept of the Concurrent List was borrowed
from the Australian Constitution.

39.question_text_en:
Q.18 Regarding the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA),
which of the following best describes the admissibility of
digital evidence?

options.text_en: It is only admissible as secondary evidence.
It requires a physical signed copy to be valid.

It is treated as primary evidence if authenticated per Section
63.

It is not admissible in cases involving heinous crimes.
39 Download App Visit Website
MOCKMATRIX
PRACTICE TO PERFECTION

39.explanation_en:
Under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA),
2023, electronic and digital records are granted equal
legal standing with physical documents and are admissi-
ble as primary evidence when authenticated and
certified under Section 63.
Important Facts:
➤ The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 re-
placed the colonial-era Indian Evidence Act of
1872.
➤ BSA came into force on 1 July 2024 along with the
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Bharatiya Nagarik
Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS).
➤ Section 63 of the BSA lays down conditions and
certificate requirements for the admissibility of electronic
records (corresponding to Section 65B of the Indian
Evidence Act).
➤ Digital evidence includes emails, server logs, smart-
phone files, messages, digital location records, and
voice mails.
➤ The BSA explicitly categorizes electronic and digital
records within the definition of a document.

40.question_text_en:
Q.5 What is the fundamental reason for the regular
occurrence of day and night on Earth as it experiences
alternating periods of light and darkness?

options.text_en: Rotation on its own axis daily

40.explanation_en:
The rotation of Earth on its own axis from west
to east once every approximately 24 hours causes differ-
ent parts of the Earth to face toward and away from the
Sun, resulting in day and night.
Important Facts:
➤ Earth completes one rotation relative to the Sun in
approximately 24 hours (a solar day).
➤ Earth rotates on its tilted axis from west to east,
making the Sun appear to rise in the east and set in the
west.
➤ Earth's axial tilt of 23.5 degrees combined with its
YouTube Telegram 14
GENERAL AWARENESS
revolution around the Sun causes the change of sea-
sons.
➤ The imaginary line dividing the daylit side from the
dark side of the globe is called the Circle of
Illumination.
➤ A sidereal day (rotation relative to distant stars) is ap-
proximately 23 hours, 56 minutes, and 4
seconds.

41.question_text_en:
Q.6 Which phenomenon accounts for the observed shift in
the positions of stars in the night sky when viewed from
Earth at different times?
41.explanation_en:
During the course of a single night, the apparent continu-
ous motion and shifting of stars from east to west across
the night sky is caused by Earth's rotation on its
axis from west to east.
Important Facts:
➤ The apparent daily movement of celestial bodies
across the sky is known as diurnal motion.
➤ Because of Earth's rotation, all stars appear to rotate
counterclockwise around the Pole Star (Polaris) in
the Northern Hemisphere.
➤ The Pole Star appears almost stationary because it
lies nearly aligned with the northern rotational axis of the
Earth.
➤ Earth completes one full 360-degree rotation on its
axis in one sidereal day (approx. 23 hours 56 min-
utes).
➤ Over months throughout the year, seasonal changes
in constellations are caused by Earth's revolution
around the Sun.

42.question_text_en:
Q.7 Groundnut accounts for nearly half of India's major
oilseed production, mainly because:

options.text_en: It can only be cultivated in irrigated regions.
It is widely grown as a kharif crop in several states.
It requires very low temperatures for cultivation.
It is exclusively produced for export purposes.

42.explanation_en:
Groundnut is a predominant tropical and subtropical
oilseed crop that is widely grown as a kharif crop
across prominent producing states like Gujarat,
Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, and Andhra Pradesh, making it a
major contributor to India's oilseed basket.
Important Facts:
➤ Gujarat is the leading producer of groundnut in
India, followed by Rajasthan and Tamil Nadu.
➤ Groundnut accounts for approximately 40% to 50% of
the total major oilseeds production in India.
➤ Although predominantly grown as a kharif crop, it
is also cultivated as a rabi and zaid crop in southern and
peninsular India.
➤ Groundnut (*Arachis hypogaea*) is a leguminous
crop that helps in biological nitrogen fixation, improving
soil fertility.
➤ It thrives best in well-drained sandy loam and
loamy soils with warm temperatures of 20°C to 30°C.

43.question_text_en:
Q.8 Why are aggregate statistics (like death rate)
considered social phenomena rather than just individual
data?

options.text_en: They reflect patterns influenced by society.
They are collected by the government.

43.explanation_en:
In sociology and demography, aggregate statistics like
death rates are treated as social facts because they re-
veal consistent collective patterns and regularities
influenced by broader societal conditions,
healthcare infrastructure, living standards, and public
policies.
Important Facts:
➤ French sociologist Émile Durkheim demonstrated
this concept in his classic 1897 sociological study
*Suicide*, showing individual acts form measurable so-
cial facts.
➤ Aggregate rates point to structural realities including
sanitation, poverty, working conditions, and healthcare
access.
➤ Demography is defined as the scientific study of hu-
man populations, their size, structure, distribution, and
YouTube Telegram 17
GENERAL AWARENESS
changes.
➤ The Crude Death Rate (CDR) represents the
number of deaths occurring per 1,000 individuals in a
given population per year.
➤ Vital statistics in India are primarily registered under
the Registration of Births and Deaths Act,
1969.

44.question_text_en:
Q.2 Which of the following processes is correctly matched
with the organisms/cells that perform it?

options.text_en:
Anaerobic respiration - Yeast
YouTube Telegram 19
GENERAL AWARENESS
5
espiration (2 Qs)

44.explanation_en:
Yeast (a single-celled fungus) performs anaerobic
respiration (alcoholic fermentation), breaking down
glucose into ethanol, carbon dioxide, and energy in the
absence of oxygen.
Important Facts:
➤ In yeast, the end products of anaerobic fermentation
are ethanol ($C_2H_5OH$) and carbon dioxide
($CO_2$).
➤ In human muscle cells, anaerobic respiration
produces lactic acid, leading to muscle cramps during
strenuous exercise.
➤ Obligate anaerobes cannot survive in the pres-
ence of oxygen and carry out anaerobic processes ex-
clusively.
➤ Aerobic respiration occurs in the presence of
oxygen within the mitochondria of eukaryotic cells,
yielding up to 36–38 ATP molecules.
➤ Anaerobic breakdown of glucose produces signifi-
cantly less energy, yielding only 2 ATP molecules per
glucose molecule.

45.question_text_en:
Q.27 What is the role of communication satellites in
broadcasting television and internet services across
different regions globally?
45.explanation_en:
Communication satellites serve as relay stations in
space that receive, amplify, and retransmit signals back
to Earth, enabling wide-area and global signal distri-
bution for television, radio, and internet networks.
Important Facts:
➤ Most broadcast communication satellites operate in
the Geostationary Orbit (GEO) at an altitude of ap-
proximately 35,786 km.
➤ A satellite in geostationary orbit matches Earth's rota-
tional period, appearing stationary over a fixed point on
the equator.
➤ Just three geostationary satellites spaced
120 degrees apart can provide global telecommunication
coverage (excluding polar extremes).
➤ Communication satellites use transponders operating
across microwave bands such as C-band, Ku-band,
YouTube Telegram 21
GENERAL AWARENESS
and Ka-band.
➤ India launched its dedicated Indian National Satellite
System (INSAT) series for telecommunication and
broadcasting starting in the 1980s.

46.question_text_en:
Q.28 Which launch vehicle was used by ISRO to deploy
36 OneWeb satellites simultaneously, marking its entry
into the heavy commercial launch market?
46.explanation_en:
ISRO used the Launch Vehicle Mark-III (LVM3-
M3) on 26 March 2023 (as well as LVM3-M2 in October
2022) to deploy 36 OneWeb Gen-1 communication sat-
ellites into Low Earth Orbit for commercial customer
OneWeb.
Important Facts:
➤ The LVM3-M3 / OneWeb India-2 mission suc-
cessfully injected 36 satellites weighing roughly 5,805 kg
into Low Earth Orbit (LEO).
➤ The mission was executed under a commercial con-
tract between OneWeb and NewSpace India
Limited (NSIL), the commercial arm of ISRO.
➤ LVM3 (formerly known as GSLV Mk-III) is India's
heaviest rocket, capable of launching up to 4,000 kg into
GTO and 8,000 kg into LEO.
➤ The rocket features three stages: two solid rocket
boosters (S200), a liquid core stage (L110), and a
cryogenic upper stage (C25).
➤ LVM3 is also the chosen launch vehicle for India's hu-
man spaceflight mission, Gaganyaan.

47.question_text_en:
Q.26 Which country startup NitroCapt won 2025 Food
Planet Prize for green fertilizer technology using plasma
renewable energy to extract nitrogen from air eliminating
fossil fuels in production process?
47.explanation_en:
NitroCapt is a clean-tech startup based in Sweden
that developed the SUNIFIX process, which fixes atmo-
spheric nitrogen using plasma and renewable energy,
winning the prestigious Food Planet Prize.
Important Facts:
➤ The Food Planet Prize is the world's largest envi-
ronmental prize awarded by the Curt Bergfors
Foundation in Sweden.
➤ NitroCapt's proprietary technology is known as the
SUNIFIX process.
43 Download App Visit Website

➤ The conventional Haber-Bosch process contrib-
utes significantly to global greenhouse gas emissions by
relying heavily on fossil fuels.
➤ The prize recognizes scalable solutions that trans-
form the global food system toward sustainability.
➤ The prize amount for the awardee is $2 million to
help scale ground-breaking innovations.

48.question_text_en:
Q.27 Who has been awarded Sahitya Akademi Yuva
Puraskar 2025 for Hindi language among winners
announced by Sahitya Akademi recognizing literary
contributions across multiple Indian languages including
English and regional languages?
48.explanation_en:
Parvati Tirkey was chosen for the Sahitya
Akademi Yuva Puraskar 2025 in the Hindi lan-
guage for her poetry collection titled Fir Ugna (िफर
उगना).
Important Facts:
➤ The Sahitya Akademi Yuva Puraskar was in-
stituted in 2011 to promote young writers under the age
of 35.
➤ The award comprises an engraved copper plaque
and a cash prize of Rs50,000.
➤ Parvati Tirkey's collection Fir Ugna captures tribal
consciousness, ecological connection, and indigenous
struggles.
➤ Sahitya Akademi gives Yuva Puraskar in 24 Indian
languages (22 Eighth Schedule languages plus
English and Rajasthani).
➤ The parent organization Sahitya Akademi was es-
tablished in 1954 with headquarters at Rabindra
Bhavan, New Delhi.

49.question_text_en:
Q.28 Who is the author of the 2024 International Booker
Prize-winning novel 'Kairos'?

options.text_en:
Geetanjali Shree
YouTube Telegram 24
GENERAL AWARENESS

49.explanation_en:
German author Jenny Erpenbeck won the 2024
International Booker Prize for her novel Kairos,
which was translated from German into English by
Michael Hofmann.
Important Facts:
➤ The novel Kairos is set in East Berlin and explores
a destructive love affair against the backdrop of the col-
lapse of the Berlin Wall.
➤ Jenny Erpenbeck became the first German writer
to win the International Booker Prize.
➤ Michael Hofmann shared the £50,000 prize
equally with the author as its English translator.
➤ Geetanjali Shree became the first Hindi author to
win the International Booker Prize in 2022 for *Tomb of
Sand* (रेत समािध).
➤ Han Kang of South Korea won the 2016
International Booker Prize for *The Vegetarian* and the
2024 Nobel Prize in Literature.

50.question_text_en:
Q.21 According to the Human Development Report 2025
(based on 2023 data), which country recorded the highest
Human Development Index (HDI) value of approximately
0.972?
50.explanation_en:
In the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)
Human Development Report, Switzerland ranked first
globally with the highest Human Development Index
(HDI) score of approximately 0.972.
Important Facts:
➤ The Human Development Index (HDI) was
created in 1990 by Pakistani economist Mahbub ul
Haq and Indian Nobel laureate Amartya Sen.
➤ HDI evaluates three basic dimensions: a long and
healthy life, access to knowledge, and a de-
cent standard of living.
➤ The indicator is published annually by the United
Nations Development Programme (UNDP).
➤ Norway, Iceland, and Denmark regularly follow
closely among the top-tier very high human development
nations.
➤ The HDI value ranges between 0 and 1, where val-
ues of 0.800 and above indicate very high human
development.

wise or column-wise. Identify this pattern and choose the

The conclusion that expanding the metro to three more

28.question_text_en: Q.39 In chess, what does the term "fork" refer to?
28.explanation_en:
In chess tactics, a fork is a move where a single piece
attacks two or more of the opponent's pieces
simultaneously.
Important Facts:
➤ The Knight is particularly renowned for forks be-
cause its L-shaped jumping movement can attack pieces
without being threatened back.
➤ A Royal Fork specifically refers to a knight attacking
both the opponent's King and Queen at the same time.
➤ A pin is another fundamental tactic where an at-
tacked piece cannot move without exposing a more valu-
able piece behind it.
➤ A skewer is an attack on a valuable piece that, upon
moving, exposes a less valuable piece behind it.
➤ The term gambit refers to an opening move where a
player sacrifices a piece (usually a pawn) for positional
advantage.

30.question_text_en:

India mainly demonstrates which demographic principle?

options.text_en: Impact of sudden mortality shocks on population

1921 demonstrated the severe impact of sudden
mortality shocks, caused primarily by the devastat-
ing 1918 influenza pandemic, famines, and plague.
Important Facts:

ulation growth rate of −0.31% in India.
➤ The year 1921 is officially known as the "Year of
the Great Divide" in Indian demography because
population grew consistently thereafter.
➤ The 1918 Influenza Pandemic (Spanish Flu)
alone caused an estimated 12 to 17 million deaths
across British India.
➤ The Demographic Transition Model describes
the progression from high birth and death rates to low
birth and death rates.
➤ The first synchronous, modern decennial population
census in India was conducted in 1881 under Lord
Ripon.

criminal code.
➤ Causing grievous hurt by a mob of five or more per-
sons is separately penalised under Section 117(4) of
the BNS.
➤ The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 received
Presidential assent in December 2023 and came into
effect on 1 July 2024.

41.explanation_en:
The stable elliptical orbit of Earth is maintained by a dy-
namic gravitational balance where the gravitational
attraction of the Sun provides the exact necessary cen-
tripetal force balanced by the planet's orbital inertia.
Important Facts:
➤ The planetary motion of planets around the Sun in el-
liptical paths was formulated in Kepler's Laws of
Planetary Motion.
➤ The point of closest approach of the Earth to the Sun
is called perihelion (around January 3), at approxi-
mately 147 million km.
➤ The point of greatest separation between the Earth
and the Sun is called aphelion (around July 4), at ap-
proximately 152 million km.
➤ Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation states
that gravitational force is inversely proportional to the
square of the distance between two masses.
➤ The average distance of Earth from the Sun is de-
fined as one Astronomical Unit (AU), approximately
149.6 million km.

42.question_text_en:
Q.9 The primary objective of announcing the Minimum
Support Price (MSP) by the Government of India is to:

options.text_en:
Protect farmers from exploitation by speculators and
middlemen.
Reduce the area under food crop cultivation.

42.explanation_en:
The primary objective of the Minimum Support Price
(MSP) is to assure farmers a guaranteed minimum re-
turn for their produce and protect them from dis-
tress sales and exploitation by middlemen.
Important Facts:
➤ MSP serves as an agricultural price floor set by the
Government of India to protect farmers during sharp
price crashes in bumper crop years.
➤ The Government fixes MSP for 22 mandated
crops and Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) for sug-
arcane.
➤ Recommendations for MSP are formulated by the
Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices
(CACP).
➤ Following the National Commission on Farmers
(Swaminathan Commission), MSP is targeted at a mini-
mum of 50% over the cost of production (1.5
times).
➤ The central government announces MSPs twice ev-
ery year, covering both the Kharif and Rabi cropping
seasons.

43.explanation_en:
Most of the refraction of light rays entering the eye oc-
curs at the outer surface of the cornea, because
the difference in refractive index between air and the
corneal surface is greatest.
Important Facts:
➤ The cornea is the transparent, dome-shaped front
layer of the eye that provides approximately two-thirds
of the eye's total optical power.
➤ The crystalline lens provides finer adjustments to
focus images of objects at varying distances onto the
retina (accommodation).
➤ The pupil regulates and controls the amount of light
entering the eye through the action of the iris.
➤ Light rays focus on the retina, which contains light-
sensitive photoreceptor cells known as rods and
cones.
➤ The ciliary muscles alter the curvature and focal
length of the crystalline eye lens during accommodation.

44.question_text_en:
Q.30 What is the primary reason smartphones can support
multiple applications simultaneously in everyday use?
44.explanation_en:
Modern smartphones execute multitasking smoothly pri-
marily due to multi-core advanced processors
(CPUs/SoCs) and adequate Random Access
Memory (RAM) to keep background tasks active.
Important Facts:
➤ RAM (Random Access Memory) provides high-
speed volatile storage for currently running processes
and applications.
➤ Multicore mobile processors divide compute tasks
across multiple CPU cores to facilitate concurrent multi-
tasking.
➤ Mobile operating systems employ efficient task
scheduling and memory management algo-
rithms to prioritise active foreground apps.
➤ The central processing hardware in modern smart-
YouTube Telegram 21
GENERAL AWARENESS
phones is designed as an integrated System on a
Chip (SoC).
➤ Flash storage (ROM) stores persistent files, while
RAM determines how many active apps can remain
open simultaneously.

45.question_text_en:
Q.31 What is the approximate lift-off mass of the Small
Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV)?
45.explanation_en:
ISRO's Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV) is a 3-
stage launch vehicle with a total lift-off mass of approxi-
mately 120 tonnes (120 t).
Important Facts:
➤ SSLV has a height of 34 metres and a vehicle di-
ameter of 2 metres.
➤ It is configured with three solid propulsion
stages and a liquid propulsion-based Velocity Trimming
Module (VTM) as a terminal stage.
➤ SSLV is capable of launching satellites weighing up
to 500 kg into a 500 km Low Earth Orbit (LEO).
➤ SSLV was developed by the Indian Space Research
Organisation (ISRO) for low-cost, on-demand satellite
launches.
➤ The developmental flight SSLV-D2 successfully
placed three satellites into orbit in February 2023.

Public Service Commission in May 2025 and is former
Defence Secretary with constitutional provisions defined
under Articles 315 to 323 of Indian Constitution?

Former Defence Secretary Dr. Ajay Kumar was ap-

315 to 323 of Part XIV of the Constitution.

the establishment of a Public Service Commission for
