47.question_text_en:
Q.21 Who has been appointed first woman Director
General of Railway Protection Force responsible for
security of railway property and passengers and serving
until superannuation in October 2026 after approval by
cabinet committee?
47.explanation_en:
Senior IPS officer Sonali Mishra was appointed as the
Director General of the Railway Protection Force
(RPF), becoming the first woman officer to head the
central force.
Important Facts:
➤ The Railway Protection Force is an armed force of
the Union established under the Railway Protection
Force Act, 1957.
➤ The RPF operates under the administrative control of
the Ministry of Railways.
➤ The primary role of the RPF is protecting railway
property, passenger areas, and ensuring passenger se-
curity.
➤ Major security operations run by RPF include
Operation Nanhe Farishte for rescuing children
and Operation Meri Saheli for women safety.
➤ Appointments of Directors General of central forces
are cleared by the Appointments Committee of
the Cabinet (ACC).

48.question_text_en:
Q.3 During which summit was the India-Middle East-
Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC) officially announced?
48.explanation_en:
The India-Middle East-Europe Economic
Corridor (IMEC) was officially announced during the
G20 New Delhi Summit in September 2023.
Important Facts:
➤ IMEC was established via a Memorandum of
Understanding signed by India, the US, Saudi Arabia,
the UAE, the European Union, France, Germany, and
46 Download App Visit Website

Italy.
➤ The corridor consists of two main segments: the
East Corridor connecting India to the Arabian Gulf
and the Northern Corridor connecting the Arabian
Gulf to Europe.
➤ The project aims to integrate ship-to-rail transit net-
works along with clean hydrogen pipelines and digital
connectivity cables.
➤ The 18th G20 Leaders' Summit was hosted under
India's presidency at the Bharat Mandapam in New
Delhi on 9–10 September 2023.
➤ The theme of India's G20 Presidency was
"Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam" or "One Earth ·
One Family · One Future".

49.question_text_en:
Q.23 According to the 2025 global Air Quality Index (AQI)
report, which region is identified as the most polluted
region based on country rankings?
49.explanation_en:
Global air quality reports consistently rank South Asia
as the world's most polluted region due to extremely ele-
vated concentrations of hazardous particulate matter
(PM2.5).
Important Facts:
➤ South Asian countries including Bangladesh,
Pakistan, and India regularly register the highest national
annual average PM2.5 concentrations.
➤ PM2.5 refers to fine inhalable atmospheric particles
with diameters of 2.5 micrometres or smaller.
➤ Major drivers of South Asian air pollution include ve-
hicular exhaust, industrial combustion, biomass burning,
and seasonal agricultural stubble burning.
➤ The World Health Organization (WHO) annual
air quality guideline limit for PM2.5 exposure is 5 µg/m³.
➤ Topographical factors such as the Himalayan barrier
trap seasonal winter pollutants over the densely popu-
lated Indo-Gangetic Plain.

50.question_text_en:
Q.16 Price Support Scheme (PSS) is implemented under
which umbrella scheme?

options.text_en: Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay Sanraksan Abhiyan

50.explanation_en:
The Price Support Scheme (PSS) is implemented as a
key component under the umbrella scheme Pradhan
Mantri Annadata Aay Sanraksan Abhiyan (PM-
AASHA).
Important Facts:
➤ PM-AASHA was approved by the Union Cabinet in
September 2018 to ensure remunerative prices to
farmers for their produce.
➤ PM-AASHA comprises three sub-schemes: the
Price Support Scheme (PSS), the Price
Deficiency Payment Scheme (PDPS), and the
Private Procurement & Stockist Scheme
(PPSS).
➤ Under PSS, physical procurement of pulses,
oilseeds, and copra is undertaken by central nodal agen-
cies like NAFED and FCI.
➤ The Minimum Support Price (MSP) is recommended
by the Commission for Agricultural Costs and
Prices (CACP).
➤ MSP is announced by the Cabinet Committee
on Economic Affairs (CCEA) before each sowing
season.

36.question_text_en:
Q.2 Which of the following is NOT an exception to the law
of demand?
36.explanation_en:
The law of demand states that other factors remain-
ing constant, quantity demanded varies inversely with
price. While Veblen goods, conspicuous consumption,
and Giffen goods are standard exceptions where de-
mand rises with price, substitute goods adhere di-
rectly to normal market demand mechanics and do not
constitute an exception.
Important Facts:
➤ The Law of Demand demonstrates an inverse re-
lationship between price and quantity demanded ($P
\uparrow, Q \downarrow$).
➤ Giffen goods are inferior goods where the negative
income effect outweighs the substitution effect, leading
to an upward-sloping demand curve.
➤ Veblen goods (conspicuous goods) have prestige
value; higher prices make them more desirable to status-
conscious buyers.
➤ For substitute goods, when the price of one good
increases, the demand for its substitute rises, which is
consistent with standard demand theory.
➤ Alfred Marshall popularized the graphical representa-
tion of demand curves in neoclassical economics.

amendments. Which of the following features has NOT

➤ Directive Principles are non-justiciable and cannot

harmonized.

44.question_text_en:
Q.1 The Net Reproductive Rate (NRR) is said to be 1
when

options.text_en: A woman replaces herself in the population

44.explanation_en:
The Net Reproduction Rate (NRR) measures the
average number of daughters that would be born to a fe-
male if she conformed to current age-specific fertility and
mortality rates. An NRR of 1.0 indicates the exact re-
placement level—meaning each woman, on average,
bears exactly one surviving daughter to replace herself.
Important Facts:
➤ NRR = 1.0 corresponds to the replacement
level of fertility, leading eventually to a stationary
population.
➤ If NRR > 1, each generation of females is replacing
itself with a larger cohort, indicating population growth.
➤ If NRR < 1, female births are insufficient to replace
the parent generation, indicating eventual population de-
cline.
➤ NRR differs from Gross Reproduction Rate (GRR)
because NRR explicitly accounts for mortality before the
end of reproductive age.
➤ In terms of Total Fertility Rate (TFR), replacement
level is generally considered to be approximately 2.1
children per woman.

BCE, the core Tripitaka canon formed from the 5th
century BCE onwards, Buddhacharita was composed
in the 2nd century CE by Ashvaghosha, and
Hemachandra's Parishishtaparvan dates to the 12th
century CE.
Important Facts:
➤ Panini composed the Sanskrit grammatical treatise
Ashtadhyayi around the 6th–5th century BCE.
➤ The Buddhist canonical texts Tripitaka (Sutta,

scholar Hemachandra in the 12th century CE.

34.question_text_en:
Q.1 What is the difference between Gross National
Product (GNP) and Gross Domestic Product (GDP)?

options.text_en: Income of a resident from investment abroad

34.explanation_en:
The fundamental difference between GNP and GDP is
Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA), which
includes income earned by domestic residents from
abroad minus income earned by foreigners domestically.
Important Facts:
➤ The relationship is defined as GNP = GDP + Net
Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA).
➤ GDP measures total economic production within do-
mestic borders regardless of nationality.
➤ GNP measures total economic output produced by
normal residents of a nation globally.
➤ Factor income includes wages, profits, rent, and in-
vestment returns from abroad.
➤ When depreciation is deducted from GNP, it yields
Net National Product (NNP).

35.question_text_en:
Q.2 Which reform aimed to address inefficiencies in
government spending and improve fiscal discipline in the
years following 1991?
35.explanation_en:
The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget
Management (FRBM) Act, 2003 was enacted to
institutionalize fiscal discipline, reduce the fiscal deficit,
and improve public expenditure management post-1991
reforms.
Important Facts:
➤ The FRBM Act was enacted by the Indian
Parliament in August 2003.
➤ It mandated the phased reduction and elimination of
the revenue deficit and capping the fiscal deficit.
➤ The Act set a benchmark target to limit the fiscal
deficit to 3% of GDP.
➤ It requires the government to lay three fiscal policy
statements before Parliament along with the Annual
Union Budget.
➤ In 2016, the N. K. Singh Committee was ap-

36.question_text_en:
Q.4 The Union Government can legislate on a subject in
the State List under which of the following situations?

options.text_en: When Lok Sabha passes it by majority
During President's Rule in that state

36.explanation_en:
Under Article 356 and Article 357, when
President's Rule is proclaimed in a state, Parliament ac-
quires the authority to make laws with respect to sub-
jects enumerated in the State List for that state.
Important Facts:
➤ Article 356 empowers the President to issue a procla-
mation imposing President's Rule in a state.
➤ Under Article 357(1), Parliament is competent to
exercise the legislative powers of the State Legislature.
➤ Parliament can also legislate on State List matters
under Article 249 if Rajya Sabha passes a resolution
by a two-thirds majority.
➤ Under Article 250, Parliament can legislate on
State List matters during an active National Emergency.
➤ Under Article 252, Parliament can enact laws on
State List subjects when requested by two or more state
legislatures.

37.question_text_en:
Q.5 Under which condition can the President legislate for
a State without the aid of Parliament?

options.text_en: If the State Assembly is prorogued
If Governor fails to act on a Bill
If Council of States makes a recommendation

37.explanation_en:
Under Article 357(1)(a), Parliament can confer on
the President the power to make laws for a State un-
der a Proclamation of President's Rule pursuant to
Article 356, allowing the President to enact
President's Acts.
Important Facts:
➤ Under Article 356, the President assumes execu-
tive powers of the state government upon constitutional
breakdown.
➤ Article 357(1)(a) allows Parliament to delegate state
legislative authority directly to the President of India.
➤ Laws enacted by the President under this delegated
authority are promulgated as President's Acts.
➤ Under Article 123, the President promulgates ordi-
nances only when Parliament is in recess, not specifi-
cally for state legislation.
➤ Laws made under Article 357 remain in force after the
proclamation ceases until altered or repealed by
the state legislature.

38.question_text_en:

override judicial review by placing laws under the Ninth
Schedule, and was later limited by the Supreme Court in
I.R. Coelho case (2007)?
38.explanation_en:
The 1st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1951
inserted Article 31B and the Ninth Schedule to insulate

cumscribed by the Supreme Court in the I.R. Coelho
case (2007).
Important Facts:
➤ The 1st Amendment Act of 1951 introduced
Article 31B and the Ninth Schedule into the Indian
Constitution.
➤ In the landmark I.R. Coelho v. State of Tamil
Nadu (2007) case, a 9-judge bench ruled on the Ninth
Schedule.
➤ The court held that laws inserted into the Ninth
Schedule after April 24, 1973 are subject to judicial
review.
➤ Any Ninth Schedule law violating the basic struc-

can be struck down.

39.question_text_en:
Q.5 Under which condition can fundamental rights be
suspended, and who has the authority to do so?

options.text_en: By Prime Minister during national crisis

39.explanation_en:
Under Article 359, the President of India may
suspend the right to move any court for the enforcement
of Fundamental Rights during a National Emergency
proclaimed under Article 352.
Important Facts:
➤ A National Emergency is declared by the President
under Article 352 on grounds of war, external aggres-
sion, or armed rebellion.
➤ Under Article 358, rights guaranteed by Article 19
are automatically suspended during an emergency on
external grounds.
➤ Under Article 359, the President may by presiden-
tial order suspend the enforcement of other specified
fundamental rights.
➤ The 44th Amendment Act, 1978 mandated that
enforcement of Articles 20 and 21 can never be sus-
pended under Article 359.
➤ The Prime Minister or Parliament cannot unilaterally
suspend fundamental rights enforcement.

40.question_text_en:
Q.1 Who among the following was the first chief justice of
supreme court in British rule?
40.explanation_en:
Sir Elijah Impey was appointed the first Chief Justice
of the Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William in
Calcutta, established under the Regulating Act of
1773.
Important Facts:
➤ The Supreme Court of Judicature at Calcutta was es-
tablished pursuant to the Regulating Act of 1773.
➤ Sir Elijah Impey held the office of Chief Justice from
1774 to 1783.
➤ He was a close school friend and associate of the
first Governor-General, Warren Hastings.
➤ Impey's judicial decisions included the controversial
trial and hanging of Raja Nand Kumar in 1775.
➤ Impey and Hastings both subsequently faced im-
peachment proceedings in the British Parliament.

41.question_text_en:
Q.1 What is the main feature of the Peninsular Plateau of
India?
41.explanation_en:
A major defining feature of the Indian Peninsular Plateau
is its volcanic origin, notably evidenced by the exten-
sive basaltic lava sheets forming the Deccan Trap.
Important Facts:
➤ The Deccan Traps were formed by massive flood
basalt eruptions at the end of the Cretaceous period
(around 66 million years ago).
➤ Weathering of these volcanic basalt rocks produced
the fertility-rich black soil (regur) ideal for cotton.
➤ The Peninsular Plateau is part of the ancient, stable
landmass of Gondwanaland.
➤ The highest peak of the Peninsular Plateau is
Anamudi (2,695 m) in Kerala.
➤ Peninsular rivers flow in broad, shallow valleys indi-
cating an advanced, mature stage of erosion.

43.question_text_en:
Q.3 What does a higher crude birth rate (CBR) indicate
about a region's demographic stage?

options.text_en: It is in advanced demographic transition
It has an early demographic transition

43.explanation_en:
A high Crude Birth Rate is characteristic of the early
demographic transition stage, where fertility re-
mains high while mortality rates begin or continue to fall,
causing rapid growth.
Important Facts:
➤ Crude Birth Rate (CBR) measures the number of live
births per 1,000 individuals per year.
➤ In Stage 1 and Stage 2 of demographic transi-
tion, birth rates remain consistently elevated.
➤ High birth rates result in a wide demographic base
with a large proportion of dependent youth.
➤ Advanced demographic stages (Stage 3 and 4) are
marked by low CBR and low CDR.
➤ High CBR combined with falling mortality leads to the
phenomenon of population explosion.

44.question_text_en:
Q.4 What is the major policy implication of a bulging youth
population in India as seen in demographic surveys?

options.text_en: It necessitates investment in skills & employment

44.explanation_en:
A bulging youth population constitutes a demographic
dividend, requiring urgent policy prioritization and in-
vestment in education, vocational skill develop-
ment, and employment creation.
Important Facts:
➤ The demographic dividend refers to economic growth
potential when the working-age population (15–64
years) exceeds dependents.
➤ Over 65% of India's population is currently
within the working-age demographic bracket.
➤ Reaping this dividend requires targeted investments
under initiatives like Skill India and Make in India.
➤ Failure to create adequate quality jobs can turn de-
mographic dividend into demographic disaster.
➤ The median age of the Indian population is relatively
young at approximately 28 years.

45.question_text_en:
Q.5 Which of the following would be the most appropriate
indicator of demographic dependency?
45.explanation_en:
The dependency ratio directly measures demo-
graphic dependency by calculating the ratio of depen-
dents (people younger than 15 and older than 64) to the
productive working-age population (15–64).
Important Facts:
➤ The dependency ratio is calculated as:
[(Population aged 0–14 + Population aged
65+) / (Population aged 15–64)] × 100.
➤ It is broken down into the youth dependency ra-
tio and the old-age dependency ratio.
➤ A lower dependency ratio implies a larger proportion

of productive workforce, generating a demographic
dividend.
➤ A high dependency ratio exerts fiscal pressure on
public healthcare, education, and social pension
funds.
➤ Crude birth rate and sex ratio measure fertility
rates and gender composition respectively, not
dependency.

46.question_text_en:
Q.4 Why does a diamond sparkle more than other
transparent materials?

options.text_en: It absorbs light and releases it gradually
Its refractive index allows dispersion and internal reflection
It scatters light uniformly in all directions

46.explanation_en:
Diamond has a very high refractive index (about
2.42) and a low critical angle of approximately 24.4°.
This promotes repeated total internal reflection
and high dispersion of light into brilliant colors.
Important Facts:
➤ Diamond has a refractive index of approximately
2.42, which is exceptionally high for a transparent solid.
➤ The critical angle for a diamond-air interface is ex-
tremely small at about 24.4°.
➤ Sparkle in cut diamonds is primarily caused by total
internal reflection.
➤ High optical dispersion separates white light into dis-
tinct spectral colors (fire).
➤ Diamond is an allotrope of carbon arranged in a
rigid tetrahedral lattice.

48.question_text_en: Q.1 How do antigens stimulate an immune response?

options.text_en: By binding to lymphocytes and activating them

48.explanation_en:
Antigens stimulate the immune response by binding
specifically to receptors on lymphocytes (T cells
and B cells). This binding triggers their clonal activa-
tion, proliferation, and differentiation.
Important Facts:
➤ Antigens are foreign substances that elicit an immune
response by binding to specific lymphocyte recep-
tors.
➤ B lymphocytes recognize antigens via membrane-
bound antibodies and differentiate into plasma cells.
➤ T lymphocytes recognize processed antigens pre-
sented on MHC molecules.
➤ The specific molecular region of an antigen recog-
nized by an antibody is called an epitope.
➤ Clonal selection and activation result in both effector
cells and long-lived memory cells.

49.question_text_en: Q.4 Ozone (O₃) at ground level is considered as:
49.explanation_en:
Ground-level tropospheric ozone is a secondary air
pollutant and a major constituent of photochemical
smog. It causes significant respiratory damage and
harms vegetation.
Important Facts:
➤ Ground-level ozone is formed by photochemical reac-
tions between NOx and VOCs in the presence of sun-
light.
➤ Unlike beneficial stratospheric ozone, tropospheric
ozone is classified as a hazardous criteria air pollu-
tant.
➤ Exposure to tropospheric ozone exacerbates asthma,
bronchitis, and reduces lung function.
➤ Ground-level ozone is a primary oxidizing component
of photochemical smog.
➤ It reduces agricultural productivity by damaging plant
cells and inhibiting photosynthesis.

50.question_text_en:
Q.4 Which of the following is a key goal of the Quad's
(Quadrilateral Security Dialogue) infrastructure initiatives?

options.text_en:
To create an alternate infrastructure to the Belt and Road
Initiative.
To promote trade between Europe and Asia.
To create a military infrastructure network.
To isolate certain nations from global infrastructure.

50.explanation_en:
The Quad promotes transparent, high-standard, debt-
sustainable infrastructure in the Indo-Pacific, offering a
viable alternative to China's Belt and Road
Initiative (BRI).
Important Facts:
➤ The Quad comprises four democratic nations: India,
the United States, Japan, and Australia.
➤ The Quad Infrastructure Coordination Group focuses
on sustainable, debt-free financing across the Indo-
Pacific.
➤ In 2021, the Quad announced major initiatives for cli-
mate, critical technologies, and infrastruc-
ture development.
➤ The partnership aims to provide alternatives to
opaque financing associated with China's Belt and
Road Initiative.
➤ Quad members jointly promote the Blue Dot
Network standard for global infrastructure certification.
